additional.simplyswords_epicfied.arcanet: Standard combo: press A 6 times. Dash attack: A while running. Jump attack: Space+A. Aerial slice: dash attack-B-A-A-A-A-A.

Innate skill combo: send target to air by dash attack, then hold B and attack in air(require first successful hit). Combining with Ender obscuris skill opens window for better combo. Extended Arcanic slice: dash attack-B-A-A(+Ender obscuris)-A(+Ender obscuris)-A(+Ender obscuris)-B. Arcanic sliced dive: dash A-B-A-A-A-A(hold B after any of A).
Innate skill: hold B to dive into air and then hold B once more. Triggers powerful slam from sky, damage scales with innate skill stacks and sweeping edge enchant.
additional.simplyswords_epicfied.brimsto: Standard combo: press A 8 times. Fast combo: A-A-B. Advanced combo: A-A-A-B-A-A-A-B-B. Brimstone heat-up combo: A-A-A-B-A-B. Dash attack: A while running. Jump attack: Space+A.

When appear special icon on right side hold B to inflict target on fire. this effect can be stacked to 2. Hold B right after basic 4 to extinguish fire from targer, dealing additional damage and increase heat level for innate skill

To activate hold C first and then B, this attack inflict only long stun. When appear special icon on right side hold B to activate one of special skills: Brimstone conversion(require atleast 15-20% heat), Brimstone prison(require atleast 40-50% heat), Domain of Flames(require 90-100% heat)

After Brimstone overheat(C+B) hold B. Trigger fire explosion and transform Brimstone Claymore into 'forbidden flame' form, gain completely different combat style.  This mode locks heat level and comsume it over time. To exit this form use C+B, it will trigger Brimstone prison and transform weapon back into normal form. Standard combo: press A 10 times. Advanced combo: A-A-A-A-B(repeat as much as possible)-A-A-A-A-B(repeat as much as possible)-A-A. Jump attack trigger guard break on enemy.

After Brimstone overheat(C+B) when heat level is more than 40% hold B. catch enemy with strong hit and release soul fire, this attack inflict 'Brimstone flame' what have longer duration and can be consumed by basic 4 B multiple times.

After Brimstone overheat(C+B) when heat level is more than 90% hold B. Burn all targets in 5x5 area and inflict 'Brimstone flame' on them. Every 2 seconds all targets within 'Domain of flames' take fire damage. Heat level gain in this state is doubled until it reach 0%.
additional.simplyswords_epicfied.dormant: Standard combo: press A 5 times. Dash attack: A while running. Jump attack: Space+A.
additional.simplyswords_epicfied.hearthf: Standard combo: press A 7 times. Volcanic rage combo: press A 9 times. Volcanic explosion: after 9th attack of volcanic rage combo press A, can be triggered multiple times. Dash attack: A while running. Jump attack: Space+A.

Innate skill: To activate hold B, highly not recommended to activate using hypervitality. Enters into 'Volcanic rage' mode. Gives stun immunity and more powerful combo, but damages wielder over time. To cancel this mode hold B again. Volcanic invasion: Space+A-A multiple times.

To activate hold C. Enters into 'Volcano channel' state. In this state wielder can barely move, lose health in exchange of resistance and charging more powerful final attack. There are 4 types of charging, each one have unique sound, icon and animation on which state one you are. Charged 1: Hold C for until unique sound, release strong spin attack what hit target 3 times. Charged 2: Hold C for until unique sound second time, release strong upperslash. Charged 3: Hold C for until unique sound third time, release powerful hit on the ground. Charged 4: Hold C for until unique sound fourth time, gain 3x damage buff on next hit, can be stacked with charged attack. Volcano destruction: Hold C 4 times to get buff, and then 3 more times to activate charged 3, released strongest attack. Volcano desctruction deal over 105 magic + over 115 melee damage at it's base.
additional.simplyswords_epicfied.shadows: Standard combo: press A 8 times. Dash attack: A while running. Jump attack: Space+A. Shadowcatch: A-A-A-A-A-A-A-A-Space+A
While attacking at right time, automatically parries any incoming damage. You can parry negative potion effect like poison or wither
Greatly enhances stamina regeneration. Now it regenerate even while attacking.

Innate skill: To activate hold B. First hit apply long stun, then next deal 1.5x damage from basic one, this skill can be stacked up to 2. Continue hold B if you hit more than 1 targer to deal additional slash.
While have 2 stacks of innate skill Hold B-0.25sec delay-Hold B-release, last slash deal 1.75x damage of basic one, can be canceled by using standard combo.
additional.simplyswords_epicfied.slumber: Standard combo: press A 5 times. Dash attack: A while running. Jump attack: Space+A.
additional.simplyswords_epicfied.soulren: Standard combo: press A 6 times. Dash attack: A while running. Jump attack: Space+A. Awakened Demon mode: press A 11 times. Wither corruption: in Awakened Demon mode press Space+A(inflict wither V if target have no effects, or additional I-III stacks), require 2.5 hearts.
Apply sweeping edge III on Soulrender to greatly enhance wither effect chance and stacks from attacks. Enhances Awakened Demon mode.

Hold C to aim, release to shoot, 5 sec cooldown, require innate skill points. Shoot a withered soul on target, if projectile hit entity remembers it's last position. After that press C to teleport target to that position and apply stun on it.

Innate skill: To activate hold B. Enter to Awakened Demon mode, set timer to 20(or 50 with sweeping edge III). Completely changes moveset, first 2 attacks of basic combo have chance to apply wither on target(this effect can be stacked), third attack consume all wither stacks from target dealing additional damage and heal wielder, increase timer depend on how many stacks were consumed(+2 sec for each). Rest of attacks have chance to increase Awakened Demon mode timer by 2 sec per hit.

While in Awakened Demon mode, to activate press C. Require more than 80 seconds of Awakened Demon mode timer, consume 80 seconds of it. Summons black hole, while it active: stacks wither effect very fast, attach all nearby entities to black hole. After few seconds it explodes dealing huge damage based on stacked wither effect.
additional.simplyswords_epicfied.stars_e: Bright galaxy mode: press A 6 times. Galaxy eclipse mode: press A 6 times. Stars cycle: A while running. Jump attack: Space+A. Stars cutter: while in Galaxy eclipse mode Space+A(repeat A as long as stamina allows it).
By using Stars cycle attack you can switch between Bright galaxy and Galaxy eclipse modes.

Innate skill: To activate hold B. This attack apply special glow effect on all nearby entities and throw them 7 block up. Hitting mob with glowing apply blindness effect on them and gives invisibility on wielder for 6 seconds, any attack on entity with blindness effect in Galaxy eclipse mode resets the timer. This skill can be stacked to 2

In this mode: lose ability to guard, but gain stronger attacks and combo instead. Delayed stars cutter: Space+A(repeat A with 0.75-1 sec delay). Galactic cutter: Stars cycle(if in Bright galaxy mode)-B-Delayed stars cutter. Eclipse cutter: A-A-A-A-A-Delayed stars cutter.

Gear switched off in the config doesn't vanish - it stays craftable, and a piece already on a horse still shows but stops working.
New pieces can't be fitted: the medkit and horseshoe slots disappear, and the harness slot only takes a cart.

A JSON config at $(l)config/icys-better-horses.json$()  toggles whole systems without removing the mod - admins use it to set what a world allows.$(br2)With $(l)Cloth Config$()  installed you can edit the same settings in game.

Every switch takes $(l)yes$()  or $(l)no$(). The main ones:$(br2)$(li)$(l)stabilizer$(), $(l)medkit$(), $(l)hooves$()  - the gear.$(li)$(l)horse_exclusivity$()  - owner-only riding.$(li)$(l)multiriding$()  - two riders on one horse.
$(li)$(l)horse_combat$()  - charges, kicks and spooks.$(li)$(l)horse_revival$()  - bringing dead horses back.$(li)$(l)horse_management$()  - the roster screen.

The $(l)tuning$()  block holds the numbers: passive bond gain, horse spawns, the $(l)revival cost$()  in levels and the bond it takes, the $(l)whistle range$(), where 0 means anywhere, and $(l)dismount_command$(): wander, follow or stay when you get off.
$(l)breeding_foods$()  lists what puts a horse in love: a golden carrot, golden apple or enchanted golden apple unless the server changes it.
Everything to get started - claim and bond a horse, read its stats, ride smarter, and how breeding and coats work.

$(li)$(l)Hold Your Horses$()  - tame a horse.$(li)$(l)Stable Reading$()  - get hold of this book.$(li)$(l)All Tacked Up$()  - craft the Upgraded Saddle.$(li)$(l)Home Is Where the Hay Is$()  - set a horse's home.
$(li)$(l)Hell on Hooves$()  - take a horse to the Nether.$(li)$(l)Foal Play$()  - breed two horses.$(li)$(l)Best of Both Worlds$()  - raise a mixed-breed foal.
Better Horses brings its own advancements. Tame your first horse and the tree opens up.$(br2)None of it is required - it's a checklist for a long life in the saddle.

$(li)$(l)Ride or Die$()  - reach 100 bond.$(li)$(l)Built Different$()  - ride at 25 blk/s.$(li)$(l)Second Chance$()  - let an Andalusian take a killing blow for you.$(li)$(l)Pegasus, Sort Of$()  - survive a 30 block drop on a Glidewing Harness.
$(li)$(l)Pocket Dimension, Four Legs$()  - fit an ender chest.$(li)$(l)Stable Genius$()  - own ten horses at once.$(li)$(l)Gotta Tame 'Em All$()  - own all fifteen breeds.

$(l)/horse set coat blood_bay$()  recolours the horse you ride, the one you look at, or the nearest within 8 blocks.$(br2)Press Tab after $(l)coat$()  to see that breed's coats. $(l)random$()  rolls one.

To pick horses with a selector, put it before the property:$(br2)$(l)/horse set @e[distance=..6] coat grey$()$(br2)Every breed horse it catches is changed. Any whose breed lacks that coat are skipped and named in chat.
The same command sets more than coats:$(br2)$(l)gender$()  male or female$(br)$(l)speed$()  blocks per second$(br)$(l)jump$()  blocks$(br)$(l)health$()  hit points$(br)$(l)bond$()  0 to 100
Stats snap to the breed's range, and chat tells you when a number was clamped. Tab on a stat suggests the breed's top and bottom.$(br2)Speed and jump are base stats. Bond still adds its bonus on top.
$(l)/horse coats thoroughbred$()  lists a breed's coats in chat. Leave the breed off to see the coats of the horse you ride or stand beside.$(br2)Anyone can use this one, no cheats needed.

Operators can recolour, restat and spawn horses with $(l)/horse set$()  and $(l)/horse spawn$(). Both need cheats on, or op level 2 on a server.$(br2)They only work on this mod's breeds. Vanilla horses, donkeys and mules are left alone.

$(l)/horse spawn thoroughbred$()  makes a fresh horse where you stand.$(br2)Add options after the breed, in any order: $(l)coat$(), $(l)gender$(), $(l)speed$(), $(l)jump$(), $(l)health$(), $(l)bond$(), $(l)baby$()  and $(l)owner$().
$(l)/horse spawn arabian coat=wild_bay gender=female speed=15 bond=100 owner=Steve$()$(br2)Anything left out rolls like a wild horse of that breed. The owner has to be online.
Each bar fills toward the mod's ceiling, not this horse's own range:$(br2)$(li)Speed up to $(l)26.25 blk/s$().$(li)Jump up to $(l)16.45 blk$().$(li)Health up to $(l)50 HP$().
Speed and jump ceilings include the full-bond bonus, so a strong horse reads short until it's bonded. Health does not grow with bond.
The $(l)Disown$()  button at the bottom gives the horse back to the wild after a confirmation, the same as on the roster. It refuses while the horse still wears gear.
Press your $(l)Horse Whistle$()  key while mounted for a full profile of the horse you're riding. Unmounted, the same key whistles your mount.

$(li)$(l)Gender$()  and $(l)Breed$()  (with a $(l)(mix)$()  tag if cross-bred).$(li)$(l)Coat$()  - color plus markings.$(li)$(l)Bond$()  - value out of 100 with a fill bar.$(li)$(l)Speed$()  - blocks per second.$(li)$(l)Jump$()  - block height.$(li)$(l)Health$()  - hit points.
Set $(l)horse_exclusivity$()  to $(l)no$()  in the config and any player can ride any owned horse - handy for shared stables.

$(l)/horse trust PlayerName$()  lets one player ride on their own. It covers every horse you own, now and later; $(l)/horse untrust$()  takes it back.$(br2)See $(l)Trusted Riders$()  for what that hands over.
An owned horse only answers to you - anyone else taking the reins is bucked off at once. It will still take a second rider, but only while you're in the saddle.
Look at an owned horse and press your $(l)Horse Command Wheel$()  key. Pick a wedge, or click outside to cancel.$(br2)$(li)$(l)Follow$(): it trails after you.

$(li)$(l)Wander$(): grazes and roams a 32x32 area around where you gave the order.$(li)$(l)Stay$(): it waits where you left it.$(li)$(l)Set Home$(): marks the spot as home and switches to Stay.$(li)$(l)Return Home$(): sends it back to that spot.
Tame a horse fully and it becomes $(l)owned$()  and starts using Better Horses' systems.
Carrots, potatoes, beetroot, melon, sweet and glow berries and sugar cane all heal a horse, grow a foal and help tame a wild one.
They give no bond.$(br2)Hold any food a horse likes nearby and it turns its head to watch you, begging.
Press $(l)Horse Whistle$()  to call your active horse, or the last one you rode. Mounted, the same key opens the info screen.$(br2)Bond runs 0 to 100, and every 20 points adds speed and jump.

$(li)Stay near your horse for slow passive gain.$(li)Its first $(l)Name Tag$()  gives +10 bond.$(li)A $(l)Golden Apple$()  gives +2 bond.$(li)A $(l)Brush$()  gives +1 bond, with a five-minute cooldown.
A trusted rider is treated as you are: mounting, riding pillion, driving a cart, the gear screen, saddlebags and cart chest, fitting gear, shearing and commands.
The one thing they $(l)cannot$()  do is disown it. Releasing a horse stays with its owner.
$(l)/horse untrust PlayerName$()  revokes it, bucking them off on the spot if they're riding.$(br2)$(l)/horse trusted$()  lists everyone you trust.
A trusted rider can ride your horse away and you can't whistle it back. Only trust people you'd hand a lead to.

$(l)/horse trust PlayerName$()  lets that player ride every horse you own.$(br2)Trust is stored per player, not per horse, so it covers every horse you tame later - you never run it again for a new mount.
Once a horse is fully tamed, this mod marks it as yours right away. From there you can turn an ordinary mount into a proper road companion.
Better Horses turns an ordinary mount into a lasting companion: ownership, bonding, and a stack of riding fixes. This book covers all of it.
Tame a horse and it's registered to you at once. From there you can bond with it, equip it, and command it.
$(li)$(l)Set Active$()  - the horse your whistle calls from now on.$(li)$(l)Whistle$()  - calls it to you; it walks if it's close, teleports if it isn't.
$(li)$(l)Send Home$()  - packs it off to its saved home.$(li)$(l)Disown$()  - gives it up for good, after a confirmation. Strip its gear first.

The fastest way to fetch a mount too far off to whistle, or resting in another dimension.$(br2)Nearby, the numbers follow it as it moves. Resting, they're the last spot it stood - exactly where you'll find it.
Always in that horse's own dimension, shown beside its gender.
A horse that dies stays on the roster, darkened. $(l)Summon$()  brings it back in front of you for $(l)10 levels$(), free in Creative, and it returns with $(l)20$()  less bond.
Its gear stays where it died, so go back for it. $(l)Forget$()  removes it for good.$(br2)Servers set the cost and the bond loss, or switch revival off.
Press $(l)Manage Horses$()  for the roster - every horse registered to you, wherever it is.$(br2)A horse marked $(l)Resting$()  is in an unloaded chunk. It's safe, and still answers the whistle.
Pick a horse and it appears in 3D on the right, so you can tell them apart.$(br2)Three lines sit under the model:
$(li)Its $(l)coordinates$(), as X, Y, Z.$(li)Its $(l)bond$(), out of 100.$(li)Whether it has a $(l)home$()  set.
A field guide to the fifteen horse breeds: what they look like, what biomes they call home, and what to expect when you meet one wild.
$(l)At bond 0:$()  A map filled from the saddle covers twice the usual ground.$(br2)$(l)At bond 40:$()  Three times.
$(l)At bond 100:$()  Four times, and structures it rides past get marked - modded ones included.
Bold patchwork coats with dramatic $(l)white field$()  patterns.$(br2)Speed: $(l)8-15$()  blk/s$(br)Jump: $(l)2-4.5$()  blk$(br)Health: $(l)15-30$()
Whatever you kill from a Paint's saddle drops as if your weapon carried $(l)Looting$().$(br2)$(l)At bond 0:$()  Looting I.$(br2)$(l)At bond 40:$()  Looting II.
$(l)At bond 100:$()  Looting III.$(br2)A stronger Looting weapon still wins - the two don't stack.
$(l)At bond 0:$()  The rider takes reduced damage while mounted.$(br2)$(l)At bond 40:$()  That reduction gets stronger.
$(l)At bond 100:$()  $(l)Second Chance$(): a killing blow is taken by the horse instead, which survives on one heart. Long cooldown.
An agile Iberian breed with a thick mane, common on open meadows.$(br2)Speed: $(l)9-15$()  blk/s$(br)Jump: $(l)2-5.5$()  blk$(br)Health: $(l)25-40$()

$(l)At bond 0:$()  Night vision while you ride it in the dark, no torch needed.$(br2)$(l)At bond 40:$()  $(l)Herding$(): with an empty hand, livestock within $(l)20 blocks$()  trail the horse and keep up at a trot or canter.
Pause it per horse from the command wheel.$(br2)$(l)At bond 100:$()  $(l)Auto-feed$(): with a chest on, it feeds livestock within $(l)12 blocks$()  the right breeding food from its storage.
Tough and athletic, and the only breed whose coat always carries $(l)dots$().$(br2)Speed: $(l)8-15$()  blk/s$(br)Jump: $(l)2-4.5$()  blk$(br)Health: $(l)15-30$()
Spawns naturally in:$(br2)$(li)Plains.$(li)Wooded Badlands.$(li)Savanna Plateau.$(li)Sunflower Plains.$(br2)
$(l)At bond 0:$()  Speed builds while you move, to +10%% after twenty seconds. Stopping bleeds it off at 2%% a second.$(br2)$(l)At bond 40:$()  The ceiling doubles to +20%%.
$(l)At bond 100:$()  Ceiling in twelve seconds, with a two second grace so a brief pause no longer wipes it.
Compact and hardy - bred for desert crossings and badlands runs.$(br2)Speed: $(l)11-15$()  blk/s$(br)Jump: $(l)3-6$()  blk$(br)Health: $(l)15-20$()
$(l)At bond 0:$()  Six rows of storage, two above any other draft and the biggest chest in the mod.$(br2)$(l)At bond 40:$()  Seats three riders, as long as it is not carrying a chest.

$(l)At bond 100:$()  $(l)Brick Break$(): at a gallop it punches a $(l)three-wide, three-tall$()  hole through weak blocks, but only through walls three or more tall - lower obstacles get stepped over. Costs health, half a minute to recover. Off by default in the config.

Belgium's draft breed and the strongest horse here - broader than a Percheron, heavily feathered, and built to pull rather than carry.$(br2)Speed: $(l)7-10$()  blk/s$(br)Jump: $(l)1-3.5$()  blk$(br)Health: $(l)35-50$()
Spawns naturally in:$(br2)$(li)Taiga.$(li)Old Growth Spruce Taiga.$(li)Old Growth Pine Taiga.$(li)Forest.$(br2)
$(l)At bond 0:$()  Barding grants $(l)25%% more armour$(), and charge and kick damage read armour too.$(br2)$(l)At bond 40:$()  Wearing barding grants the rider Resistance.
$(l)At bond 100:$()  $(l)Deflect$(): arrows and other projectiles are stopped before they land, off the horse $(l)and off its rider$().
Scotland's draft giant and the showiest of the four - a parade horse before a ploughing one.$(br2)Speed: $(l)7-10$()  blk/s$(br)Jump: $(l)1-3.5$()  blk$(br)Health: $(l)35-50$()
Spawns naturally in:$(br2)$(li)Windswept Hills.$(li)Windswept Gravelly Hills.$(li)Windswept Forest.$(li)Old Growth Pine Taiga.$(br2)
$(l)At bond 0:$()  Neutral mobs lose interest in you, and anything already angry drops the grudge.$(br2)$(l)At bond 40:$()  The same calm extends to hostile mobs.
$(l)At bond 100:$()  $(l)Dressage$(): rear the horse and every hostile in front is thrown back and loses its target.
The all-black horse of the Dutch lowlands - tall, powerful, always show-ready.$(br2)Speed: $(l)9-15$()  blk/s$(br)Jump: $(l)2-5.5$()  blk$(br)Health: $(l)25-40$()
Spawns naturally in:$(br2)$(li)Dark Forest.$(li)Forest.$(li)Pale Garden.$(li)Old Growth Spruce Taiga.$(li)Taiga.$(br2)
$(l)At bond 0:$()  Four rows of storage, a row more than a pony deserves.$(br2)$(l)At bond 40:$()  Pulls a cart at full speed, normally a draft's job.
$(l)At bond 100:$()  Six rows, level with the Belgian, plus $(l)Hearthlight$(): after dark it glows and lights the ground it crosses.
A small Tyrolean breed, chestnut with a flaxen mane, sure-footed on slopes.$(br2)Speed: $(l)8-13$()  blk/s$(br)Jump: $(l)2-4.5$()  blk$(br)Health: $(l)25-40$()
Spawns naturally in:$(br2)$(li)Snowy Slopes.$(li)Grove.$(li)Meadow.$(li)Frozen Peaks.$(li)Jagged Peaks.$(li)Stony Peaks.$(br2)

$(l)At bond 0:$()  Soul sand, cobwebs, berries and honey do not slow it, and berry bushes draw no blood from it or its rider.$(br2)$(l)At bond 40:$()  $(l)Winter Coat$(): neither horse nor rider freezes.
$(l)At bond 100:$()  $(l)Clear Head$(): poison, wither and hunger are refused outright - on the pony always, and on you while you ride.
A short, shaggy pony from Iceland with an unusually smooth extra gait.$(br2)Speed: $(l)8-13$()  blk/s$(br)Jump: $(l)2-4.5$()  blk$(br)Health: $(l)25-40$()
Spawns naturally in:$(br2)$(li)Snowy Plains.$(li)Snowy Taiga.$(li)Ice Spikes.$(li)Frozen Peaks.$(li)Jagged Peaks.$(li)Snowy Slopes.$(li)Grove.$(br2)
$(l)At bond 0:$()  Bonds $(l)half again as fast$()  as any other horse. Time near you, golden apples and name tags all count for more.$(br2)$(l)At bond 40:$()  That climbs to $(l)double$().
$(l)At bond 100:$()  $(l)Adaptable$(): a slice of every other class at once, including a fourth storage row and a higher step.
A compact American breed, at home on the trail or in the field.$(br2)Speed: $(l)8-15$()  blk/s$(br)Jump: $(l)2-4.5$()  blk$(br)Health: $(l)15-30$()
$(l)At bond 0:$()  Nearby hostiles are outlined and the horse snorts a warning. It also heals itself without food - $(l)a heart every 15 seconds$().

$(l)At bond 40:$()  Its healing climbs to $(l)a heart every 8 seconds$(), and it starts healing $(l)you$()  too - $(l)a heart every 10 seconds$()  in the saddle.$(br2)$(l)At bond 100:$()  Rider healing doubles to $(l)a heart every 5 seconds$().
Free-roaming and weatherproof, and rarely the same coat twice.$(br2)Speed: $(l)9-15$()  blk/s$(br)Jump: $(l)2-5.5$()  blk$(br)Health: $(l)25-40$()
$(l)At bond 0:$()  Soul sand, cobwebs, berries and honey do not slow it, and berry bushes draw no blood from it or its rider.

$(l)At bond 40:$()  $(l)Momentum$(): the longer it runs straight, the harder its charge lands - up to half again at full wind.$(br2)$(l)At bond 100:$()  $(l)Chain Charge$(): a charge that kills leaves no cooldown, so it can run straight through a group.
A French draft breed - heavy and muscular, but graceful for its size.$(br2)Speed: $(l)7-10$()  blk/s$(br)Jump: $(l)1-3.5$()  blk$(br)Health: $(l)35-50$()
$(l)At bond 0:$()  Stand still for a second, then move off, and you get +30%% for 5 seconds. Ten second cooldown.
$(l)At bond 40:$()  The burst climbs to +45%%.$(br2)$(l)At bond 100:$()  Cooldown drops to 8 seconds.
Stocky and broad-chested - a ranch horse, very fast over short distances.$(br2)Speed: $(l)11-15$()  blk/s$(br)Jump: $(l)3-6$()  blk$(br)Health: $(l)15-20$()
Spawns naturally in:$(br2)$(li)Plains.$(li)Sunflower Plains.$(li)Savanna.$(li)Savanna Plateau.$(li)Windswept Savanna.$(br2)
$(l)At bond 0:$()  Anything that has locked on but not yet swung gets snorted at and usually thinks better of it. Once it has hit you, it is too late.$(br2)$(l)At bond 40:$()  The radius widens.
$(l)At bond 100:$()  $(l)Brick Break$(), as the Belgian: a $(l)three-wide, three-tall$()  hole through weak blocks, walls three or more tall only. Off by default in the config.
England's largest draft horse - taller than a Clydesdale, just as patient, and feathered on all four legs.$(br2)Speed: $(l)7-10$()  blk/s$(br)Jump: $(l)1-3.5$()  blk$(br)Health: $(l)35-50$()
Spawns naturally in:$(br2)$(li)Forest.$(li)Birch Forest.$(li)Old Growth Birch Forest.$(li)Windswept Forest.$(li)Dark Forest.$(br2)
$(l)At bond 0:$()  +35%% speed for 3 seconds whenever you gallop on level ground, no wind-up, then 5 seconds before it fires again.
$(l)At bond 40:$()  The burst climbs to +50%%.$(br2)$(l)At bond 100:$()  The burst lasts 5 seconds, so you are boosted about half the time.
The classic racing horse - tall, lean, and an easy first pick for long rides.$(br2)Speed: $(l)11-15$()  blk/s$(br)Jump: $(l)3-6$()  blk$(br)Health: $(l)15-20$()
The five horse classes, the breeds inside each, and what every one of them can do.
The heavy tier. Slowest legs, most hearts, worst jump, and the only horses that will carry a chest and two riders at the same time.

Four rows of storage as standard.$(br)A chest $(l)and$()  two riders, which no other class allows.$(br)Pulls a loaded cart at full speed - every other class drags at -30%%.$(br)Heavy knockback resistance.
Charge damage 1.25x, knockback 2x, the hardest in the game.$(br)Spooks at half the usual rate.
Small, stubborn and much harder to kill than they look. Ponies go places the big breeds physically cannot.

Steps $(l)two full blocks$()  without jumping, where every other horse steps one.$(br)No fall damage under 15 blocks.$(br)Walks on powder snow with no hoof gear.$(br)Heals slowly on its own, without food.
Charge and kick damage 0.75x, with a race horse's light knockback.$(br)Standard spook chance.
The fastest legs in the stable on a single row of hearts - highest jump, softest charge.$(br2)All three get their speed a different way, so the ground you ride decides which one wins.
Fastest speed and highest jump of any class.$(br)Lowest health in the game.$(br)Charge and kick damage 0.6x, the weakest.$(br)Standard spook chance.
Every horse belongs to one of five classes. The class sets the range its speed, health and jump roll from, plus perks shared by every breed in it.
The breed decides your one unique ability, which grows at $(l)bond 40$()  and again at $(l)bond 100$().
Fifteen breeds, five classes. A horse's class sets its stat range and the perks it brings to the trail.
The horses you take somewhere dangerous. Nearly the toughest in the game, and the only ones that will not panic on you.
$(l)Never spook$(), at any bond level.$(br)Never rear when struck, so you keep your seat and your heading.$(br)Medkits last twice as long.$(br)Charge and kick damage 1.5x, the highest.
Stock horses, built for ground you have already worked. Give them a road and they pick up speed on it.
Health and pace sit close to an ordinary horse. What you are buying is everything around the riding.
+10%% speed on roads, rising to +20%% at bond 40 and +50%% at bond 100.$(br)Roads means paths, gravel, cobble, brick and anything tagged `horse_road`.$(br)Standard damage and spook chance.

A horse at a full $(l)gallop$()  in a straight line is a weapon - whatever you steer into takes the hit, with no swing of your own.$(br2)It arms after about $(l)a second$()  straight and keeps building for $(l)three$().
Turning sharply or stopping resets it; slower straight movement and jumps keep it building.$(br2)Only on the ground, with a rider, at a true gallop - free riding or the $(l)Gallop$()  gait.

Base hit $(l)7$(), scaled by class: $(l)War$()  1.5x, $(l)Draft$()  1.25x, $(l)Western$()  1x, $(l)Pony$()  0.75x, $(l)Race$()  0.6x.$(br2)$(li)$(l)Horse armor$()  adds up to $(l)3$(); a $(l)Clydesdale$()  gets up to $(l)5$().
$(li)Speed and wind-up near double it on a long straight run.$(li)Nothing lands harder than $(l)30$().$(br2)Draft horses throw a target furthest, war horses next. Light classes barely shift it.
When something hurts you, every horse you own within $(l)16 blocks$()  knows.$(br2)A loose horse at $(l)bond 40$()  or better runs your attacker down.
It breaks off under a third health, or if the fight drags $(l)32 blocks$()  from where it started. A horse told to $(l)Stay$()  stays.
Come at a horse from behind and it kicks, on the same class multiplier as the charge. Owned or wild, saddled or loose, they all do it.
Its owner, anyone they trust, and whoever is in the saddle never take one. After kicking, a horse not already defending someone bolts for about three seconds.
A meter beside your hotbar fills as the charge winds up. Full means the next thing you touch gets all of it; after a hit it refills over about $(l)five seconds$().
A $(l)Percheron$()  at bond 100 skips that wait whenever its charge kills. The $(l)Toggle Horse Charge$()  key switches it off.
A fight your horse picks isn't always one it can win. $(l)Horse Whistle$()  breaks off every horse you own that's fighting or bolting.
They don't trot back - they run for about $(l)three seconds$(), which is the point: it pulls a horse out from under something far too big. Whistle again once they're clear.
The charge spares everything you'd rather keep:$(br2)$(li)You, and anyone riding with you.$(li)Players you $(l)trust$().$(li)Other horses you own.$(li)Anything allied to you or to the horse.
The rest of the field in front of the horse is fair game.
The horse under you reacts the other way: it may panic and throw you off.$(br2)The odds drop as it learns to trust you - $(l)10%%$(), $(l)7%%$()  at bond 40, $(l)5%%$()  at bond 100.
$(l)Draft$()  horses spook half as often, $(l)War$()  horses never. It won't dump you in midair or over a drop.$(br2)$(l)horse_combat$()  turns all of this off, and each part has its own switch too.

Lightning or a creeper going off within $(l)16 blocks$()  is far scarier than a hit. A green horse always bolts, throwing you if you're riding it.$(br2)Bond $(l)40$()  cuts that to $(l)70%%$(), bond $(l)100$()  to $(l)50%%$().
$(l)Draft$()  horses bolt half as often, $(l)War$()  horses never. A horse told to $(l)stay$()  holds its ground.
The working end of the Glidewing Harness. Keep spares: one on an $(l)Anvil$()  refuels a spent harness by $(l)80%$().
A small copper-and-gold capsule. No harness without it, and a spent harness runs on it.
Every craft in the mod, with a note on when each piece is worth making.
Right-click the cart with a $(l)Chest$()  to mount it in the bed. $(l)Sneak$()  and right-click to open it: a full $(l)double chest$()  on the small one, $(l)ninety$()  slots on the large.
A chest fills a small bed, so no back-seat passengers - the driver's bench still seats two. The large cart keeps two of its four bed seats.
Slot the cart into the $(l)Upgraded Saddle$()  and it rolls along behind your horse. It shares the harness slot, so a horse carries one or the other.
Quickest way: right-click the horse holding the cart, as long as it wears an Upgraded Saddle and that slot is empty.
Right-click the small cart with any $(l)hoe$()  to drop a plough behind the bed.

Drive over grass, dirt, coarse or rooted dirt, podzol or mycelium and it turns a $(l)three-wide$()  strip to farmland in one pass. It reaches two blocks up or down, so hills get turned too, and clears grass and flowers.

Fit a $(l)shovel$() instead to lay a three-wide $(l)dirt path$() over grass and dirt using the same plough.$(br2)The tool loses a point per block and takes the plough with it when it breaks, so bring a good one - $(l)enchantments count$().$(br2)$(l)Shears$()  take it back off, plough before chest. Only the small cart takes one.
Two $(l)Wheels$(), a row of planks for the bed, and two slabs on top. Make the wheels first.

A small cart seats four: two on the driver's bench, first up drives, and two in the bed. The large cart carries $(l)six$(), four in the bed.$(br2)Animals climb into the bed on their own, and one can ride shotgun beside you.

The cart takes anything a $(l)boat$()  would, and its $(l)Riders$()  tab picks which: passive, neutral or hostile.$(br2)$(l)Sneak$()  and right-click an animal to set it down, or hit $(l)Unload all$().

The big wagon has a tarp roof. Undead riding under it $(l)won't burn in daylight$(), so it's a safe way to haul a zombie villager home. Fold the tarp away on the $(l)Cart$()  tab and they burn like anywhere else.
$(l)Shears$()  take the chest off and drop it beside the horse. Empty it first - a loaded chest refuses.
Things come off in the order they went on, and the slot flashes $(l)red$()  if you skip a step: chest, then cart, then saddle.
Fit a cart to a $(l)draft$()  horse and you get the big one, a covered wagon on four wheels. Every other class pulls the small two-wheeled cart.
$(l)Sneak$()  and right-click the cart, or press $(l)Open Cart$(), and pick a model on the $(l)Cart$()  tab. Parked carts too.
Only drafts may go large, and a cart refuses if its passengers or load wouldn't fit the new bed, or a parked one has no room to grow.
Right-click the ground to stand a cart up on its own, shafts down, no horse needed. A parked cart is decoration, but a $(l)Chest$()  works on it as on a hitched one.
Hit it a few times to pick it up, like a boat. Break one with a chest fitted and the chest and its contents drop too.
Horseshoes take $(l)Frost Walker$()  at an $(l)Anvil$()  from an enchanted book. A horse running over water then leaves a trail of $(l)frosted ice$(), like a player wearing frost-walker boots.
Horseshoes cross powder snow instead of falling through, and soften fall damage. Everyday tack for mountains and cold biomes.
Copper ingots and a leather strap, for a steadier step in rough country.
Freeze radius follows the $(l)Frost Walker level$(). The trail samples the horse's movement, so fast horses can't outrun it. Lava still isn't safe.
If a hit would drop your horse below half health, the medkit is spent and grants $(l)Regeneration$(), $(l)Instant Health$(), $(l)Resistance$()  and $(l)Fire Resistance$().
Emergency tack: wool, healing supplies and a regeneration potion.
About $(l)2 minutes$()  of gliding. It only wears while open, and a gauge beside your hotbar shows what's left.
Run it dry and it stays on the horse but won't deploy. Refuel it on an $(l)Anvil$()  with a $(l)Canister$(): one restores $(l)80%$(). Nothing else repairs it.
Built for ravines and cliffs. On a big fall it deploys, slows the descent, and can cancel fall damage entirely.

Right-click the horse holding it to fit, as long as it wears an Upgraded Saddle with that slot empty. Horses only - mules, donkeys and the undead sort can't wear one.(I'm too lazy to make separate models)
Bind your canisters into the full harness and mount it on the upgraded saddle.
Every craft in the tack room, gathered here for a quick reference.
Any $(l)Better Horses$()  item plus a $(l)Book$()  makes a fresh handbook.
Keep one in your travel chest and one at home. Cheap to remake.

Any horse that wears armour also gets a $(l)banner$()  slot, upgraded saddle or not. The banner hangs from the armour, so fit armour first.$(br2)Horse armour also takes armour enchantments from books at an $(l)Anvil$().

Any carpet in the $(l)Carpet$()  slot is drawn in place of the saddle, over any armour. Each colour has its own design, fitted to every breed.$(br2)It is purely for looks, and only the mod's breeds take one.
A plain $(l)Chest$()  gives storage on the horse screen: three rows on most horses, more on drafts and a few others. Empty it before removing, or the contents drop.
An $(l)Ender Chest$()  instead makes those 27 slots your $(l)Ender Inventory$(), shared with every ender chest you own. Swapping back keeps the contents.
The core of the tack room: a vanilla $(l)Saddle$(), copper and a few diamonds.

Hold the $(l)Upgraded Saddle$()  and look at a horse for a $(l)Horse Stats$()  panel above your hotbar:$(br2)$(li)$(l)Gender$()$(li)$(l)Breed$()$(li)$(l)Speed$()  - blocks per second$(li)$(l)Jump$()  - block height
Handy for checking wild stock before taming.
Equipped, it opens five gear slots: $(l)Chest$(), $(l)Horseshoe$(), $(l)Medkit$(), $(l)Glidewing$()  and $(l)Carpet$(). Most of the mod starts here.
A wheel alone does little. Two, with planks and slabs, make a $(l)Horse Cart$().
Sticks for spokes, planks for rim and hub - any wood. Two make a cart.
The coat always comes from the palette the inherited breed allows. Two $(l)Quarter$()  horses give a Quarter pattern; a mixed pair can throw either side's palette.
Which coat is a coin flip: $(l)half$()  the time it wears a parent's coat, the other half one $(l)neither parent wears$()  - so two black Shires often throw a bay or a roan.
A $(l)Golden Carrot$(), $(l)Golden Apple$()  or $(l)Enchanted Golden Apple$()  puts a tamed adult in love. Servers can change that list.
A horse that bred recently will not take a golden apple until its cooldown is over.
Two horses of the same gender won't mate - you'll be told so, the food is still eaten, and the hearts just run out.
When a foal is born:$(br2)$(li)$(l)Gender$()  is a coin flip.$(li)$(l)Breed$()  comes from one parent at 50/50. Matching parents pass it cleanly; different breeds give the foal a $(l)(mix)$()  tag.
$(li)Cross-species pairs (horse + donkey) give the matching species placeholder.
Health, speed and jump are $(l)max(parent1, parent2) + delta$(), delta rolling $(l)-0.5$()  to $(l)+1.0$(). Foals can beat both parents, but the foal's breed range is the ceiling.
Every horse has a gender, a breed, and a coat, and they all get passed down. Learn the science of stable husbandry.
Beyond $(l)Bond$(), every horse carries four pieces of identity:$(br2)$(li)$(l)Gender$()  - male or female, donkeys and mules included.

$(li)$(l)Breed$()  - one of fifteen real breeds; a species label for donkeys, mules and skeleton or zombie horses.$(li)$(l)Mixed-Breed$()  - a $(l)(mix)$()  tag when a foal inherits two breeds.$(li)$(l)Coat$()  - color and markings, tied to the breed.

Press $(l)Horse Whistle$()  while mounted for the $(l)Horse Info Screen$()  - gender, breed, coat and stat bars. Holding the $(l)Upgraded Saddle$()  and looking at any horse shows a $(l)Horse Stats$()  panel with gender, breed, speed and jump.
Pull up a hay bale, stablemaster. This handbook is your barn-side cheat sheet for turning an ordinary horse into a trail partner worth keeping.
A few easy riding tricks for long roads, rough water, forest shortcuts, and hauling a friend along for the trip.
Press $(l)Gear Up$()  (V) while riding to shift up a gait: $(l)Walk$(), $(l)Trot$(), $(l)Canter$(), $(l)Gallop$(). $(l)Gear Down$()  (Z) shifts back down, all the way to a halt.
The current one prints over your hotbar. An $(l)Icelandic$()  tolts where others trot.$(br2)Once set, the horse holds the gait. You steer, and never touch $(l)W$().

Hold $(l)W$()  or $(l)S$()  and the gait steps aside until you let go, then picks up where it was. Neither key wraps: $(l)Gear Up$()  stops at $(l)Gallop$(), $(l)Gear Down$()  at a halt.$(br2)Cruise clears the gait outright, as does dismounting or changing horse.
$(li)$(l)Walk$()  - about $(l)2$()  blk/s.$(li)$(l)Trot$()  - about $(l)4.4$()  blk/s.$(li)$(l)Canter$()  - about $(l)6.8$()  blk/s.$(li)$(l)Gallop$()  - the horse's own top speed.
The first three are set paces - a plough horse and a racer walk side by side. Only the gallop shows what a fast horse is worth, and a slower horse just gives you all it has.
A $(l)Saddle$()  (vanilla or upgraded) on a horse in $(l)Creative$()  tames it instantly, no waiting on hearts.
You step off on the side you are looking toward, and the horse starts to wander there unless the server picked follow or stay.

Riding keeps your $(l)hunger$()  and $(l)XP$()  bars on screen, with the horse's hearts above them.$(br2)$(l)Ctrl$()  plus your inventory key, or the icon beside the horse screen, swaps to your own inventory and back.
A ridden horse should feel responsive. Better Horses fixes the small frictions vanilla horses had.
Mounting no longer snaps your camera - the $(l)horse turns to match you$().

Standing still, you get $(l)90 degrees$()  of free look before it follows, so you can scan the horizon without dismounting.$(br2)Hold $(l)Free Look$()  (Left Ctrl) to look anywhere while the horse keeps its heading.
$(li)Step height is raised a tenth, so a gallop doesn't trip on slabs, paths or full blocks.$(li)Mounted block-breaking is 75% of on-foot speed.
Double-tap $(l)W$()  to auto-ride: the horse keeps moving and you just steer. Tap a movement key to take back control.
$(li)Two players can share one horse.$(li)The first rider keeps the reins.$(li)The second gets a back seat.
Press $(l)Rear Horse$()  to put a horse on its hind legs - the one you're riding, or one you're looking at within $(l)12 blocks$().

It must be yours or one whose owner trusts you, and it ignores you while someone else holds the reins.$(br2)Purely for show. A horse also rears when struck, costing you a moment's steering, though a $(l)War$()  horse never does.
$(li)They float instead of sinking in water.$(li)They cross water faster.$(li)Leaves lose collision while you ride, so forests feel like a path.

boss_screen.traveloptics.general.eclipse: Eclipse attacks are among the most dangerous attacks a boss can perform and are marked early by a desaturated screen effect. A prompt appears at the top of the screen indicating whether Counterspell or Reversal can counter the incoming attack. Some bosses may also have a specific visual tell before the attack lands. Failing to counter an Eclipse attack is almost always fatal.
boss_screen.traveloptics.general.element: Getting hit by Zaevorath's non-physical attacks will generally apply a debuff based on her current element. Nature applies Lesser Irradiated, reducing healing received by 10% per amp. Fire applies Rend, reducing armor by 5% per amp. Aqua applies Mana Wither, reducing the victim's maximum mana by 10% per amp.
boss_screen.traveloptics.general.jump_at: Certain attacks are marked with a special arrow up indicator icon on the boss, showing that the attack must be dodged by jumping. These attacks are extremely powerful and can often end or severely injure you if the jump is not timed properly. The indicator's duration indicates how quickly you need to react, with faster indicators requiring a quicker response. Different jump attacks may have different indicator durations and timing requirements.
boss_screen.traveloptics.general.loot_pr: Dying within a certain radius of the entity will prevent your inventory from dropping... this acts as a localized Keep Inventory feature. The radius varies but usually big enough
boss_screen.traveloptics.general.status_: Certain overpowered status effects, such as Abyssal Shroud and Heartstop, are ineffective and will be automatically cleared every 3 seconds. Additionally, hard crowd control spells, such as Vortex of the Deep or Black Hole, etc., will be automatically dispelled.

Certain overpowered status effects, such as Abyssal Shroud and Evasion, are ineffective and will be automatically cleared every 3 seconds. Hard crowd control spells, such as Vortex of the Deep or Black Hole etc., will also be automatically dispelled. Additionally, any Resistance effect exceeding Level II will be automatically discarded and replaced with Resistance II while retaining its original duration.
boss_screen.traveloptics.nightwarden.adv: The Nightwarden gradually adapts to damage types, eventually reducing incoming damage from that type upto a certain amount. Damage dealt while adapting still works and contributes to his Resurgence Counter.

In Phase 3, the Nightwarden drops clones one by one on his target's position, which deals magic damage and, if it hits, removes one of your positive effects and may apply Anti-Heal. The Nightwarden can predict your movement, so deceive him by moving unpredictably - use quick direction changes or fast strafes, or boost your movement speed.

When he teleports the first time, he takes a moment to grab his scythe before spinning once. After the second teleport, he immediately performs another spin. You can easily avoid the first spin by running away since there’s a short delay after he grabs the scythe. When you hear the second teleport sound, Blink or teleport right after it to dodge the follow-up spin completely or can use slight movement speed boost to evade it.

The Nightwarden fights in three phases. Phase 1 is spell-focused and only takes full damage from certain magic types. Phase 2 is melee-focused, resisting most non-melee damage while unleashing combo attacks. Phase 3 combines melee and magic, becoming more aggressive, also empowering some attacks.

Filling the Resurgence Counter increases the Nightwarden’s magic power and melee lifesteal. The bonuses applies depending on his phase and attack type. The counter can only be reset using Anti-Magic (e.g. Counterspell), which also clears all adaptations from the Nightwarden and removes every effect from nearby entities.

When he teleports to the center and starts channeling this attack, keep your distance. If you’re too close when the first burst hits, it can deal massive damage, almost a one-shot without defense abilities and greatly heal the Nightwarden. During this time, the dragon he summons deal constant percent-based damage that ignores I-frames.

When transitioning from Phase 2 to Phase 3, he begins charging Supernova. Watch for the color change in the Dying Star, counterspelling right after it changes will cancel the Supernova completely and deal an instance of unavoidable percent-based damage back to him.
boss_screen.traveloptics.nightwarden.dif: Shear of the Stars attack now create Stellar Trails
Melee hits in phase 2 and 3 will apply Anti-Heal for 2sec
Meant for players with utterly broken stats/mods
Shear of the Stars attack now create Stellar Trails

boss_screen.traveloptics.nightwarden.lor: Once a mortal mage driven by love and loss, he sought the forbidden path to bring back the one he lost. His search led him beyond what mortals were ever meant to reach into the silent threshold between life and the void. Now bound within a shell that moves but no longer lives, he remains aware, able to feel, to listen - yet forever unable to touch the world he once knew. What lingers is not the man he was, but the echo of his promise, refusing to fade.
boss_screen.traveloptics.nightwarden.sug: Counterspell provides a major advantage in battle
Bring at least 3 schools of damage spells
“Blink” spell can be used as dodge-roll
boss_screen.traveloptics.nightwarden.tit: He who gave up being, to keep a promise
boss_screen.traveloptics.zaevorath.advan: Zaevorath burrows underground and becomes invisible, periodically striking upward at her target from below. Her head briefly surfaces from the ground during each strike and can be attacked. The same phase elemental conditions apply. Hitting the exposed head during this state increases damage dealt to her by 40%. Successfully biting her target regenerates her Elemental Shield based on the max shield amount.

Zaevorath is protected by an Elemental Shield that changes with each phase. Nature shield takes increased damage from Fire, Fire shield takes increased damage from Aqua, and Aqua shield takes increased damage from Lightning. Attacking with the wrong element reduces damage dealt. Attacking with the same element as her current shield will heal it instead. The shield's remaining strength is shown on the bar below her main health bar.
Each phase introduces a distinct, high-damage attack: Reappearance of Ruin, Descent of Decay, and Rift of the Waning Moon. These attacks deal an incredible amount of damage and should be avoided.

Feast is an Eclipse attack and Zaevorath's most dangerous move, only usable when her health is at or below 50%. The Eclipse effect marks it early with a desaturated screen. Once the Eclipse effect fades, her elemental alignment and body color shift into a Lunar state. A Counterspell cast during this window will interrupt and cancel the attack. Failing to interrupt allows her to complete Feast, instantly executing her target, restoring her to full health, and fully refreshing her current Elemental Shield. Each successful Feast also adds a stack of Devour, which increases her attack damage and can stack infinitely. A successful Feast does not apply a cooldown, allowing her to attempt it again as long as the health condition is met. Interrupting it does apply a cooldown.
Zaevorath fights in three phases, each requiring a different elemental approach to deal with her shield effectively. Her behavior and attacks shift with each phase transition.

Once the Elemental Shield is fully depleted, Zaevorath activates a Shield Layer for additional protection. The Shield Layer refreshes on every phase transition along with the element change, so it must be dealt with each phase. A Counterspell cast on her will dissipate it. Leaving the Shield Layer active causes her to take reduced damage from all sources. Once the shield and the layer are both gone, her health takes damage from any source including the active element, and melee attacks deal full damage directly.
boss_screen.traveloptics.zaevorath.lore: She was not born - she was built. A group of bio inventors attempted to create a living being from opposing elemental forces, held together by science and pieces of ancient magic they barely understood. The result was BMSL-01, their first and only success, and their greatest mistake. The forces inside her were never meant to coexist. When they began tearing each other apart, her creators abandoned her rather than face what they had made, leaving her deep in a cave to fade on her own. She did not fade. The forces kept clashing, her mind fracturing slowly under the weight of what she was never meant to be. What remains is not the creature they made, only a hunger with no end.
boss_screen.traveloptics.zaevorath.name: Zaevorath

Aqua, Fire, and Lightning damage spells are recommended
"Blink" spell can be used as dodge-roll

config.combat_evolution.datapack_help.be: Plays an Epic Fight animation, with attack phase overrides, timed events, and hit events.
Guards against incoming attacks for a set duration. Supports counterattacks, guard events, and movement while guarding.
Moves forward/backward and sideways for a set duration, for repositioning, retreating, or strafing.
config.combat_evolution.datapack_help.co: Checks whether the current target's Epic Fight action state level is within an inclusive integer range.
Checks whether the current target's Epic Fight action state level matches any integer in the list.
Checks the target's angle relative to this entity's facing. LEFT/RIGHT use 0–180° on that side; ROUND uses a circular range that can cross 0°.
Checks whether the current target has the specified /tag scoreboard tag. Enter the tag name.
Compares this entity's health or health ratio with a threshold. A ratio of 0.5 means 50% of maximum health; CONTAIN includes equality.
Checks whether this entity's CE phase variable is within an inclusive integer range. Behavior start settings can modify this variable.
Checks whether this entity's CE phase variable matches any integer in the list.
Compares this entity's CE stamina or stamina ratio with a threshold. A ratio of 0.5 means 50% of maximum stamina; CONTAIN includes equality.
Checks whether the current target is in Epic Fight's guard break state.
Checks distance to the current target in blocks. Includes the minimum and excludes the maximum.
Checks this entity's health or health ratio using the selected comparator. Ratios use 0–1.
Checks the Epic Fight weapon category of the item in the offhand.
Checks a player's name. Requires a player context and may not apply to ordinary mobs.
Rolls independently each time the condition is checked. Range: 0–1; 0.25 gives a 25% chance to pass each check.
Checks whether the specified skill is active. Requires a player skill context and may not apply to ordinary mobs.
Uses Epic Fight's NBT condition to check a data value at the specified key path.
Uses Epic Fight's angle condition to compare target direction with this entity's facing, in degrees.
Checks the angle between target direction and this entity's facing on the horizontal plane, in degrees.
Uses Epic Fight's distance condition to check distance to the current target, in blocks.
Uses Epic Fight's eye height condition to check the target's height relative to this entity.
Condition %s is supplied by another mod or registry entry. Consult its documentation for parameters and supported entities.
config.combat_evolution.datapack_help.ev: Fires when a guard hit selects a counterattack. Can cancel the guard hit animation for that hit.
Fires when this entity's attack is blocked or parried, filtered by attack phase and whether the defense was a parry.
Legacy behavior start event. Runs when the behavior starts, just like onBehaviorStart.
Fires when an attack hits an entity and returns the selected result, optionally for a specific phase. MISSED broadly covers hits that are evaded or canceled.
Fires when this behavior starts. Can run a command alongside behavior start settings such as stamina and phase changes.
Fires when the counterattack actually starts.
Fires on a successful guard hit when guard is not broken and no counterattack is being prepared.
Handles this entity's incoming hit check. Can run a command and return a hit result; it does not write back a damage amount.
Runs commands by animation time: TICK every tick; IN_TIME once when crossing a time point; BETWEEN_TIMES every tick from the inclusive start to the exclusive end. Times are in seconds.
config.combat_evolution.datapack_help.fi: Adds to this node's extra end cooldown in ticks, which is added to the root's end cooldown. If setCoolDown is also present, it overrides this value.
Adds to this entity's CE phase variable when the behavior starts. Negative values decrease it. Use phase conditions to build multi-stage combat.
Adds this amount to this entity's CE stamina when the behavior starts. Negative values reduce stamina.
Restricts which global roots from this combat set may be inserted. An empty list allows all global roots in the set. Invalid references are retained and do not make the list unrestricted.
Upper angle bound in degrees.
Lower angle bound in degrees.
Epic Fight animation played by this behavior. Timed events use this animation's timeline.
Animation playback speed multiplier: 1 is normal speed, 2 is double speed. Timed events still use animation time.
Transition time parameter when switching to this animation, in seconds.
Selects the armature resource used for animation. Its bones must match the model and animations.
Multiplies base armor negation for the selected attack phase. A base value of 0 remains 0 after multiplication.
Selects an entity attribute and its base value override. Equipment, effects, and other modifiers can still affect the result.
Base value for the selected entity attribute. Equipment, effects, and other attribute modifiers can still affect the result.
Attempts to return to the previously saved behavior when this root ends. Requires a behavior that can be resumed.
Fixed stamina lost when this entity's attack is parried. This is not health damage.
Names the current behavior node for identifying it in the hierarchy, searching, and behavior switching.
Duration of guard break after stamina is exhausted, in ticks. Normally 20 ticks = 1 second.
Allows this mob to be considered for assassination. Distance, angle, awareness, and other requirements still apply.
Allows the current behavior to select global behavior roots within this combat set, subject to the global name allowlist.
Allows this node to be considered for interrupting its parent. The parent's interrupt window, this node's conditions, and selection rules must still allow it.
Cancels this guard hit animation when a counterattack is prepared, allowing the counter to proceed without that animation.
Epic Fight weapon category required for the offhand item.
Name displayed on the boss bar.
Resource path of a custom boss bar texture. It must meet the selected style's requirements.
Selects a registered CE boss bar style.
Enables a CE boss bar for this mob.
Resource ID of the sound event to play, e.g. combat_evolution:music.test_bgm.
Music playback cycle duration in ticks. Determines when looping restarts; it is not an offset for skipping an intro.
Fade-in duration when music starts, in ticks.
Fade-out duration before the music cycle ends, in ticks. Fading starts at duration minus this value.
Restarts playback when the configured music cycle duration is reached.
Enables the configured boss battle music for this mob.
Volume multiplier for this music. Game sound settings also affect the actual volume.
Chance to pass each condition check, from 0 to 1: 0 never passes, 1 always passes.
Movement speed multiplier passed to navigation while chasing a target. Actual speed also depends on movement attributes and pathfinding.
Runs on the server at the selected executor's position and rotation, with permission level 2 and command output suppressed.
GREATER/LESS mean above/below; ABSOLUTE uses points, RATIO uses a ratio. CE's CONTAIN variants include equality.
Initial cooldown after the behavior root is loaded, in ticks. Normally 20 ticks = 1 second.
Animation played when a defense behavior counterattacks.
Chance to counter on each guard hit in RANDOM mode, from 0 to 1.
NEVER disables counters; RANDOM rolls a chance on each guard hit; END counters when the accumulated guard hit count reaches the threshold.
Multiplies base damage for the selected attack phase. 1 keeps the original value; 2 doubles it.
Open the list to search and select damage type tags added to this attack. Multiple tags can be selected; hover over an entry for details, then apply the selection.
Upper distance bound in blocks. CE's target distance condition excludes this value.
Lower distance bound in blocks. CE's target distance condition includes this value.
Sets the Epic Fight faction for faction and friendly-fire checks. Actual target selection still depends on the entity's target goals and other logic.
Start angle in degrees. In ROUND mode, 330→30 crosses the front; 0→360 normalizes to the same angle and does not represent a full circle.
Forward/backward movement input while wandering: positive moves forward, negative backward. Actual speed also depends on the entity's movement attributes.
Whether to play the guarding pose animation while wandering during defense.
Multiplies the base guard stamina cost factor for this behavior. The default 1 preserves the base cost; 0 makes guarding cost no stamina.
Stamina cost factor applied to incoming impact when a datapack mob guards a hit.
Duration of guarding in ticks. Normally 20 ticks = 1 second.
Switches to guarding while moving. The numeric field sets the duration in ticks; forward and strafe control movement direction.
Threshold for this entity's health. ABSOLUTE uses health points; RATIO uses current/max health, e.g. 0.5 means 50%.

Inclusive upper integer bound. Phase conditions check this entity's CE phase; attack level conditions check the current target's action state level.
Inclusive lower integer bound. Phase conditions check this entity's CE phase; attack level conditions check the current target's action state level.

Data key or path used by Epic Fight's NBT value condition.
Allowed action state levels of the current target, as comma-separated integers.
Upper bound of the condition's range. Units and boundary rules depend on the condition.
Base cooldown before the behavior root can be selected again after ending, in ticks. Node-specific extra end cooldown is added to this value.
Accumulated guard hit count required to counter in END mode.
Lower bound of the condition's range. Units and boundary rules depend on the condition.

Name used by the player name condition.

Off: self. On: interaction entity for hit/blocked events, attacker for guard hit events, current target for other events including hurt events. No valid executor means no command; @s refers to the executor.
On matches parried attacks only. With the filter off, both ordinary blocks and parries can trigger the event. This does not grant the ability to parry.
Attack phase index within an animation, starting at 0. -1 means all phases. This is separate from the entity's CE phase variable.
Allowed values of this entity's CE phase variable, as comma-separated integers such as 0, 2, 4.
Candidates are compared by priority first. Eligible candidates at the highest priority are then selected by weight. Roots require a priority above 0 for regular selection.
Time to recover from empty to full stamina after the guard break waiting period, in ticks.
Selects the client entity renderer. It must be compatible with the model and armature.
Resets the remaining guard time to the full configured duration on each guard hit.
DEFAULT preserves the original result; other values override this incoming hit interaction's result category. This does not modify or write back damage.
Names a behavior root within this combat set. Global behavior references use this name; keep it unique within the set.
Client model scale multiplier. 1 keeps the original size; this does not resize the entity's hitbox.
End angle in degrees. In ROUND mode, an end below the start creates a range crossing 0°.
Sets this node's extra end cooldown in ticks, overriding addCoolDown. The result is added to the root's end cooldown.
Sets this entity's CE phase variable when the behavior starts. If combined with a phase addition, loader registration order determines execution order.
Sets this entity's CE stamina when the behavior starts. If combined with a stamina addition, loader registration order determines execution order.
LEFT/RIGHT check 0–180° on the left/right side. ROUND: 0° front, 90° right, 180° rear, 270° left.
Resource ID of the skill to check, in namespace:path form. Requires a player context with skill support.
Threshold for this entity's CE stamina. ABSOLUTE uses stamina points; RATIO uses current/max stamina.
In the normal stamina state, ticks to wait after leaving an action or guard before regeneration starts. Requires the stamina regeneration attribute.
Controls interruption without stun immunity. Exclusions: 1 none; 2 SHORT; 3 SHORT/LONG; 4 SHORT/LONG/HOLD; 5 as 4 + FALL; 6 as 4 + KNOCKDOWN; 7 as 4 + both; other values as 7 + NEUTRALIZE.

default keeps the animation's setting; NONE applies no regular stun; other values select a stun type. Target immunity can still affect the result.
Name of the /tag scoreboard tag required on the current target.
End animation time for an interval event, in seconds. Execution stops at this time; it must be greater than the start.
Animation time in seconds. IN_TIME fires once when crossing this point; BETWEEN_TIMES starts running every tick from this point.
TICK runs every tick; IN_TIME runs once when crossing timeStart; BETWEEN_TIMES runs every tick in [timeStart, timeEnd). Times are in seconds.
Data value to match in Epic Fight's NBT value condition.

Extra time to wait after this behavior ends if no child behavior can run yet. If a child's conditions become satisfied during the wait, execution continues with that child. In ticks; normally 20 ticks = 1 second.
Duration of wandering in ticks. Normally 20 ticks = 1 second.
Relative selection weight among candidates at the same priority. Use positive values; higher values make selection more likely.

config.structure_layout_optimizer.dedupl: Deduplicate shuffled template pool element list

Whether to use an alternative strategy to make structure layouts generate slightly even faster than the default optimization this mod has for template pool weights. This alternative strategy works by changing the list of pieces that structures collect from the template pool to not have duplicate entries.
This will not break the structure generation, but it will make the structure layout different than if this config was off (breaking vanilla seed parity). The cost of speed may be worth it in large modpacks where many structure mods are using very high weight values in their template pools.

Pros: Get a bit more performance from high weight Template Pool Structures.
Cons: Loses parity with vanilla seeds on the layout of the structure. (Structure layout is not broken, just different)

config.waystones.cooldowns.warpStoneCool: The cooldown between usages of the warp stone in seconds. This is bound to the player, not the item, so multiple warp stones share the same cooldown.
config.waystones.cooldowns.warpStoneUseT: The time in ticks that it takes to use a warp stone. This is the charge-up time when holding right-click.
config.waystones.inventoryButton.creativ: The x position of the warp button in the creative menu.
The y position of the warp button in the creative menu.
config.waystones.inventoryButton.invento: Set to 'NONE' for no inventory button. Set to 'NEAREST' for an inventory button that teleports to the nearest waystone. Set to 'ANY' for an inventory button that opens the waystone selection menu. Set to a waystone name for an inventory button that teleports to a specifically named waystone.
config.waystones.inventoryButton.warpBut: The x position of the warp button in the inventory.
The y position of the warp button in the inventory.
config.waystones.restrictions.allowWayst: Set to true if players should be able to teleport between waystones by simply right-clicking a waystone.
config.waystones.restrictions.dimensiona: Set to 'ALLOW' to allow dimensional warp in general. Set to 'GLOBAL_ONLY' to restrict dimensional warp to global waystones. Set to 'DENY' to disallow all dimensional warps.
List of dimensions that players are allowed to warp cross-dimension from and to. If left empty, all dimensions except those in dimensionalWarpDenyList are allowed.
List of dimensions that players are not allowed to warp cross-dimension from and to. Only used if dimensionalWarpAllowList is empty.
config.waystones.restrictions.generatedW: If enabled, waystones generated in worldgen are unbreakable.
config.waystones.restrictions.globalWays: Set to false to allow non-creative players to make waystones globally activated for all players.
config.waystones.restrictions.leashedDen: List of leashed mobs that cannot be taken with you when teleporting.
config.waystones.restrictions.restrictRe: If enabled, only the owner of a waystone (the one who placed it) can rename it.
config.waystones.restrictions.restrictTo: If enabled, only creative players can place, edit or break waystones. This does NOT disable the crafting recipe.
config.waystones.restrictions.transportL: If enabled, leashed mobs will be teleported with you.
Whether to take leashed mobs with you when teleporting between dimensions.
config.waystones.worldGen.customWaystone: These names will be used for the PRESET name generation mode. See the nameGenerationMode option for more info.
config.waystones.worldGen.dimensionAllow: List of dimensions that waystones are allowed to spawn in through world gen. If left empty, all dimensions except those in worldGenDimensionDenyList are used.
config.waystones.worldGen.dimensionDenyL: List of dimensions that waystones are not allowed to spawn in through world gen. Only used if worldGenDimensionAllowList is empty.
config.waystones.worldGen.forceSpawnInVi: Ensures that pretty much every village will have a waystone, by spawning it as early as possible. In addition, this means waystones will generally be located in the center of the village.
config.waystones.worldGen.frequency.tool: Approximate chunk distance between waystones generated freely in world generation. Set to 0 to disable generation.
config.waystones.worldGen.nameGeneration: Set to 'PRESET_FIRST' to first use names from the custom names list. Set to 'PRESET_ONLY' to use only those custom names. Set to 'MIXED' to have some waystones use custom names, and others random names.
config.waystones.worldGen.spawnInVillage: Set to true if waystones should be added to the generation of villages. Some villages may still spawn without a waystone.
Set to 'DEFAULT' to only generate the normally textured waystones. Set to 'MOSSY' or 'SANDY' to generate all as that variant. Set to 'BIOME' to make the style depend on the biome it is generated in.
config.waystones.xpCost.blocksPerXpLevel: The amount of blocks per xp level requirement. If set to 500, the base xp cost for travelling 1000 blocks will be 2 levels.
config.waystones.xpCost.dimensionalWarpX: The base xp level cost when travelling between dimensions. Ignores block distance.
config.waystones.xpCost.globalWaystoneXp: The multiplier applied to the cooldown when teleporting to a global waystone via inventory button or warp stone.
config.waystones.xpCost.inventoryButtonX: The multiplier applied to the base xp cost when teleporting via the inventory button.
config.waystones.xpCost.inverseXpCost.to: Set to true if experience cost should be inverted, meaning the shorter the distance, the more expensive. Can be used to encourage other methods for short-distance travel.
config.waystones.xpCost.maximumBaseXpCos: The maximum base xp cost (may be exceeded by multipliers defined below), set to 0 to disable all distance-based XP costs.
config.waystones.xpCost.minimumBaseXpCos: The minimum base xp cost (may be subceeded by multipliers defined below).
config.waystones.xpCost.portstoneXpCostM: The multiplier applied to the base xp cost when teleporting from a portstone.
config.waystones.xpCost.sharestoneXpCost: The multiplier applied to the base xp cost when teleporting from one sharestone to another.
config.waystones.xpCost.warpPlateXpCostM: The multiplier applied to the base xp cost when teleporting from one warp plate to another.
config.waystones.xpCost.warpStoneXpCostM: The multiplier applied to the base xp cost when teleporting using a Warp Stone item (not the Waystone block, Konstantin)
config.waystones.xpCost.waystoneXpCostMu: The multiplier applied to the base xp cost when teleporting from one waystone to another.
config.waystones.xpCost.xpCostPerLeashed: How much xp is needed per leashed animal to travel with you.

createdieselgenerators.ponder.large_dies: Setting up a Modular Diesel Engine
Modular Diesel Generators function like normal Diesel generators.
Once you give them some fuel, they will produce Kinetic Energy ...
They will generate stress proportionally to how much engines you stack.
Beneath the surface, some chunks hide Crude Oil deposits
To find these Chunks, you'll need to use an Oil Scanner

Additionally, different Biomes will have different levels of Crude Oil
You can extract the Crude Oil with a pumpjack
createdieselgenerators.ponder.pumpjack.t: Every Pumpjack needs a Pumpjack Bearing
... you can extract the crude oil with a Mechanical Pump.
Next, build the body of the Pumpjack
Don't forget to glue the contraption!
To power the Pumpjack, you'll need to use a Pumpjack Crank.
To start extracting Crude Oil from the chunk, you'll need to excavate a hole below the pumpjack head
Place a straight, vertical pipe going all the way to bedrock ...

description.config.bclib.client.ui.force: The world type determines how a world is generated. In most cases, BetterX should be kept as the default (you can change the type at any time in the world creation screen). This type is optimized for maximum compatibility between DataPacks, our mod, and other Fabric mods. It also provides some unique features for BetterNether and BetterEnd. You should only disable this option if you have a reason to do so!
description.config.bclib.client.ui.suppr: The warning screen appears whenever your world does not use the vanilla version settings. This can happen when you start a world in a preview version, but also when you use mods to change the world creation. If this option is enabled, the warning will be skipped when you load an existing world. It will still be displayed (as a reminder) when a new world is created.
BCLib includes a simple version checker that can notify you when new updates of our mods are available. To do this, we need to read a resource from one of our web servers. To process the request, together with your IP address (we need to know where to send the response) we also send your Minecraft version (so we can choose the right mod version). The transmitted data will never be used or processed by us for other purposes, but must be stored in our log files for 4 weeks for legal reasons.
