dialogue.saintsdragons.ivy.dragon_atroxi: Atroxia regalis. Now that one? The name? I did not make that up.
The gold shining off of it. Looking it in the snow is truly something.
If the reports about its cryomancy are accurate, I'd wager most of the energy is being routed through there.
The head shape reminds me a lot of the Egyptian nemes.
Gold ornamentation, the markings around the eyes... very pharaoh-like.
Which is ironic, because this dragon lives in cold areas.
A frost dragon dressed for ancient Egypt.
Nature has absolutely no respect for thematic consistency.
...Heh.
I bet this thing can do a planche. Haha!
Look at those shoulders. It absolutely can!
That classification is officially recognized by the Dracological Society. Blame them.
Good job, %1$s.
You continue to surprise me day after day.
Truly a fascinating dragon. I've never seen one with that type of body before.
Isn't it just permanently cardio, though?
Two primary limbs, no hind legs, no wings... somehow still built like it expects the mountain to move before it does.
Those arms are doing almost all of the work. Walking, climbing, supporting that entire torso...
I think we can also count the tail, since it's practically a third point of support.
And that tail is definitely not just there for balance.
The tip of its tail is beautiful. I can look at it all day.
dialogue.saintsdragons.ivy.dragon_cinder: Ah, yes... the Cindervane. Pyrovela migrantis. Simply elegant.
They move a lot! And they have breathtaking, burning, cinder-like wing patterns!
So... Pyrovela migrantis!
Which means... 'Wandering Flamewing...?' Which is a mouthful. Yikes.
...Okay, Cindervane makes sense too. Since, like, it flies... and uh, wing patterns, and it's shorter--
MY POINT IS-- %1$s sorry. My point is that the Cindervane is truly an excellent dragon.
Transportation, combat, et cetera.
A long, sleek body with large wings and tail rudders is quite a design for aerial maneuvers.
But don't judge them by how they look.
The suckers pack a really mean punch. Really, REALLY mean.
Some dude I know named Gloth was almost bombed to death by a Cindervane because he thought it was a good idea to lasso it like some horse.
Did you make that up?
The folks just started calling the noodle that way.
Hah! Who did he think he was? Dragon Overlord??
And I know for a fact that they explode when they hit the ground on impact while self-immolating.
Which is... kinda messed up, but dang. Pretty rad.
Good job on taming yours, though.
At least you didn't die, hm?
The name Pyrovela migrantis.
Made what up?
N-No?
No! I mean...
Forget it. Fine. I did make it up because I can.
I mean, come on! It makes sense, no? And it is official!
dialogue.saintsdragons.ivy.dragon_ignivo: It's alright. I forgive you.
No, I'm not going to.
I'm sorry for acting like that. Forgive me? Please?
Great! Let's move on. It's not that serious anyway.
What? What's wrong?
You have got to be kidding me.
ECOLOGICAL RESET BUTTON. GEOLOGICAL HATE CRIME. TERRAIN DELETION EVENT. ACT. OF. GOD--
You get what I mean.
AND THE AUDACITY OF THIS DRAGON OF YOURS.
Why is it so basic-looking? I mean, don't get me wrong. I love the scales and how it generally looks.
And why can it stand up? What kind of crap is that?
It can fly while being that big. It can somehow unleash a wave of heat so scorching hot that it basically vaporizes everything around it.
This thing reminds me an awful lot of another dragon that's even more destructive...
Something about Castle Schrade... eh, whatever. They must be long-lost cousins.
And it belongs to you after a few beatdowns? Great. Fantastic.
What, you jealous?
Congrats. I guess.
Yeah, I do.
An Ignivorus. You have... an Ignivorus.
Yes, you are.
No. I'm not.
I don't believe you.
I'm not!
Alright, fine, you're not jealous.
Nope. Still not believing.
NUH-UH. YOU DO BELIEVE ME.
Okay... so, let me get this straight.
I've spent almost my whole life trying to prove the existence of this dragon to the Dracological Society because it was so rare...
I didn't say it like that...
Just for you to casually go, "Oh yeah, I have a pet Ignivorus."
...Doesn't matter. You're insane. You are actually insane.
You managed to tame a catastrophic event. A walking natural disaster.
Regional extinction event. Mobile evacuation order. Localized apocalypse. Environmental hazard.
...Ugh. I guess I admit that I am.
I'm happy for you, and not at the same time.
Why? Well, because you proved its existence even before me.
And you get to ride it. Experience it and what it is capable of.
But I understand what you went through to even tame that thing. Wholeheartedly.
Fine. I'm leaving. Goodbye. Don't convince me to come back.
...I'm kidding! Haha! You should've seen the look on your face!
It's fine. I loved the back-and-forth.
Let's move on. It's not that serious anyway.
Or maybe you beamed it with a Raevyx... regardless--
dialogue.saintsdragons.ivy.dragon_nullja: If you own it, then you probably know what it can do.
Teleportation, invisibility, and protection from Shulker bullets are some pretty cool stuff.
And they are so peaceful to just look at.
Floating around the barrens with each other. Eating Chorus Fruits and bullying Shulkers.
Not a single care for what's going on around them.
If I was reincarnated and could choose? I would definitely NOT be a Nulljaw.
Why would I say that? I don't know. Randomness.
Anyway, good job on taming one.
dialogue.saintsdragons.ivy.dragon_raevyx: Hah... well, you're like me then.
I did, in fact, tame a Raevyx when she was just a little thunderling.
All baby dragons are gullible and so easy to tame.
Which makes them quite cute and endearing.
Looks like we have something in common.
That is pretty nice in my book.
It seems like you've tamed it when it was still a baby.
Impressive! Looks like my instinct did not let me down, after all.
I thought you'd be atomized by its beam by now.
But that'd be stupid, because you're here.
Glad you're by my side.
I think that your Raevyx is very beautiful.
The words could be pure, serene, and innocent.
Or let's just say that it felt like it was meant for me.
You can also say that I was obsessed with the species itself.
I was pretty young, back then, when I first found the egg.
Oh, and I forgot to mention.
It was next to a dead Raevyx mother.
Mutilated. Killed and butchered for parts.
I didn't think I would discover a Raevyx at all.
Looking at yours, it brings back a lot of memories.
Please take great care of your Raevyx.
The Raevyxian are one of the strongest, smartest, fastest, deadliest and coolest-looking dragons, in my opinion.
I do not doubt you in the slightest whenever it comes to handling dragons.
Hm...
Let's put the matter at rest for now.
I absolutely love the way the spines run alongside the back.
And the wing patterns resembling lightning bolts are truly magnificent.
Forgive the glazing, but it was the first dragon I've ever encountered, you know?
Well, not exactly... more in the form of an egg instead.
The egg was... mesmerising. The red streaks highlighted the darkness around the shell.
When I touched it, I felt... alive? And the egg itself was hatching, too.
Sorry, I don't have the right word to describe how I've truly felt at that moment.
I fought it. And when I knocked it out, I went in for the tame.
I tamed it when it was a baby. I just fed it normally.
How did you manage to tame it, anyway?
dialogue.saintsdragons.ivy.dragon_stegon: Looks like you already have a Binder! Tremendous work, %1$s!
The sooner you make a Binder for it, the better. Trust me.
Oh yes, absolutely. Quite the sturdy friend you got.
But that did not trouble one bit, hm?
Great job. It's beneficial to have this dragon around.
A Stegonaut is an awesome dragon to have.
The base of their neck is really thick and strong. You can sit and add storage on it.
It'll help you with carrying alongside your items if you ever need more room.
I like to think of them as ancient protectors.
Being around them makes me feel safe and secure.
I also think that it's lovely that they travel in packs.
Not many dragons travel in packs like Cindervanes and Stegonauts.
They are also easy to tame. Albeit a bit harder to find since they live in Lush Caves...
dialogue.saintsdragons.ivy.dragon_varasu: Hmm... the Varasuchus. Crocodilian drake thingy.
Why not just... free yourself from the shackles of your owner? It baffles me.
And this goes for all dragons, by the way.
I guess dragons are just... big, scary, powerful... dogs?? Whatever, I'm rambling.
Things we do, %1$s, I'm telling you.
But regardless of everything...
You should be proud of yourself for successfully taming one.
Got thrown from its back and hopped back on. Got thrown again. Repeat until you've tamed it.
Proves you're even more resilient than it is.
What is it?
I also remembered something.
I had a dream about a purple Varasuchus. The dreams felt floaty for some reason.
For a semiaquatic flightless dragon... this thing is terrifying.
The shade of the purple was just glimmering in the endless void. The tranquility of everything.
I once thought I spotted it in the wilds... but I guess I was just seeing things.
Almost as if it was kissed by the void.
Maybe try hatching a Varasuchus's egg in The End. Who knows?
When pushed to its limit, it will stand up on its hind legs and start using its front legs... or arms to fight.
And those arms are equipped with the meanest and sharpest claws I can ever imagine.
You know, I've always wondered...
Who even discovered the way of taming a Varasuchus by just riding it like a horse?
I mean, seriously. Why? How? You don't look at a big and menacing-looking dragon and go, "Yeah, I'm gonna ride it."
Also, pause on that last sentence. But, um... yeah, I am so glad I'm not that person.
And the Varasuchus can for sure take on a human. Why not?? Why become docile after a few buckings?
dialogue.saintsdragons.ivy.dragon_volita: Let's see... biting, horn goring, clawing, water or poison breath. Poison ball. BURROW. BODY SLAM--
And they can fly, they can perfectly be on land, and they can swim...
What is this dragon? Just what on Earth is this?
What made them evolve to just... have these? A kraken? Cthulhu? An even bigger and nastier sea dragon??
They are SCARY. I hate encountering them. I'd steer clear unless I know what I am doing.
And if I have no choice but to tame a Volitans? I'd prepare for the worst. Stock up on everything I can.
At least you can make arrows from the quills that they drop... so that's a win, right?
But hey, look at you, %1$s. You've got it!
Let me tell you something. They are invasive.
One minute, you're underwater, swimming, minding your own business, lalala~
Like, dude, where did you come from?
And they eat dolphins. Isn't that just cute?
What else? Oh, right. Poison. Lots and lots of poison.
And what are the things this dragon can do?
dialogue.saintsdragons.ivy.end_visit.end: Hm... aside from the Endermen and the Ender Dragon? I quite like it here.
With your help, however, we may be able to weaken them.
As we travel through the End Barrens, you'll see what I mean.
As long as you don't look an Enderman in the eyes, you're fine. And after the Ender Dragon has been defeated, there's nothing to worry about.
I get to see the Nulljaws floating around, doing their own thing and minding their own business. I also get to try the 'local' cuisine, most notably Chorus Fruit.
I was teleported near the edge of the barrens when I bit into one! It would've been the end for me, pun intended, had a Nulljaw not saved me because it was attracted to the Chorus Fruit in my hand...
And I've always wondered what would hatch from the Ender Dragon's egg. I think it'd look like a slimmer Ignivorus, don't you?
But... there's one thing I've got to tell you.
Recently, travelers in the End have seen... horrid creatures. Not Nulljaws, of course, but dark, ravenous beasts whose birthing sacks have mysteriously appeared.
Thankfully, they only seem to spawn when approached.
However, their presence is quite concerning. I've only visited the End Barrens a few times, and I don't intend to venture there alone again.
dialogue.saintsdragons.ivy.end_visit.res: Back to what I was saying...
Now, where did I leave off...? Oh, yes.
Right, we were talking about this...
dialogue.saintsdragons.ivy.first_meeting: I'm friendly.
I'm not friendly.
Oh? That's either confidence or a warning. I haven't decided which. So... friendly or not?
I was hoping you'd say that... it's nice to make your acquaintance.
Okaaay... Well, I was hoping you'd not say that...
Tell her your name.
That's a pretty name.
Oleander? Isn't that poisonous?
Never heard that name before.
Well, anyway. My name is Ivy. Ivy Oleander. The last name is kind of uncommon. Rare, even. But yeah, you?
Tell her your name.
Just call me Ivy. Gonna tell me your name?
It's a pleasure meeting you, %1$s. I'm sure we'll get along just fine.
Welp, not much of a pleasure, %1$s. But better than nothing.
What should I call you?
What should I call you?
Tell her your name.
Anyway. What's your name?
Use your Minecraft username.
Choose what Ivy calls you.
What would you like me to call you?
Use your Minecraft username.
Choose what Ivy calls you.
What am I calling you, then?
That's kind of the point, I think. My mother had a thing for unusual things.
Though if you've somehow met another Oleander, I'd be very interested to hear about it.
Most people don't catch that. You're more observant than you look.
...Thank you. Most people just say it sounds like a plant. Which, well. It is. Two of them, actually.
Welcome to my home. Where I live alone and... peaceful.
No, you are not. Why would you think that? Oh, wait, yeah. It'd make sense for you to think so... but no, %1$s, you're not.
ahem
Don't get smart...
Excellent. I have some good stuff you'd like to take a look at.
Woah, what? Your 'wares' wares??
Yes, I'd like to trade with you.
Ah, hey-ho, stranger. Yes. You found her. Would you like to see my wares?
Well, your fault for not specifying!
...E-Excuse me? What--what was that supposed to mean? Was it such a good idea to say that to someone who you did not know?
WHAT?? Wha--you should've... you shouldn't even be thinking about that in the first place!
Ugh...
See? That's so much better!
Yes, show me your wares.
Then? Would you like to trade with me?
Ah, I see. No worries.
Then we'll call it progress.
I'll show you what I have.
That's a fair question. A trader, mostly.
Gardener when the weather cooperates.
And occasionally the person people bother when they need dragon-related advice.
It's a start.
Though I suppose that doesn't really answer your question, does it?
Yes, I'd like to trade with you.
No, I'm good.
With that being said, would you like to trade?
Maybe I'm not most people.
I'm sorry. Am I trespassing?
I was told a trader lived out here.
Who are you exactly?
Oh, hi there. I didn't expect to see anyone here. Most people don't find this place by accident. You must love exploring, hm?
Where was I? Ah, right.
Back to what I was saying...
Now, where did I leave off...? Oh, yes.
Right, we were talking about this...
dialogue.saintsdragons.ivy.known_greetin: Ah, I see you've made up your mind.
I will be able to appear near you. I'll get used to being transported suddenly.
I'll give you an item that will help you, and it is quite important to me. I trust you'll keep it safe.
Whenever I can't get to you, use this, and well, something magical will happen, for lack of a better explanation.
Oh, right! I'm glad you asked, actually. I almost forgot.
You're welcome. Try not lose it, hm? You won't get a second one.
I'll stay here. Please don't die in your adventuring.
Please don't go for too long.
Don't you dare forget about me.
I'll be here eating dirt, then.
I'll be wandering around until you come back.
I'll hanging about until you come back.
Back again? I was starting to think the woods scared you off.
Ah, %1$s! I thought I heard something walking around.
Careful, %1$s. Keep showing up like this and I might think you enjoy my company.
Good to see you again! Try not to let that go to your head.
What do you think of my Raevyx?
Let me know what you think about my Varasuchus.
I'd love to hear your thoughts on my Ignivorus.
Share some of your thoughts on my Volitans?
What do I do if you can't get to me?
What can you tell me about my Nulljaw?
What did you do before all this?
What are your thoughts on the Nether, Ivy?
We're here in the End. What's on your mind?
What do you do out here?
You know a lot about dragons?
You again. Still not friendly, or was that just your opening act?
Well, if it isn't the 'not friendly' person.
Hi, 'friend.' Or maybe you're not friend?
Hello again. Still not trespassing, before you ask.
Oh it's the trespass-- %1$s, I mean, it's %2$s! Hi.
If you're here to make another joke, I reserve the right to charge extra.
What a great first impression you've just left behind...
dialogue.saintsdragons.ivy.known_meeting: Yep. I know. When it comes to dragons, it's not really a walk-in-the-park sort of situation.
I did have help from a guy with the name that has something to do with your diaphragm involuntarily slamming downward super fast.
And he had a really cute black dragon with him. Big green eyes. Almost like a cat. And it moved like one, too.
I've spent a lot of time studying dragons. Especially the Raevyx. But, uh, let's not talk about that.
Point is, dragons are more complicated than people want them to be.
You can say that, sure.
But it's enough to know when someone is about to get killed. Which is, unfortunately, often.
Wrong how?
Sounds complicated.
And it's enough to know people are usually wrong about them.
No, for most of the time.
No, for most of the time.
But dangerous? Yes. Always.
But dangerous? Yes. Always.
But monster is a word people use when they don't want to understand what they're afraid of.
But monster is a word people use when they don't want to understand what they're afraid of.
Except for... the damn %1$s. Eugh. Steer clear from those weird freaks.
Volitans
Except for... the damn %1$s. Eugh. Steer clear from those weird freaks.
Volitans
They are extremely lethal and sneaky despite their appearances. I almost got jumped by one when I was looking for a trident underwater...
They are extremely lethal and sneaky despite their appearances. I almost got jumped by one when I was looking for a trident underwater...
And I was lucky enough to gather a lot of spines for arrows when they shed.
And I was lucky enough to gather a lot of spines for arrows when they shed.
Ah, right. A strange young chief. Clever. Awkward in a way that somehow worked for him.
It was close. Almost a tie, actually.
Almost... I think he won. I don't know.
I would've liked to win, but... it was fun. Anyway, yeah, that's it. We exchanged goodbyes and that was that.
I couldn't help but notice the prosthetic first time I met him.
I didn't ask too many questions. Some are better remembered as stories.
He had a black dragon with him. Big green eyes. Aerodynamic wings. Sleek body. Truly beautiful.
Moved like a cat. Looked at people like it knew exactly how stupid they were.
That dragon wasn't young. Not old either. But it carried itself like something that had survived more than a few bad ideas. I wish I had known its name.
But then the rider claimed his dragon was the fastest thing in the sky.
Which was rude, because my Raevyx was right there.
So we raced.
Some are territorial. Some are curious. Some are clever enough to pretend they aren't.
Some are territorial. Some are curious. Some are clever enough to pretend they aren't.
So dragons aren't just monsters?
And some... well. Some are best admired from a very safe distance and left alone.
So dragons aren't just monsters?
And some... well. Some are best admired from a very safe distance and left alone.
I could talk about dragons for hours, but that would be rude. Probably.
I could talk about dragons for hours, but that would be rude. Probably.
Anyway. That's probably more dragon talk than you asked for. I hope you weren't overwhelmed.
That rider you mentioned... who was he?
That's all for now.
Anyway. That's probably more dragon talk than you asked for. I hope you weren't overwhelmed.
Most people talk about dragons like they're all the same. Big wings, sharp teeth, bad temper. Blah, blah, blah.
That's like saying every person with a sword is a knight.
Or like, if a cat suddenly makes barking-like sounds, it's a dog. Does that make sense? No? %1$s, anyway.
Ahem
Where was I? Ah, right.
Back to what I was saying...
Now, where did I leave off...? Oh, yes.
Right, we were talking about this...
Well... not really. Expert is a dangerous word.
Sometimes I think, 'Wouldn't it be easier to look for an egg and raise one from the start?'
But even that takes patience. And fish. An unreasonable amount of fish.
Anyway.
I know enough to stay humble. That's more than most experts can say.
The moment someone says they understand dragons completely, I start looking for the nearest exit.
Or a shovel.
Depends how confident they sound.
People hear it and start assuming you know everything. I don't.
Villagers often ask me how to tame certain types of dragons. I teach them the proper methods, make sure they're prepared, and send them off with enough knowledge and equipment to not die immediately.
A lot of the time, they still fail miserably.
Not because they're stupid. Well... not always.
Most just don't have the patience, caution, or nerve to deal with a wild dragon.
And then some ask me how to tame a Raevyx while looking like a tumbleweed with pockets.
Like, come on. You look like that and want to tame THE GRIM REAPER?! They can barely tame a Cindervane!
Ahem. Sorry. I didn't mean to yell.
Mhm. Gardening.
Plants are easier to negotiate with. Usually.
I grow herbs, roots, flowers, a few things that are useful for medicine...
...and a few things that are useful when medicine is no longer the plan.
Relax. I label the dangerous ones. Most of the time.
Where was I? Ah, right.
Back to what I was saying...
Now, where did I leave off...? Oh, yes.
Right, we were talking about this...
Oh, you have no idea. People, especially the villagers, have grown quite fond of some dragon species.
Don't even dare throw one at me, though. I'll hate you forever...
So yes. People do ridiculous things with dragons.
Sometimes the dragons do ridiculous things back.
There was a villager I knew named Nimriel who was bucked off a juvenile Varasuchus while trying to ride it, and apparently, he broke his hip after hitting the ground.
And then someone fell off from a Cindervane, but luckily, they fell into a forest with dense trees.
Hah! Trees are still trees. Unlucky individual.
And then ME, specifically. Have you even heard of a Mossback?? Actually, here's a better one: why does that thing exist?!
I accidentally dropped one because it was slippery, and I got hit with a foul and overwhelming stench that blinded and POISONED me!
The audacity of those things. To have wings and cannot fly while being fat, and stinky?! Ugh...
I had to wait it out. I was sweating the whole time like a sinner in a church pew while I was at it...
After the effects had worn off, it ran away, the little prick... funny thing is, they don't even react when you pick them up. And you can throw them.
People do ridiculous things with dragons?
Gardening?
So you're a dragon expert?
That's all I need to know.
Anything else?
People do ridiculous things with dragons?
Gardening?
So you're a dragon expert?
That's all I need to know.
A little trading, a little gardening, and a little making sure people don't do something ridiculous with dragons.
Gotcha.
I can't even think because it's too hot...
The point is, the Nether is weird, which circles back to it having its own charm, I think. And I only came along because you're with me. Otherwise, I'd never look twice at it.
I'm sweating a lot right now... Let's just hurry up with whatever you're trying to do and get out of this place, please?
I've gone into the Nether a few times to look for Netherite and smaller things like Glowstone Dust and Nether Wart... but I failed on the Netherite part.
Simply because I can't stand the heat or some of the denizens here.
I kind of like the biomes, especially the Crimson Forest. It reminds me of the color of my dragon...
Also, I absolutely hate the Piglins. I almost got jumped because I forgot to wear my gold helmet.
Don't get me started on the Ghasts. Why do they make those weird sounds? How can they float? Why do they look so creepy? I didn't do anything to them, and I still got a fireball shot at me?!
Striders are just weird old men with toothpicks for legs, standing in a lake of lava.
I tried luring one onto land and dragging it back to the Overworld, but seeing it shiver out of the lava made me pity it.
And Wither Skeletons and Blazes? Absolutely not. Bunch of freaks...
Back to what I was saying...
Now, where did I leave off...? Oh, yes.
Right, we were talking about this...
dialogue.saintsdragons.ivy.quest_cinderv: You... You already tamed one?
Well... That certainly makes this easier! I suppose I do not need to explain the dangerous part anymore.
Cindervanes are migrating this season, and that tends to make people reckless.
How do I tame a Cindervane?
No way. I'm out.
I want you to tame one. Properly, that is. Just to test your mettle.
Good. Come back once you've tamed one.
...Very well. I understand why you are hesitant.
And honestly, that's one of the more reasonable answers I've heard.
We'll revisit the matter later, if you want to, of course.
Very well. I'll explain again. It's good to be thorough.
I suggest you look for food items like cod, salmon, or raw chicken. Or everything. They are not picky when hungry.
If you want better odds, trade with me for fish and eggs. I can make you Hearty Dragon Meals.
Once you have the food, look for Cindervanes in mountainous biomes, like Stony Peaks, Jagged Peaks, Frozen Peaks, Snowy Slopes, Groves, and even Meadows.
...And potentially other high-altitude areas from other 'biome mods' or whatever that means.
Once you've found one, just approach it, and tame it like how you would tame a dog or a cat.
Do NOT hit it. Please. If you've somehow made it mad, then it's best to run away, or chug a Fire Resistance Potion, or worse... kill it.
When you've tamed one, come back to me, then we'll see where things go.
Can you go over it one more time?
Crystal clear.
I already tamed a Cindervane.
Is everything clear?
...Didn't I tell you not to hit it?
Well, I'm still glad you didn't die. Good job.
Are you sure? Very well. Here to a bountiful future.
You did? And you came back with all your limbs intact and not dead?
That's already better than most!
I followed your advice.
It wasn't that hard.
It tried to burn me a little.
How did it go?
That's good! I do take pride in my advice sometimes.
Especially when dragons are involved.
I don't want to. What are you gonna do about it?
%1$s I was just kidding! You should've seen the look on your face...
Pfft--
Well... I didn't say that. But yes. I want to.
I'll come with you.
...Something the matter? It's alright. Take your time.
You can do it. I'll be rooting for you.
Now go and get your first dragon.
Ah-ah. Careful now.
Dragons hear arrogance better than commands. But I suppose you are right. Cindervanes are quite straightforward to deal with.
But... regardless, you did succeed. So, good job.
What?
Just promise me one thing.
Hah! Get a load of this... You're humble. I like it.
Come on, that Cindervane is child's play for someone like you.
A little. But don't let it inflate your head, ok?
You haven't seen what others can do. But if you had, then well, I hereby take everything back.
But yes. You handled that well.
Can you go over it one more time?
I haven't done it yet.
I did it. I've tamed a Cindervane.
Yes? Have you encountered any trouble?
Treat your dragons well.
I've been thinking... staying here has its comforts, you know?
Quiet mornings. Familiar paths. Fewer things trying to bite me. No Mossbacks...
But problems involving dragons rarely come knocking politely at my door.
Come with me, then.
Only if you want to.
I could use your help.
If I travel with you, maybe I can stop a few before they become tragedies. And... sightsee more. And dragonwatching. And... I'm gonna stop myself from rambling.
Let's get going, %1$s.
Of course. It's better to ask twice than rush in unsure.
So, did I prove myself?
What now?
You sound surprised.
Most people want dragons to obey. You let one choose. And that matters a lot to me. More than people think.
Well, I'm not, actually. I already know you can handle yourself pretty well.
I am. Not because I thought you'd fail. But because I've seen plenty of confident people fail loudly.
Yes. And I could use yours.
Mm... now? Maybe having a companion like you wouldn't be a bad idea at all.
Now? Now I decide whether following you is brave, useful, or a terrible lapse in judgment. But it's possibly all three.
dialogue.saintsdragons.ivy.recruited_fav: Both.
Hmm... that depends. You mean favorite as in what I actually eat, or favorite as in what I wish I was eating?
I’d go absolutely feral for Beef Wellington.
Or duck confit.
That is a significant jump from baked potato.
Maybe steak au poivre with mushroom risotto on the side.
I contain multitudes.
And I’d wash all of that down with... black coffee.
I KNOW. I know. Don’t... don’t even judge me.
I just love black coffee.
Together?
And 2% milk.
...No. Seperately.
As in what I actually eat? Bread, dried meat, berries, whatever keeps well and doesn’t fill me up too much.
Exciting, I know.
What I would wish for, though... has to be a proper meal.
Hot, filling, difficult to ruin. Usually.
Baked potato, rabbit if I can get it, some bread, maybe carrots.
That specific?
Pumpkin pie afterward.
I think about food a lot when I’m traveling.
But if we’re talking properly good food?
dialogue.saintsdragons.ivy.recruited_gre: Glad to have you with me.
dialogue.saintsdragons.ivy.recruited_pas: Yeah.
Before the trading?
I found a Varasuchus roost once, though. No sign of the dragon itself.
Which was weird. I was so excited to finally see one.
I saw Cindervanes a lot back then too.
It was nice watching them fly together at first. Then it got a little... ordinary.
Anyway. Back to what I actually did.
That last one sounds useful.
I liked figuring out what lived where. What grew where. What could kill me where.
Yes. Extremely useful. Usually learned slightly too late, but useful.
I also like to do things for myself.
I just liked seeing new places. Finding things I’d only ever read about.
So, were you a researcher?
Dragons especially.
I mostly wandered around and made questionable decisions in places I probably shouldn’t have been.
Mm... no. Well, unofficially, at least.
“Curious woman with a notebook” would probably be more accurate.
The Dracological Society has people with actual qualifications.
Sounds qualified enough.
I have dirt under my fingernails and several very confident opinions.
Please never say that around an academic.
Exploring, gathering plants, collecting samples, sketching things, taking notes.
I was fascinated by dragons too.
But for the longest time, all I ever found were Mossbacks.
And... those aren't even dragons. Right?
I never cared enough to look into them properly.
Some people say you can eat them.
Give me a break. Leave me out of that.
dialogue.saintsdragons.ivy.recruited_tra: No. I used to travel mostly on my own.
That's just... not it.
So you just became a merchant?
At least they'll give you emeralds for normal things first.
More or less, yeah.
...That sounded suspicious.
It also gives me a reason to move between settlements without attracting too much attention.
Did it? Don't think too much about that.
Exploring, gathering, taking notes... that sort of thing.
Why?
Trading came later, though.
Well, besides trading dragon parts for eggs, I sell other things too.
Food costs. Equipment costs. Repairs cost. Everything costs.
And apparently people will pay quite a lot for things I was already carrying around anyway.
Most of my regular trading is with villagers, so naturally that means emeralds.
Why emeralds? No idea.
You're telling me I have to climb the highest mountain imaginable to find some, just so I can trade for a bucket of cod?
Sometimes I do, yeah.
Built me quite a bit of stamina.
I recommend the exercise. Not the wildlife.
I don’t do that recreationally.
That sounds a little antisocial.
Besides, trading gives me an excuse to meet people without actually having to stay around them for very long.
...No? I thought it sounded efficient.
Anyway, you get better at this sort of thing with experience.
You learn a lot about people from what they’re willing to trade for.
Some need food. Some need tools. Some desperately need three stacks of rotten flesh for reasons I refuse to question.
Who knows? Maybe word will get around about my honeyed words and terrifying negotiating skills.
I like finding things people actually need.
Or just helping people, generally. Putting a smile on someone’s face.
Food, materials, tools, supplies... that part feels useful.
I enjoy the occasional conversation too. The exchange itself can be nice.
Haggling, though? No.
Really? You seem pretty good at it.
I hate haggling.
Hah! Being good at something does not mean I enjoy it.
I’m also good at running from angry wildlife.
dialogue.saintsdragons.ivy.recruited_vis: Hello to you too. Take care.
I already have a travelling companion. But I can still trade with you.
I am spoken for, in the companion sense. The shop is still open, though.
Sorry. My companion and I travel together. That does not mean I have stopped being a trader.
There's little I can say to you, I'm afraid. We can still trade.
Sorry. There's only so much of me to go around. We can still trade.
You seem nice and all, but I've teamed up with someone else. We can still trade, though.

effect.monsterexpansion.bleeding.guidebo: Makes you take damage over time. This effect can stack, making the damage interval shorter. On its own, the damage isn't anything to be afraid of, but it can be devastating if its allowed to stack up. This status' duration will go down slower depending on how fast you are moving. To get rid of it the fastest, the hunter must crouch while staying still.
Makes you unable to move nor attack for a short duration. This status is very common and can be inflicted by most monsters' roars. However as common as it is, the monsters also do not attack when roaring, making the status not as dangerous. As the effect will likely end before the monster can finish roaring.
effect.monsterexpansion.flarevein.guideb: Makes you take damage over time. This effect can stack, making the damage interval shorter. On its own, the damage isn't anything to be afraid of, but it can be devastating if its allowed to stack up. This status' duration will go down slower depending on how slow you are moving. To get rid of it the fastest, the hunter must be sprinting, or even better, roll around until the status is cured. The hunter must be careful as to not stay still, as doing so will increase the duration instead.
effect.monsterexpansion.frostvein.guideb: Makes you move slower, attack slower and jump lower. This effect can stack, making the movement speed decrease more severe. This effect can really be devastating if its allowed to stack up as you may not be able to jump over even a singular block. This status currently does not have a remedy making it incredibly dangerous if the hunter is fighting in rough terrain.
effect.monsterexpansion.stunned.guideboo: Makes you unable to move nor attack for a short duration. This can be inflicted by all monsters if the hunter is often hit by attacks. The effect instantly ends if the hunter is hit again. The damage source does not matter, making allies and self-inflicted damage a viable way to end the effect early. However this effect is still very dangerous as the monster may follow up with a devastating attack before the hunter can recover.

Interesting... I’ve not seen one like this before!
You understand the value of true rarity. I appreciate that!
The ocean thanks you, as do I!
The sea has its secrets… this may be one of them!
Every item has a story. I’ll make sure this one is remembered!
I don’t do business when the sun is up. Wait for the night!
The morning is for peace, not trading. Return when the stars shine!
Let me enjoy the waves... Come back at night!
Not now. The tide is all I need this morning!
Find me when the night falls, not under the sun!
entity.traveloptics.dialogue.fading_mage: The Nightwarden's suffering hath ended, freed at last by thy hand... Thou mayest now walk the path to "Act II - Saelune"
entity.traveloptics.fading_mage.f1.dialo: I began to learn. Alone. In silence.
I tried to prove it could come back.
Magic had cost. But so did silence!
What was taken cannot be replaced.
But maybe... someone else can find what I couldn’t...
Not because magic faded… but because they were told it had.
A world run by metal and logic leaves no room for dreams.
They laughed when I said magic was still here.
Some truths aren’t forgotten... they’re buried.
entity.traveloptics.fading_mage.f2.dialo: The story was clean.
Someone offered them something. And apparently that... was enough!
I kept thinking that part.
They had something to do. Something... involving Saelune
And I was in the way.
So they gave me a direction to run...
And I ran
...toward NOTHING.
While I chased the thing they invented, something was being done to her.
That time, I didn't know what -
Too clean...
Only that they needed me gone to do it.
Now I have had a long time down here to be sure of it...
"Something from the End. Wanted magic gone. Took her."
Every witness. The same words.
The EXACT same words.
A hoax...
Built carefully— Given to the people I trusted.
And they handed it to me without blinking.

Debug Sandevistan Frame Hitches

Disabled by default. For frames exceeding the threshold, logs afterimage counts and CPU timings for afterimages, mask preparation, player masks, afterimage masks, and post-processing. Supported GPUs also provide asynchronous timings for afterimages, masks, and post-processing. framesAgo identifies the age of each GPU sample; n/a means unavailable, not zero cost. Timing never waits for the GPU. Logs are limited to once every 0.5 seconds; disable after testing.
Sandevistan Hitch Log Threshold (ms)

epic_parcool_momentum.configuration.fast: FastRun edge-blur samples

Controls the number of blur samples used for the FastRun screen edge. The default is 6. Higher values produce smoother trails but add full-screen shader texture reads. When FastRun and Sandevistan overlap, only one shared post-processing pass runs and uses the higher sample requirement.
FastRun edge-motion blur strength

Controls the radial texture-sampling distance at the screen edge during FastRun. Higher values create longer edge trails. The default 0.03 keeps the image readable because the stronger speed feedback now comes from FOV and radial stretching.
Collapses the detailed FastRun camera speed-effect settings to reduce configuration-screen clutter.
Expands the detailed FastRun camera speed-effect settings. The master toggle and current parameter values are not changed.
FastRun edge-effect full position
Sets where the FastRun stretch and blur reach full strength near the screen edge. This should be greater than the start position. The default 0.90 gives the outer screen a stronger sense of motion.
FastRun edge-effect start

Sets where the effect begins when moving outward from the screen center, using a rectangular screen radius where 0 is near the center and 1 is near the edge. The default 0.42 lets the speed effect cover a wider peripheral area; lower values cover more of the screen.
FastRun camera speed effect

Enables the complete local FastRun camera-speed effect: additional camera FOV, center-out radial stretching, sparse white procedural speed lines, edge stretching and light motion blur. Minecraft's normal speed-based FOV remains active, and EPM adds its value afterward. Disabling this option removes every FastRun camera effect.
FastRun camera-effect fade-in ticks

Client ticks used for the edge effect to reach its target strength after FastRun begins and movement speed rises. The default is 2 ticks for an immediate acceleration response; higher values transition more gently.
FastRun camera-effect fade-out ticks

Client ticks used for the edge effect to disappear after leaving FastRun, hitting an obstacle, or losing horizontal speed. The default is 6 ticks to retain momentum without leaving a long visual tail.
FastRun extra FOV degrees

Sets the base additional camera FOV while FastRun is moving. At full movement intensity it reaches a sustained 140% of this value, so the default 10 degrees produces up to 14 degrees. The FOV uses a separately filtered sustained-movement speed: extreme startup-step impulses are limited before smoothing, while genuine movement slowdown still makes the FOV fall gradually. When FastRun ends, it fades out using the configured fade-out ticks. Fixed or scoped camera FOV states remain unchanged.
FastRun center-out radial stretch

Controls a center-preserving FOV-like texture stretch. The screen center remains stable, while displacement increases nonlinearly toward every border. The default is 0.08. It now follows only sustained FastRun movement intensity and no longer receives the startup pulse. This runs inside the existing shared post-processing pass and adds no extra texture samples.
FastRun sustained edge-stretch strength

Controls sustained outward screen-edge stretching while FastRun is moving. It does not change camera FOV or actual player speed. Excessive values can create strong image distortion, so a subtle value is recommended.
FastRun dynamic blur inward expansion

Controls how far the FastRun blur region expands inward toward the screen center at maximum dynamic speed. The default 0.16 changes the default blur transition from 0.42-0.90 to approximately 0.26-0.74. A higher value affects more of the central image.
FastRun dynamic blur strength multiplier

Sets the maximum multiplier applied to FastRun radial motion-blur strength as movement speed rises. The default 2.00 increases the configured blur strength from 0.03 to at most 0.06. Blur sample count is not increased, so this does not add texture samples.
FastRun dynamic effect full-speed multiplier

Sets the effective movement-speed multiplier where FastRun dynamic effects reach maximum strength, relative to normal FastRun. The default 2.00 means the extra blur and speed-line acceleration reach their maximum at approximately twice the normal FastRun movement speed. The calculation uses the movement-speed attribute and ParCool's configured FastRun modifier, so startup dashes, knockback and falling do not create false spikes.
FastRun dynamic speed-line acceleration

Sets the maximum multiplier applied to procedural speed-line travel speed. The normal FastRun fastest layer remains the configured 5.00. With the default multiplier 1.25, sufficiently high sustained speed increases the fastest layer smoothly up to 6.25; slower layers remain proportionally below it.
FastRun speed-line center clearance

Keeps an aspect-corrected circular area around the crosshair free of speed lines. The default is 0.68 followed by a soft transition, moving the first visible rays farther toward the screen border. The clear area remains circular at widescreen resolutions instead of becoming rectangular.
FastRun speed-line density

Controls how many angular sectors receive a generated speed line. The default 0.38 produces a relatively sparse look similar to the reference video. Higher values fill more directions but can make the image busy and reduce target visibility.
FastRun speed-line opacity

Controls the final opacity of all FastRun speed-line layers. The default is 0.80. The value is multiplied by filtered FastRun movement intensity, so slowing down naturally makes the lines less visible and leaving FastRun uses the existing fade-out transition.
FastRun speed-line length

Controls the base radial length of generated speed-line segments. The reference contains many rays extending from the central clear area almost to the border, so the default is 0.46. Individual lines still vary, while the three layers generate long bright lines, medium lines and faint short lines.
FastRun speed-line outer fade start
Sets where speed lines begin fading as they approach the screen border. The default 0.98 allows lines to nearly reach the edge like the reference footage. Lower values create a softer outer boundary.
FastRun speed-line travel speed

Controls how quickly generated line segments travel from the protected screen center toward the border. The default is 5.00 and now represents the fastest procedural layer. The other two layers use 52% and 76% of this value, preserving unsynchronized motion without exceeding the configured speed.
FastRun procedural speed lines

Enables sparse white radial speed lines generated directly by the existing FastRun Shader. No video decoder, frame sequence or additional full-screen pass is used. The lines follow the separately filtered sustained-movement intensity, so the startup-step impulse does not instantly maximize them.
FastRun startup step animation
true: allows one startup step when entering FastRun. false: entering FastRun never plays a startup step.

true: when Vault starts from FastRun, releases ParCool's Vault action at 6 ticks and keeps a short FastRun grace window so close obstacles can chain through ParCool's original Vault detection. false: keeps ParCool's original Vault action timing and disables this mod's FastRun Vault chaining assist.

epic_parcool_momentum.configuration.sand: Enable Activation White Flash
Produces a short full-screen white exposure flash when the Sandevistan activation distortion reaches its peak, then rapidly fades instead of remaining for the skill duration.
Activation White Flash Strength
Controls the maximum amount of white exposure mixed into the screen. The default is 0.72 for a strong reference-like flash; lower values preserve more scene detail, while 1.0 approaches pure white.
Sandevistan Afterimage Opacity
Initial opacity of textured Sandevistan afterimages.
Collapses the detailed Sandevistan afterimage settings without changing the master toggle or current values.
Expands the detailed Sandevistan afterimage settings, including local and remote limits, lifetime, spawn distance, and stationary-action afterimages.
Sandevistan Fading Afterimage Color

Lifetime in ticks of each Sandevistan afterimage.

Maximum number of Sandevistan afterimages retained for the local player.
Sandevistan Middle Afterimage Color
Sandevistan Afterimage Minimum Distance
Minimum movement distance in blocks before another afterimage can be captured.
Sandevistan New Afterimage Color
Enable Activation Chromatic Aberration

Separates the red and blue channels radially during the Sandevistan activation pulse, recreating the high-speed impact seen in the reference video. It only runs during the distortion pulse; disabling it saves two texture reads.
Activation Chromatic Aberration Strength

Controls the maximum sampling offset between the red and blue channels. The default is 0.012, keeping the center stable while producing visible edge fringing. Excessive values create strong colored ghosting.
Collapses the detailed Sandevistan edge-blur settings without changing the blur toggle or current values.
Expands the detailed Sandevistan edge-blur settings, including overall intensity, trail length, sample count, and blur-region positions.
Enable Sandevistan Edge Blur

Applies a radial speed blur around the world view while Sandevistan is active. HUD elements, text, and the first-person hand remain sharp. Disabling this option stops the post-processing shader from running.
Edge Blur Full-Strength Position

Controls where blur reaches full strength. The current default is 0.80. 0 represents the screen center and 1 represents the border. This should normally be greater than Edge Blur Start Position; lower values reach full strength sooner.
Edge Blur Overall Intensity
Controls the overall amount of edge blur. 0.0 makes it invisible and 1.0 uses the full effect. Adjust this when you want weaker blur without changing the area covered by it.
Edge Blur Sample Count
Controls how many additional texture reads are used for each pixel. The current default is 10. Higher values look smoother but require more GPU work; lower-end GPUs can reduce this to 4–6.
Edge Blur Start Position
Controls where blur begins. The current default is 0.60. 0 represents the screen center and 1 represents the border; higher values restrict blur to a thinner outer edge.
Edge Blur Trail Length

Controls how far each sample moves toward the screen center, which determines the length of the speed-blur trails. The current default is 0.30. Values from 0.05–0.10 are moderate, 0.15–0.30 create a strong high-speed effect, 0.30–0.45 approach Awaken's grappling-hook impact, and 0.45–0.60 are extreme and may visibly stretch the screen edges.
Collapses the detailed Sandevistan activation-distortion settings without changing the distortion toggle or current values.
Expands the detailed Sandevistan activation-distortion settings, including stretch strength, duration, rise time, and affected-region positions.
Activation Distortion Duration Ticks

Controls the total time from the beginning of one activation distortion pulse until it fully disappears. The default is 12 ticks, or about 0.6 seconds. This does not change the duration of the Sandevistan skill itself.
Enable Sandevistan Activation Distortion

Applies a radial screen-edge stretch when Sandevistan activates, then automatically fades it into the normal sustained edge blur. This reuses the existing post-processing pass and does not affect the time-dilation simulation.
Activation Distortion Full-Strength Position

Controls where the activation distortion reaches full strength. The current default is 0.60. This should normally be greater than Activation Distortion Start Position; lower values reach maximum stretch sooner.
Activation Distortion Rise Ticks

Controls how many ticks the activation distortion takes to rise from zero to full strength. The current default is 5 ticks, allowing the stretch to build over a short interval. Setting this to 0 reaches the peak immediately; the effective rise time is limited by the total duration.
Activation Distortion Start Position
Controls where the activation distortion begins. The default is 0.45. 0 represents the screen center and 1 represents the border; higher values preserve a larger undistorted center area.
Activation Distortion Stretch Strength

Controls the maximum outward stretch of the screen edges during activation. The current default is 0.20, producing a clearly visible camera impact. Values from 0.05–0.12 are gentler, 0.12–0.22 approach the strong stretch in the reference video, and higher values may excessively magnify the edges.
Enable Sandevistan
Enables the Sandevistan time-dilation skill.
Sandevistan Filter Color
Collapses the detailed Sandevistan green-filter settings without changing the filter toggle or current values.
Expands the detailed Sandevistan green-filter settings, including filter strength and fade timing.
Enable Sandevistan Green Filter
Enables the low-cost green Sandevistan screen filter.
Sandevistan Filter Fade-In Ticks
Ticks used to fade in the Sandevistan screen filter.
Sandevistan Filter Fade-Out Ticks
Ticks used to fade out the Sandevistan screen filter.
Sandevistan Green Filter Intensity
Strength of the green Sandevistan screen filter.
Sandevistan Remote Afterimage Limit
Maximum number of Sandevistan afterimages retained for each remote player.
Stationary Action Afterimage Opacity
Starting opacity of stationary action afterimages. The default is 0.85, then it smoothly decreases toward the independently configured end opacity over the stationary action lifetime.
Stationary Action Afterimage Color
Constant hexadecimal RGB color used throughout the lifetime of stationary action afterimages. The default is cyan-blue #33E6FF. They do not use the moving trail cyan, purple, and orange gradient.
Stationary Action Afterimage Display Delay

How many client ticks to wait after capturing a stationary attack or action pose before displaying its afterimage. The default is 2 ticks, approximately 0.1 seconds. The delay uses a fixed client-tick counter and is independent of frame rate. Setting it to 0 displays the afterimage during the next render stage after capture.
Stationary Action Afterimage End Opacity

Target opacity reached at the end of a stationary action afterimage's lifetime. The default is 0.45. With a 15-tick lifetime, a fixed nonlinear curve fades slowly at first and accelerates later, reaching 0.45 on tick 15.
Stationary Action Afterimage Interval

How many ticks pass between pose captures while the player performs an Epic Fight attack or action without moving. The default is 2 ticks. Lower values produce a smoother attack trail but increase the number of visible afterimages and rendering cost. Ordinary idle standing does not create afterimages.
Stationary Action Afterimage Lifetime
How many ticks each stationary Epic Fight action afterimage remains visible. The default is 15 ticks and is completely independent from the moving trail lifetime.

A core that Chesed draws its power from. 

Can be applied to any weapon in crafting table. 

When attacking entities with a weapon that is enhanced with Lightning Core there is a chance to struck the target with Chesed lightning that will do a percentage of weapons damage while inflicting {{(fdbosses:effect)id=fdbosses:shocked}}.

Shock:
{{(fdlib:image)path=fdbosses:boss_damage}}: {{(fdbosses:config_float) config=effectConfig, value=shockDamageReductionPercent}}% outgoing damage reduction.
{{(fdlib:image)path=fdbosses:boss_duration}}: {{(fdbosses:config_float) config=itemConfig, value=lightningStrikeShockDuration}} ticks.

Lightning: 
{{(fdlib:image)path=fdbosses:boss_damage}}: {{(fdbosses:config_float) config=itemConfig, value=lightningStrikeDamagePercent}}% of weapon damage.

Summon chance:  {{(fdbosses:config_float) config=itemConfig, value=chanceToSummonLightningStrike}}%

Can be used to phase through the blocks at high speed.

§cWarning!§r

Mobs will still be able to damage you, you are immune only to suffocating in blocks.

Phasing duration:
{{(fdlib:image)path=fdbosses:boss_duration}}: {{(fdbosses:config_float) config=itemConfig, value=phaseSphereUseDuration}} ticks.

Geburah's Core.

Can be applied to any armor in crafting table.

Gives players a buff: Incoming damage is reduced and is capped at the amount of the last damage taken (after all resistances).

Not stackable.

Damage reduction:

fdbosses.boss_drop.fdbosses.malkuth.fdbo:
The core of Malkuth.

Can be attached to any item that has damage to be able to summon Malkuth fireballs.

Use an item to release a fireball that will deal a percentage of item damage and ignite the targets.

Crouch while using an item to release an iceball that will slow the targets instead.

Damage:
{{(fdlib:image)path=fdbosses:boss_damage}}: {{(fdbosses:config_float) config=itemConfig, value=playerMalkuthFireballToolDamagePercent}}% of tool damage.

Item ability cooldown:

§6In right hand:§r

Acts as grappling hook for blocks. Casts Malkuths crush attack at grapple position.
If used on ground while facing downwards propels the user up into the air.

§6In left hand:§r

Acts as a grappling hook for entities. Makes user automatically attack the target, then knocks user back from the target.

§6Combo:§r

Using an item in the left hand and then moving it back to the right hand resets its cooldown.

Crush Damage:

fdbosses.bosses.description.chesed:
A creature born out of rocks corroded by sculk. Wields enormous magic power.

§cRecommended weapon type: {{(fdlib:item)item=minecraft:diamond_axe}}
fdbosses.bosses.description.geburah:
{{(fdlib:item)item=minecraft:bow}} §cRanged weapon is recommended!§r

Every human is born in sin, hence, the judges are needed. To be a judge is to bear an unwavering sense of justice, the one that our hero had. But, like sins of people, hero's life was also fading away. The people needed him, so the hero devoted himself to eternal justice and thus Geburah was born. And so the people lived happily in the world without sin for many many years.
As centuries passed and generations changed, more and more people started complaining: “Was it really a good idea to make sinful being – an eternal judge?”
As years passed less and less people were complaining, until no one was left to complain.
fdbosses.bosses.description.malkuth:
The Qliphoth of Malkuth. Benevolent King who ruled over a once-prosperous land, whose blind, excessive generosity became his kingdoms demise.

§5Devs Note: Its better to fight him at night.§r
fdbosses.core_ability.fire_and_ice_core: Can be combined with items that has damage. Allows summoning Malkuth fireballs on item use.
fdbosses.core_ability.justice_core: Can be combined with equippable items. Incoming damage amount cannot exceed the last damage amount you have received. Decreases incoming damage by %s%%.
fdbosses.core_ability.lightning_core: Can be combined with items that has damage. Gives an ability to summon Chesed lightnings on hit.
fdbosses.skills.chesed.blocks_descriptio: Tears out blocks from the earth and hurls them onto target.
fdbosses.skills.chesed.crystals_descript:
Casts this ability before the lightning ray attack.

Destroys all crystals and then summons 1 crystal on each side of the battlefield.

If a crystal is destroyed by a player, that player becomes {{(fdbosses:effect)id=fdbosses:chesed_energized,level=1}}.
fdbosses.skills.chesed.earthquake_descri:
Slams the earth emitting a shockwave and lightnings that travel out from Chesed position.

During second phase more lightnings are summoned and their movement speed is increased.
fdbosses.skills.chesed.electrified_air_d: Air above Chesed crackles with power. Entities that interact with it are damaged.
fdbosses.skills.chesed.electrified_air_s:
Air: 
{{(fdlib:image)path=fdbosses:boss_damage}}: {{(fdbosses:config_float) config=chesedConfig, value=electrifiedAirCurrentHealthDamagePercent}}% current HP.

Instantly kills affected entity if HP is lower than  {{(fdbosses:config_float) config=chesedConfig, value=electrifiedAirInstadeathHP}}.
fdbosses.skills.chesed.espheres_descript:
Releases ball lightnings that travel out from Chesed.

These ball lightnings cannot be reflected.
fdbosses.skills.chesed.final_description:
Drains power from monoliths and then unleashes a lightning strike that damage everyone on the battlefield. 

Amount of damage depends on how many monoliths are in an active state. 

While Chesed casts this ability, monoliths are invulnerable. 

Deactivated monoliths become active again after this ability ends.
fdbosses.skills.chesed.final_stats:
Attack: 
{{(fdlib:image)path=fdbosses:boss_damage}}: {{(fdbosses:config_float) config=chesedConfig, value=finalAttackDamagePercentPerMonolith}}% Max HP per active monolith.
fdbosses.skills.chesed.kinetic_field_des:
Uses this attack only on second phase.

Traps players in a kinetic field that doesn't allow them to escape.

Periodically summons lightnings in all kinetic fields.
fdbosses.skills.chesed.lightning_ray_des:
Casts Crystals ability before this ability and then begins to fire lightning rays with tremendous power at target. 

Lightning ray deals 0 damage to targets affected by {{(fdbosses:effect)id=fdbosses:chesed_energized}}.

If a target is a charged ray reflector Chesed takes 1 damage.

During second phase the frequency of attacks is increased.

§lTip!§r

While charging the attack, Chesed tries to aim slightly beyond the target movement and stops aiming moments before releasing the lightning ray.
fdbosses.skills.chesed.mightiness_descri:
Chesed cannot be hurt directly and its arena cannot be easily escaped from.

All damage inflicted by Chesed cannot be lowered by any resistances.

Gives all combatants {{(fdbosses:effect)id=minecraft:night_vision}} while alive.

If a player looks away from Chesed, that player is inflicted with {{(fdbosses:effect)id=fdbosses:chesed_gaze}}.

Chesed proceeds to second phase when hp drop below 50%.
fdbosses.skills.chesed.monoliths_descrip:
Spawns 4 monoliths when summoned. 

Monoliths deactivate upon death and cannot be damaged anymore.

Monoliths gain additional {{(fdbosses:config_float) config=chesedConfig, value=additionalSecondPhaseMonolithHP}} HP on second phase.
fdbosses.skills.chesed.rockfall_descript:
Fires lightning beam at the ceiling causing it to crumble while summoning lightnings around combatants. 

During second phase amount and frequency of lightnings are increased.
fdbosses.skills.chesed.roll_description:
Rolls around the arena damaging and pushing away everyone who step in its way. 

During second phase leaves a fire trail behind.
fdbosses.skills.geburah.birds_of_justice:
Summons 4 Judgement Birds on the battlefield. When a bird is killed, Geburah will respawn it after a certain time.

Judgement birds have an ability to cast laser beams to attack combatants.

Each bird has an area where it detects its targets, if no targets are found within the area, the bird flies back to its home point.
fdbosses.skills.geburah.divine_judgement:
Ignites two flames on the scales and starts charging a powerful move.

Summons bells around the arena, each bell, when hit, displaces the corresponding scale plate and disappears. §aBells can be hit with ranged weapons.§r

If the scales are balanced attack is §acanceled.§r If the scales are not balanced, Geburah §claunches the attack.§r

Each combatant on the arena is damaged for the percentage of their current hp, accumulate 3 sins and have all their positive effects removed.

Current HP damage percent: 
{{(fdlib:image)path=fdbosses:boss_damage}}: {{(fdbosses:config_float) config=geburahConfig, value=ultimateMoveHealthPercentage}}%
fdbosses.skills.geburah.earthquake_descr:
Stomps the ground with a special mechanism, releasing a shockwave.

The techniques of divine architecture allows Geburah to withstand its own earthquakes.
fdbosses.skills.geburah.justice_hammer_d: Summons a magic justice hammer that strikes the ground after a small delay.
fdbosses.skills.geburah.laser_beam_descr:
Geburah rotates its cannons around, predicting the combatants motion, releasing a powerful laser beam thereafter.

§oYour chest feels tight.
fdbosses.skills.geburah.ray_description: Geburah charges an attack and fires a devastating ray from its core at target.
fdbosses.skills.geburah.round_and_round_: Emits constantly active lasers from its cannons, rotating them around with slow speed.
fdbosses.skills.geburah.roundstrike_desc: Geburah rotates cannons randomly and shoots projectiles.
fdbosses.skills.geburah.sin_crystal_of_s:
When this sin is active Geburah casts projectiles that put Crystals of Sin in combatants inventory that explode after a certain time.

If a Crystal of Sin explodes in the inventory - a sin is accumulated.
fdbosses.skills.geburah.sin_jumping_sin_: When this sin is active jumping is considered a sin.
fdbosses.skills.geburah.sin_kill_entity_: When this sin is active killing any entity is considered a sin. Since Geburah is not-so-fair judge, killing combatants doesn't count.
fdbosses.skills.geburah.sin_move_clockwi:
When this sin is active, moving §earound§r §eGeburah§r in the §copposite§r direction of arrows is considered a sin.

§oOh, round and round we go-
fdbosses.skills.geburah.sin_pressed_too_:
When this sin is active performing more than 5 actions is considered a sin.

§oActions are any button press. Pressing and holding the buttons is allowed.
fdbosses.skills.geburah.sin_stay_still_s: When this sin is active, standing still is forbidden for humans.
fdbosses.skills.geburah.traps_descriptio: Geburah randomly throws around immobilizing traps. When an entity steps on or flies above it - the trap §ccatches the entity§r and disallows it to move for certain time.
fdbosses.skills.malkuth.arcslash_descrip:
Damage type: §cFire§r / §bIce§r

Malkuth charges up his swords and releases aerial slashes in arcs, covering the whole arena.
fdbosses.skills.malkuth.armor_descriptio: Malkuth wields impenetrable armor, capable of neglecting any damage.
fdbosses.skills.malkuth.cannons_descript:
Damage type: §cFire§r / §bIce§r

Malkuth jumps on the wall behind him and orders his cannons to fire devastating shots at the target.

When this ability is cast, combatants cannons can be used once again, unless they are broken.

§lSecond phase:§r

When second phase starts Malkuth orders his cannons to break cannons on combatants side.
fdbosses.skills.malkuth.chainpunch_descr:
Damage type: §7Basic§r

Malkuth pulls every combatant, who were in the air, and punches them with overwhelming force.
fdbosses.skills.malkuth.earthshatter_des:
Damage type: §7Basic§r

Malkuth leaps to the target and crushes the earth, hurling everyone who were caught in the attack into the air.

During the second phase, if there are broken cannons on the combatants side, spawns a special crystal at the attack location that is capable of repairing cannons.
fdbosses.skills.malkuth.fair_duel_descri:
Combatants can use two cannons on their side to fight on equal ground with Malkuth.

Right click a cannon to fire a shot.

Combatants can only use the cannon of type they are currently weak to.

After firing a shot, cannon becomes unusable until the next use of Cannonade ability.
fdbosses.skills.malkuth.fire_and_ice_des:
While on an arena combatants may be weak to §cFire§r or §bIce§r.

Current damage type you are weak to can be seen on the crosshair.

Malkuth abilities deal three types of damage:

1: §7Basic§r - regular damage type.

2: §cFire§r - makes targets weaker to §cFire§r damage, deals reduced damage to targets that are weak to §bIce§r.

3: §bIce§r - makes targets weaker to §bIce§r damage, deals reduced damage to targets that are weak to §cFire§r.

§lExample:§r

If target that is weak to §cFire§r receives §bIce§r damage, its amount is reduced and that target becomes weaker to §cFire§r.

If target that is weak to §cFire§r receives §cFire§r damage, its amount is not reduced and target becomes weaker to §cFire§r.
fdbosses.skills.malkuth.hellshaper_descr:
Damage type: §cFire§r / §bIce§r

Malkuth slams the earth, summoning floating islands, hurling everyone in the air and rendering the floor impossible to walk on.

Launches fireballs at these islands thereafter.
fdbosses.skills.malkuth.impaling_doom_de:
Damage type: §cFire§r / §bIce§r

Malkuth slams the earth, releasing either a §cFire§r or §bIce§r spikes that travel in the slam direction.

When colliding with combatants those spikes hurl them up into the air.
fdbosses.skills.malkuth.knights_duty_des:
During the bossfight all combatants receive {{(fdbosses:effect)id=fdbosses:knight}} .

When combatant escapes the arena before the fight ended {{(fdbosses:effect)id=fdbosses:knight}} transforms into {{(fdbosses:effect)id=fdbosses:coward}} .

Lava field is not a part of the arena!

When a combatant with {{(fdbosses:effect)id=fdbosses:coward}} steps into arena once again, it changes back to {{(fdbosses:effect)id=fdbosses:knight}}.

§oCowardness is not allowed! Death penalty!§r
fdbosses.skills.malkuth.side_rocks_descr:
Damage type: §cFire§r / §bIce§r

Malkuth tears up boulders from the earth, imbuing them with his magic and hurls them onto player.
fdbosses.skills.malkuth.slash_descriptio:
Damage type: §cFire§r / §bIce§r

Charges one if his swords and releases an aerial slash traveling towards the target.

The damage type of the slash is based on the sword that was charged.

This slash is capable of slicing through crystals.
fdbosses.skills.malkuth.tsars_wrath_desc:
Damage type: §cFire§r / §bIce§r

Malkuth summons two giant swords and orders them to slam the ground with devastating force.

§lSecond phase:§r

Also fires his cannons before the attack lands.
fdbosses.skills.malkuth.tsars_wrath_stat:
Sword:
{{(fdlib:image)path=fdbosses:boss_damage}}: Infinite

This attacks damage can be fully negated, despite the damage reduction value.
fdbosses.skills.sinner.sinner_descriptio:
Every combatant on the arena becomes a {{(fdbosses:effect)id=fdbosses:sinner}}.

Geburah declares §9sinful§r §9actions§r each time an attack pattern changes. When a §ecombatant§r or a §estructure§r commits a sin, their sin counter increases. Commiting too much sins result in §cimmediate death.§r

Current sinful actions are displayed at Geburah's screens.

Running from the battlefield or flying is always considered a sin.
fdbosses.tldr.chesed:
Chesed damage pierces armor and shields.

To damage Chesed:

Wait until lightning ray attack, kill a crystal with an axe to get {{(fdbosses:effect)id=fdbosses:chesed_energized,level=1}}, run to a ray reflector and make Chesed hit it. You are immune to lightning ray attack when you are {{(fdbosses:effect)id=fdbosses:chesed_energized}}.

Chesed has an attack which damage depends on the amount of active monoliths, if all monoliths are active - there is no way to survive the attack. To deactivate a monolith - kill it.
fdbosses.tldr.geburah:
Each combatant on the arena becomes a {{(fdbosses:effect)id=fdbosses:sinner}}. When attack pattern changes Geburah marks certain actions as sinful, committing too many sins causes immediate death.

Current sins are displayed at Geburah's screens.

§lGeburah is capable of commiting sins too.§r
fdbosses.tldr.malkuth:
Cannot be attacked directly.

When player is weak to §cFire§r it receives decreased §bIce§r damage, and other way around if player is weak to §bIce§r, it receives decreased §cFire§r damage.

Current weakness can be seen on the crosshair.

Use cannons on the arena to attack Malkuth, you can only use the cannon of type you are currently weak to.

gui.traveloptics.computer.system_hack.ru: The slots at the bottom right. Every code you pick gets stored here in the order you picked it. Space is limited. If the Buffer fills up and you still have sequences left, the hack fails.
The grid on the left. Every code you can pick is sitting in it. Click on a code and it gets shelved into your Buffer. The timer only starts running on your first pick.
Marked with a clock icon. It enters the Buffer like any normal code, but picking it instantly burns 10% off your remaining timer.

You start locked to the top row, so you can only pick from there. Once you pick a code, you get locked to that code's column instead. Then a row again, then a column, alternating with each pick. Only the highlighted line is selectable.
Marked with a signal icon. It never enters your Buffer, costing zero space. Use it as a free jump onto an intersecting row or column when the current line has no valid picks.

The code chains you need to land inside your Buffer, in the exact order shown. You need to clear all of them. They can share codes, so a single good pick can advance two chains at once. If a pick breaks a chain, it resets to find a new starting point. When every chain is done, hit COMPLETE to lock it in.
