gui.xaero_box_category_include_list_incl: Automatically include all entities from this list, and other lists included in this category, in the super-category/parent of this category, except the entities in the exclude list. That way you don't have to manually add duplicates on each level.

Automatically include all elements from this list, and other sub-lists included in this category, in the super-category/parent of this category. That way you don't have to manually add duplicates on each level. Keep in mind that super-categories are not going to check the exclusion lists of this category.
gui.xaero_box_category_list_add:
Supports player names, entity/item identifiers or patterns with special characters * ) ( and |. 
 
 * - matches anything. 
 )( - parenthesis, mostly for usage with |. 
 | - the OR operator to match different sequences in the same location. 
 
 For example: 
 minecraft:creeper 
 minecraft:zombie(_villager|_horse) - zombie villagers and horses. 
 minecraft:a*l - any vanilla entity which starts with 'a' and ends with 'l'.
gui.xaero_box_category_protection: Category protection prevents you from (accidentally) deleting, moving, renaming a category or changing its "Hard Include" setting.
gui.xaero_box_cave_maps: Mapping mode that can go deeper than the surface blocks, mainly to display underground caves and interiors of buildings. The ceiling size refers to the size of a horizontal "square" of solid blocks that has to be detected above you to activate the cave mode.
gui.xaero_box_cave_maps2: Mapping mode that can go deeper than the surface blocks, mainly to display underground caves and interiors of buildings. The ceiling size refers to the size of a square ceiling of solid blocks that has to be detected above you to activate the cave mode. The solid blocks don't have to be on the same Y level.
gui.xaero_box_cave_mode_allowed: Mapping mode that can go deeper than the surface blocks, mainly to display underground caves and interiors of buildings. Cave mode is usually enabled automatically (see "Auto Cave Mode"), but can also be toggled manually with a key binding (see "Manual Cave Mode Start Y").
gui.xaero_box_cave_mode_allowed_dimensio: A list of dimension IDs, separated by comas, where cave mode should work. If the list is empty (just []), cave mode works in every dimension.
gui.xaero_box_cave_mode_toggle_timer: The minimum time to wait between toggles of cave mode to prevent flickering when quickly switching between being under blocks and not. The latest world map mod has a separate setting for this as well.
gui.xaero_box_cave_zoom: Specifies, how much to zoom the minimap further in when the cave mode is active.
gui.xaero_box_claims_pac_required: The chunk claim feature requires the Open Parties and Claims mod!
gui.xaero_box_closing_menu_when_hopping: Closing the menu when hopping to a waypoint (left-clicking in the menu)
gui.xaero_box_compass: The cardinal directions displayed on the minimap.
gui.xaero_box_compass_color: The color of the background/shadow under the cardinal directions displayed on the minimap.
gui.xaero_box_compass_over_everything: Render the cardinal direction letters (N, E, S, W) above all map elements, as opposed to under some, e.g. waypoints.
gui.xaero_box_compass_over_wp2: Render compass letters (N, E, S, W) over the on-map waypoints. This only works for the on-frame compass location.
gui.xaero_box_compass_scale: The scale of the compass letters NESW when using the on-map compass location.
gui.xaero_box_compass_scale2: The scale of the cardinal direction letters NESW. For the "Auto" option, go all the way to the left.
gui.xaero_box_controls:
Controls 
 
 Click and drag to scroll the map. 
 Scroll the mouse wheel to zoom in and out (CTRL for precise). 
 Right-click the map for some useful shortcuts. 
 Hold right-click and drag the mouse to select an area for an action (e.g claiming). 
 Some UI buttons have additional key bindings displayed in their tooltip. 
 
 Right-click a map element (e.g. waypoint) for options. 
 %1$sClick here to edit the key bindings.
gui.xaero_box_controls_minimap:
§2%s§r to create a new waypoint. 
 §2%s§r to create a quick temporary waypoint. 
 §2%s§r to switch the waypoint set. 
 §2%s§r to toggle rendering all waypoint sets. 
 §2%s§r to open the full waypoint menu.
gui.xaero_box_controls_pac: §2%s§r to open the Parties and Claims menu.
gui.xaero_box_current_profile: Your currently used client config profile.
gui.xaero_box_default_enforced_profile: The ID of the server config profile the values of which are enforced for players by default.
gui.xaero_box_delete_reached_deathpoints: Automatically delete deathpoints when you are within 4 blocks from them. This requires the deathpoint to be visible in world or on the minimap. A deathpoint is protected from deletion for 5 seconds after its creation.
gui.xaero_box_dimension_scaled_max_waypo: Scale the maximum waypoint render distance by the current dimension's coordinate scale (e.g. 1/8 in the Nether).
gui.xaero_box_discovered_waystone_waypoi: Automatically display discovered waystones (from the mods Waystones and Wraith Waystones) as waypoints. In Wraith Waystones, only activated ones are considered discovered.
gui.xaero_box_distance: Specifies, for which in-world waypoints to show the distance to.
gui.xaero_box_distance2: Specifies, for which in-world waypoints to show the distance to. This does not guarantee that it will be shown for multiple waypoints at once. Check out the "Multiple Waypoint Distances" setting as well.
gui.xaero_box_enlarged_minimap_a_toggle: Treat the "Enlarge Minimap" key binding as a toggle instead of having to hold it.
gui.xaero_box_entity_amount: The limit per each entity category.
gui.xaero_box_entity_depth: Display entities darker on the minimap depending on their Y level relative to you.
gui.xaero_box_entity_radar_categories: Configure specific entity categories, which are usually players, hostile mobs, friendly mobs, items or other entities, separately instead of having the same configuration for every entity. You can even create your own custom categories for specific entity types.
gui.xaero_box_entity_radar_icons:
Render entity icons instead of colored dots. 
 
 Option "Player List" - render only when the "List Players" key binding (TAB by default) is pressed.
gui.xaero_box_entity_radar_names:
Render entity names under the dots or icons/heads. 
 
 Option "Player List" - render only when the "List Players" key binding (TAB by default) is pressed.
gui.xaero_box_export: Export the map as a PNG file
gui.xaero_box_export_option_full: Export the whole map even if you've made a map selection.
gui.xaero_box_export_option_highlights: Export the map with all currently enabled highlights (e.g. claims) applied to the map. When exporting the full map, highlights very far from your discovered map won't be included.
gui.xaero_box_export_option_multiple_ima: Export the map as multiple unscaled images no matter how big it is. This does not have the same memory limitations as a single image.
gui.xaero_box_export_option_nighttime: Export the map with nighttime lighting. This doesn't affect cave mode maps.
gui.xaero_box_export_option_scale_down_s:
The size, in regions, of a square image equivalent to the resolution that a large exported map will be scaled down to if necessary. For example, 20x20 stands for 400 regions, 512x512 blocks/pixels each. The resulting image doesn't have to be a square. 10x40 is also 400 regions. 
 
 Your computer or the Java heap size might not be able to handle higher export resolutions.
gui.xaero_box_full_reload: Reload all regions on the map without having to manually view them. The reloading process will work in the background and turn off when it's done. It is important to note that going to another dimension will pause it until you come back and changing maps will fully cancel it.
gui.xaero_box_full_resave: Reload and resave all regions on the map without having to manually visit them. World save maps will be converted into normal map data saved to a separate map instance "Converted World Save", stored in the folder "cm$converted", which can be transferred to multiplayer map instances for the same world, using file manager. The reloading process will work in the background and turn off when it's done. It is important to note that going to another dimension will pause it until you come back and changing maps will fully cancel it.
gui.xaero_box_further_zoomout:
Experimental! 
 Not enabled by default due to potentially bad performance but will be in the future after some optimization.
gui.xaero_box_height_limit: Maximum Y-level distance for entities until they are no longer displayed on the minimap.
gui.xaero_box_hide_minimap_under_f3: Hide the minimap when the F3 debug screen is enabled.
gui.xaero_box_hide_minimap_under_screen: Hide the minimap when a GUI screen is open, e.g. the inventory, with the exception of minimap-related screens and the chat screen.
gui.xaero_box_ignore_enforcement_if_edit: Whether you should ignore config values normally enforced by the server, if you have the server profile editing permission (e.g. you are an operator). The enforcement for the value of this option ("Ignore Enforced As Editor") can't be ignored though, allowing server owners to disable this feature if they want to, making it a bit more difficult for cheaters to circumvent server enforcement.
gui.xaero_box_ignore_heightmaps: Some servers put custom values in the world heightmaps, which may result in incorrectly rendered maps. Sometimes it may even happen in heavily modded singleplayer worlds. This option should fix such issues at the expense of a bit of performance. Do not use unless you have to. Reenter the world after toggling this option! Stored per world/server, not part of the config profile.
gui.xaero_box_info_display_background_op: The opacity of the colored backgrounds of information types that have a background enabled in the info display manager.
gui.xaero_box_ingame_waypoint_close_scal: Scale of the waypoints in world when you are very close to them. To change the scale of waypoints that are far away, use the "In-World Waypoint Icon Scale", "Waypoint Distance Text Scale" and "Waypoint Name Text Scale" settings.
gui.xaero_box_ingame_waypoint_icon_scale: Scale of the waypoint icons in world.
gui.xaero_box_keep_enlarged_minimap_unlo: Do not lock the minimap to north when enlarged if possible, which is only when using the circle shape at the time of writing this.
gui.xaero_box_legible_cave_maps: Use depth-based lighting in cave mode instead of actual block lighting, making it easier to mentally separate the different cave layers.
gui.xaero_box_light_overlay_type: Using this overlay can negatively affect the game performance because it currently does not use the World Map mod chunks and increases the minimap updating frequency. Do not keep it active all the time.
gui.xaero_box_load_chunks: Add new chunks to the non-world-save maps (multiplayer).
gui.xaero_box_manual_cave_mode_start: Which Y level to start mapping blocks from when the manual cave mode is enabled. Manual cave mode can be toggled with a key binding. For the "Auto" option, go all the way to the left.
gui.xaero_box_map_distances: Display distances to the positions or elements on the map that you right click. For positions, the distance displayed is 2-dimensional. For elements, such as waypoints and tracked players, it is 3-dimensional where applicable.
gui.xaero_box_map_item: The ID of an item required in the hotbar for the fullscreen world map to function. Set it to "-" to have no item requirement.
gui.xaero_box_map_writing_distance: The maximum X and Z distance in chunks at which chunks can be loaded or updated on a non-world-save map. For the "Unlimited" option, go all the way to the left. World save maps always generate within your render distance
gui.xaero_box_minimap_frame_color: The color of the minimap frame for the non-default colored frame styles.
gui.xaero_box_minimap_info_display_manag: Configure and/or rearrange different types of info displayed under the minimap, such as current coordinates, facing angles, dimension, biome, weather, light level, game time, real time and more.
gui.xaero_box_minimap_item: The ID of an item required in the hotbar for the minimap and waypoints to function. Set it to "-" to have no item requirement.
gui.xaero_box_minimap_radar: %s Minimap entity radar is displayed (requires Xaero's Minimap)
gui.xaero_box_minimap_size:
Size of the minimap frame that affects how much is visible. Square-shaped minimap is forced into the non-rotating mode (option "Lock Minimap North") when the size is greater than 180. 
 
 For the "Auto" option, go all the way to the left. 
 
 Size values in older mod versions: 
 Tiny - 57 
 Small - 85 
 Medium - 113 
 Large - 169
gui.xaero_box_minimap_undiscovered_opaci: The opacity of the black undiscovered areas on the map, relative to the main opacity setting.
gui.xaero_box_multiple_waypoint_info: Whether the distance can be displayed for multiple waypoints in world at once. By default, only the distance to the closest waypoint to the crosshair is displayed. Use the "Distance to WP" setting to configure which waypoints the distance could even be shown for.
gui.xaero_box_no_minimap_radar: %s Minimap entity radar is not displayed
gui.xaero_box_north_compass_color: The color of the background/shadow under the north cardinal direction displayed on the minimap.
gui.xaero_box_not_closing_menu_when_hopp: Not closing the menu when hopping to a waypoint (left-clicking in the menu)
gui.xaero_box_only_current_map_waypoints: Displaying only the waypoints bound to the current world map, even if another waypoint sub-world is selected for the minimap using the full waypoint menu.
gui.xaero_box_other_waystone_waypoints: Automatically display other types of waystones (from the mods Waystones and Wraith Waystones) as waypoints. If supported (1.20.4+), this includes sharestones in the original Waystones mod. In Wraith Waystones, this includes unactivated global waystones.
gui.xaero_box_pac_claims: Display chunk claims from the Open Parties and Claims mod as a colored overlay.
gui.xaero_box_pac_claims_border_opacity: The opacity of the chunk claims overlay border color. Chunk claims require the Open Parties and Claims mod.
gui.xaero_box_pac_claims_fill_opacity: The opacity of the chunk claims overlay fill color. Chunk claims require the Open Parties and Claims mod.
gui.xaero_box_pac_current_claim: Display claim information about the chunk that you are in. Chunk claims require the Open Parties and Claims mod.
gui.xaero_box_partial_y_teleportation: When teleporting to a waypoint, offset the Y coordinate by 0.5 to avoid falling through carpet-like blocks into the void. Otherwise, the integer Y coordinate is used.
gui.xaero_box_players_pac_required: The party player menu feature requires the Open Parties and Claims mod!
gui.xaero_box_pushbox_boss_health:
An invisible box around the vanilla boss health display that pushes the mod's interfaces out of the way. 
 
 Normal type's collision box is equal to its size and only pushes interfaces by the necessary distance. 
 
 Screen Height type's collision box is stretched across the whole screen height and always shifts colliding interfaces vertically by the Normal type's height. This can be very useful when you have multiple interfaces in a column and want all of them to be pushed.
gui.xaero_box_pushbox_potion_effects:
An invisible box around the vanilla potion effects display that pushes the mod's interfaces out of the way. 
 
 Normal type's collision box is equal to its size and only pushes interfaces by the necessary distance. 
 
 Screen Height type's collision box is stretched across the whole screen height and always shifts colliding interfaces vertically by the Normal type's height. This can be very useful when you have multiple interfaces in a column and want all of them to be pushed.
gui.xaero_box_radar_render_order: Controls the order in which the radar categories are rendered. A lower number means being rendered earlier. However, in the newer Minecraft versions dots are always rendered on top of the icons. The order still applies within dot or icon rendering though.
gui.xaero_box_radar_render_over_minimap:
Render the entities over the minimap frame instead of rendering them inside the frame. Entities rendered this way act similarly to the waypoints and stick to the border when out of bounds. Visible entities are still limited to the ones loaded on the game client side though. 
 
 Option "Player List" - render over minimap only when the "List Players" key binding (TAB by default) is pressed.
gui.xaero_box_reload_viewed_regions: Reload every region that is displayed on your screen once.
gui.xaero_box_rendering_waypoints_server: The world map waypoint rendering setting is enforced by the server!
gui.xaero_box_showing_third_party_delete: Show third-party waypoints that you have "deleted", e.g. waystone waypoints.
gui.xaero_box_start_fading_at: Minimum Y level difference requirement for an entity to start darkening on the radar when the "Show Entity Depth" setting is enabled.
gui.xaero_box_switch_to_auto_on_death: Whether to switch the waypoint sub-world to auto on deathpoint creation. This doesn't affect what sub-world the deathpoint is created in.
gui.xaero_box_teleport_default_command: The command used for waypoint teleportation if a world-specific or a server-specific command is not set in the Options menu in the waypoint screen.
gui.xaero_box_teleport_default_command_r: The command used for waypoint teleportation with rotation if a world-specific or a server-specific command is not set in the Options menu in the waypoint screen.
gui.xaero_box_temp_waypoints_global: When enabled, temporary waypoints are treated as global waypoints and ignore the waypoint render distance limits.
gui.xaero_box_tracked_player_minimap_ico: Scale of the tracked player icons on the minimap.
gui.xaero_box_tracked_player_world_icon_: Scale of the tracked player icons in world.
gui.xaero_box_tracked_player_world_name_: Scale of the text displaying the name of a tracked player in world.
gui.xaero_box_tracked_players: Display players whose locations are shared with you in one way or another (usually your party) when they are out of the minimap frame bounds or not visible for another reason.
gui.xaero_box_tracked_players_in_world: Display markers in the world for players whose locations are shared with you in one way or another (usually your party). The "common" config has an option "everyoneTracksEveryone" that enables tracking of every player.
gui.xaero_box_tracked_players_on_map: Display markers on the minimap for players whose locations are shared with you in one way or another (usually your party) when they are out of the minimap frame bounds or not visible for another reason. The "common" config has an option "everyoneTracksEveryone" that enables tracking of every player.
gui.xaero_box_ui_scale: Scale of text and other minimap UI elements. Not made for zooming in or resizing. There are separate options for that.
gui.xaero_box_update_chunks: Update chunks on the non-world-save maps (multiplayer).
gui.xaero_box_visibility_type:
In-World/Minimap Visibility Type 
 
 Local - only visible when in the maximum waypoint render distance 
 Global - always visible 
 World Map Loc. - not visible but is considered local 
 World Map Glo. - not visible but is considered global
gui.xaero_box_waypoint_type:
Enabled - regular waypoint 
 Disabled - regular hidden waypoint 
 Temporary - waypoint disappears on world exit 
 Destination - waypoint disappears when reached
gui.xaero_box_waypoints_bottom: Put newly created waypoints at the bottom of the waypoint list instead of the default top.
gui.xaero_box_waypoints_clamp_depth:
The screen depth at which in-world waypoints stop getting smaller when you go further away from them. 
 Use this if you want to make waypoints that are far away bigger/smaller on the screen. Use the "Waypoint In-World Scale" setting to also affect the size of waypoints when you are close to them. 
 
 For the "Auto" option, go all the way to the left. 
 The automatic option attempts to give you the best value for the default values of scale types, taking your FOV and screen height into account. 
 
 Default values in older mod versions: 
 Clamp Depth: 12 
 In-World Scale: 2.5 
 Name Text Scale: 0.5 
 Distance Text Scale: 0.8
gui.xaero_box_waypoints_disabled: Waypoints are disabled in the world map settings!
gui.xaero_box_waypoints_distance: Maximum render distance for local waypoints. Global waypoints are not affected.
gui.xaero_box_waypoints_distance2: Maximum render distance for local waypoints. Global waypoints are not affected. By default, the maximum distance is scaled by the current dimension's coordinate scale. You can toggle this with "Dimension-scaled Max WP Distance".
gui.xaero_box_waypoints_distance_scale:
Scale of the text displaying the distance to a waypoint in world. 
 
 Default values in older mod versions: 
 Clamp Depth: 12 
 In-World Scale: 2.5 
 Name Text Scale: 0.5 
 Distance Text Scale: 0.8
gui.xaero_box_waypoints_distance_scale2: Scale of the text displaying the distance to a waypoint in world.
gui.xaero_box_waypoints_minimap_required: The waypoint feature requires the Xaero's Minimap mod!
gui.xaero_box_waypoints_name_scale:
Scale of the text displaying the name of a waypoint in world. 
 
 Default values in older mod versions: 
 Clamp Depth: 12 
 In-World Scale: 2.5 
 Name Text Scale: 0.5 
 Distance Text Scale: 0.8
gui.xaero_box_waypoints_name_scale2: Scale of the text displaying the name of a waypoint in world.
gui.xaero_box_waypoints_scale:
Scale of waypoints in world. Use this to change the scale of all waypoints in world, including those that are near you. Use the "Clamp Depth" setting to specifically affect the size of waypoints that are far away. 
 
 Default values in older mod versions: 
 Clamp Depth: 12 
 In-World Scale: 2.5 
 Name Text Scale: 0.5 
 Distance Text Scale: 0.8
gui.xaero_box_waypoints_selected_by_mini: Displaying waypoints from the same waypoint sub-world as you are viewing in game and on the minimap. The sub-world can be switched in the full waypoint menu.
gui.xaero_category_disable_protection_co: Disable protection for the following category?
gui.xaero_category_enable_protection_con: Enable protection for the following category?
gui.xaero_category_help2:
Select a sub-category and go to its Settings to configure things like dot color, names, icons etc. 
 
 Sub-categories that are higher on the list are prioritized when multiple sub-categories include the same entity! Keep that in mind when creating custom categories. Usually, a new custom category should be placed at the top.
gui.xaero_category_settings_reset_confir: Reset the category configuration to default values?
Custom categories will be removed and the default ones will be reset.

gui.xaero_make_multi_automatic_msg2: This will swap all waypoint data between the selected sub-world and the auto one, thus simulate making the selected sub-world automatic. Make sure you know what you are doing.
gui.xaero_map_selection_box:
Manual - you are asked to select and confirm the world map every time you switch worlds or dimensions. 
 
 World Spawn - the world map is selected and confirmed automatically based on the world spawn point that the game client is aware of. Can break if the server is using the vanilla compass item for a custom function. 
 
 Single - each dimension has a single world map that is automatically confirmed. Useful for simple servers with a single world. 
 
 Server - install the world map mod on the server side to use this automatic mode.
gui.xaero_minimap_info_display_manager_h: Click and drag the elements to change the order of the displayed information.
gui.xaero_minimap_redirect_item: Disabled because you're missing the configured required item in your hotbar: %1$s!
gui.xaero_mm_box_auto_cave_mode: Enable cave mode automatically based on what's above you. The ceiling size refers to the size of a square ceiling of solid blocks that has to be detected above you to activate the cave mode. The solid blocks don't have to be on the same Y level.

If you are sure that this sub-world is from the same sub-server/world save as the auto one, then you can enable teleportation by adding a connection in the waypoint screen -> Options -> Add Sub-World Connection. But beware, if you connect unrelated sub-worlds and teleport, then there is a good chance you will suffocate in a block or die from fall damage, so be careful and connect only the right ones.

gui.xaero_uses_worldmap_hard_value: Setting value cannot be configured when using the world map chunks!
gui.xaero_uses_worldmap_screen_value: Setting value is taken from the world map screen!
gui.xaero_uses_worldmap_value: Setting value is taken from the world map settings!
gui.xaero_visit_needed: §eYou need to visit this dimension first to convert it to the new format!
gui.xaero_wm_box_adjust_height_for_carpe: Subtract 1 from the height value for short carpetlike blocks, e.g. carpet, 1-layer snow, lilypad etc. This prevents such blocks from causing harsh shading on the map like a full block. Waypoints and teleportation over these blocks should make more sense too.
gui.xaero_wm_box_arrow_color: Color of the arrow that indicates the position and the rotation of the player.
gui.xaero_wm_box_biome_blending: Smooth out biome color edges by sampling biome colors for multiple blocks for every block on the map. Turning this off can significantly improve performance when biome color calculation is modded to be much more heavyweight than vanilla.
gui.xaero_wm_box_cave_mode_allowed: Cave mode on the full screen world map. It's a mapping mode that can go deeper than the surface blocks, mainly to display underground caves and interiors of buildings. Cave mode is usually enabled automatically (see "Auto Cave Mode"), but can also be enabled manually on the world map screen.
gui.xaero_wm_box_cave_mode_allowed_dimen: A list of dimension IDs, separated by comas, where cave mode should work on the full screen world map. If the list is empty (just []), cave mode works in every dimension.
gui.xaero_wm_box_cave_mode_toggle_timer: The minimum time to wait between toggles of cave mode to prevent flickering when quickly switching between being under blocks and not. This only applies when "Auto Cave Mode" isn't redirecting to the minimap mod. The latest minimap mod has a separate setting for this as well.
gui.xaero_wm_box_cave_mode_type:
The cave mode type to use when cave mode is enabled. 
 
 OFF - display above ground even when cave mode is automatically or manually enabled (same as old world map versions without cave mode) 
 Layered - separate cave maps into multiple layers depending on the used top Y 
 Full - ignore the used top Y, use a single layer for cave maps and map everything from the world top to the world bottom
gui.xaero_wm_box_default_cave_mode_type: The default cave mode type assigned to dimensions visited for the first time in a world/server. You can read more about cave mode types by clicking the cave mode icon on the map screen.
gui.xaero_wm_box_detect_ambiguous_y: A single pixel on the map can contain multiple transparent layers and an opaque block under them. In older non-cache map data files, only the Y level (height) of the opaque block is stored in such cases, which often makes it unsafe to blindly teleport to the stored Y coordinate. When this setting is ON, the mod treats such map pixels as it would undiscovered chunks. It defaults to 2D waypoints and disables direct teleportation to such pixels. Disable this at your own risk!
gui.xaero_wm_box_display_minimap_radar: Display minimap radar on the fullscreen map. Only works when the Xaero's Minimap mod is installed.
gui.xaero_wm_box_display_server_chunk_ra: Display a square overlay on the world map around your character corresponding to the server chunk radius (server render distance).
gui.xaero_wm_box_force_fast_map_writing: Bad for performance but good for mapping out servers at very high movement speeds.
gui.xaero_wm_box_ignore_heightmaps: Some servers put custom values in the world heightmaps, which can cause incorrectly rendered maps. Sometimes it can even happen in heavily modded singleplayer worlds. This option should fix such issues at the expense of a bit of performance. Do not use unless you need to. Reenter the world after toggling the option! Stored per world/server, not part of the config profile.
gui.xaero_wm_box_ignore_map_file_locks: Proceed with using a map instance even if it is already being used by another process. This will cause region loading failures. Do not use this unless you know what you're doing. Relog after turning this on.
gui.xaero_wm_box_legible_cave_maps: Use depth-based lighting in cave mode instead of actual block lighting, making it easier to mentally separate the different cave layers.
gui.xaero_wm_box_map_teleport_command: The chat commands used on this world/server to teleport you to positions on the map. Stored per world/server, not part of the config profile.
gui.xaero_wm_box_max_loaded_regions: The approximate maximum number of 512x512 map regions to keep loaded, including "branch" regions rendered at lower (further) zoom levels. Other factors can increase/decrease the actual effective limit. A higher number improves performance but uses more RAM and VRAM which you can run out of.
gui.xaero_wm_box_pac_claims: Display chunk claims from the Open Parties and Claims mod as a colored overlay.
gui.xaero_wm_box_pac_claims_border_opaci: The opacity of the chunk claims overlay border color. Chunk claims require the Open Parties and Claims mod.
gui.xaero_wm_box_pac_claims_fill_opacity: The opacity of the chunk claims overlay fill color. Chunk claims require the Open Parties and Claims mod.
gui.xaero_wm_box_pac_player_teleport_com: The chat command used on this world/server to teleport you to other players on the map when Open Parties and Claims is installed.
gui.xaero_wm_box_partial_y_teleportation: When teleporting to a map location, offset the Y coordinate by 0.5 to avoid falling through carpet-like blocks into the void. Otherwise, the integer Y coordinate is used.
gui.xaero_wm_box_player_teleport_command: The chat command used on this world/server to teleport you to tracked players on the map (not regular radar). Stored per world/server, not part of the config profile.
gui.xaero_wm_box_skip_world_render: Skip rendering the world in the background while the world map screen is open which significantly increases the framerate. However, when this is enabled, the framerate is also manually limited to around 625 to avoid issues that come from very high framerates (such as with video recording or streaming). Some mods might not be compatible with this feature and turning it off should fix any issues but with the drawback of (usually) worse framerates.
gui.xaero_wm_box_unlimited_zoom_in: Not actually unlimited but allows you to zoom in the fullscreen map way beyond the usual limit.
gui.xaero_wm_box_unlimited_zoom_out:
Experimental! 
 Not actually unlimited but allows you to zoom out the fullscreen map way beyond the usual limit. It is not properly optimized for regular gameplay and should only be used when you don't care about that.

help.securitycraft.secure_trading_statio: The secure trading station is used to trade items between players. Owners can configure the block to accept a certain amount of a maximum of 2 items as payment. If those items are submitted by a paying player, they are dispensed at the back side of the block, and a redstone signal will be emitted. If a storage module is inserted, the payment will instead be stored within the secure trading station, and owners can set a certain amount of a maximum of 2 items to be given as a reward to paying players, which are drawn from the block's inventory.

item.irons_spellbooks.archevoker_log.ent: We reached the location to which He bade us journey, a laborious march spanning many days. As the sun surrendered to dusk, we rested our wearied bodies upon the earth for what I trust to be the final time. This morn,
we rose with purpose anew, and began to etch a barrier of logs and home of stone.

Our construction draws nigh its completion. As I pen these very words, the final shipment of supplies flow into our haven - enough timber, freshly hewn from the surrounding wilds, to finish the enclosure, and panes of glass
sent from Fort Greater. Soon shall the research commence, the likes of which may yet shake the pillars of the world.

A strange unease takes root within my mind. This magic - though wondrous - doth twist the senses. I could have sworn there was a cellar beneath the chapel's floor, and yet now none recall it. Even my most trusted lieutenant
claims such a thing never was. Am I alone in this delusion? Has madness begun to gnaw at me?
Our scouts return with tidings of a village, not far from our encampment. This is good news, for supplies dwindle. We shall lay siege and easily procure what is needed, for the distance is not great.
However, the magical research in these lands proves troublesome - few are the answers we seek. It may soon come to pass that we abandon this place, move to the next site.

◆  Echo
Your weapon swings echo, dealing additional unmitigated damage after a short delay.
◆  Goat Stampede
Chance on hit to summon a stampede of goats that charge forward, knocking back and damaging anything in their path.

When landing a Leap Slam you have a chance to immediately leap again.

Chance to gain several stacks of Might when activating a signature ability.
◆  Necromantic Arsenal
Chance on hit to summon a skeletal minion that fights with a copy of your weapon.
◆  Nullification

Chance to gain several stacks of Precision when activating a signature ability.
◆  Radiance
When hitting a target afflicted with weakness, gain Immolation for a short duration.
◆  Renewed
When activating a signature ability, you have a chance to significantly reduce its cooldown.
◆  Soulshock
While held, this weapon grants you increased Soul & Lightning spell power.
◆  Spellforged
While in your mainhand, this weapon grants you increased spell power.

Chance on spell cast to gain Barrier.
◆  Spell Standard
Chance on spell hit to drop a Spell Standard that grants Precision & Spellforged.
◆  Stealthy
Chance to gain Stealth when activating a signature ability.
◆  Verdant Trail
Leave a trail of flowers that regenerate allies and harm enemies.
◆  War Standard
When using a forward charge ability, drop a War Standard that grants Might and reveals nearby enemies.
◆  Wing Buffet
Chance on hit to summon dragon wings that send forward a gust of wind, damaging and knocking back enemies in front of you.
◆  Wolf Pack
Chance on hit to summon a wolf minion that fights with a copy of your weapon.

kaleidoscope_cookery.ponder.millstone.te: Right-click with items in hand to insert them into the millstone.
Items dropped on the millstone from above will also be automatically inserted.
Certain creatures can be placed near the millstone to be harnessed.
After which, the millstone will start processing the items.
After one full rotation, the items are transformed into products and ejected from the opening.
kaleidoscope_cookery.ponder.pot.text_1: To cook with the wok, place it on a valid heat source.
kaleidoscope_cookery.ponder.pot.text_2: First, add some oil to the wok.
kaleidoscope_cookery.ponder.pot.text_4: After adding all of the required ingredients, use the kitchen shovel to start stir-frying!
kaleidoscope_cookery.ponder.pot.text_5: Then, after enough stirs and waiting for a moment...
When there are ingredients inside a wok or stockpot, right click with a blank recipe to record its contents.
At a later time, right click the wok or stockpot with the recipe again. This will add all of the recorded ingredients on the recipe using items from your inventory.
kaleidoscope_cookery.ponder.shawarma_spi: Ingredients can be placed into both the upper and lower layers of the shawarma spit.
Each layer can hold up to 8 smeltable food items of the same type.
Provide a redstone signal to activate the spit and start cooking.
Then, wait for a period of time...
However, it burns if the food is removed with bare hands from an activated shawarma spit.
A safer method is to use a kitchen knife to remove the food...
...or to deactivate the shawarma spit before attempting to remove the food.
kaleidoscope_cookery.ponder.steamer.head: Placing Steamers
kaleidoscope_cookery.ponder.steamer.text: To cook with steamers, place it on a valid heat source.
Then, place more steamers on top of existing ones to stack them higher...
However, a single heat source can only provide heat for up to 8 steamers...
kaleidoscope_cookery.ponder.steamer_1.te: From the top, insert ingredients into the steamer.
Steamers already containing ingredients can also be directly stacked.
After placing them, right click to cover the steamer and start steaming.
Then, wait for a period of time...
When the cooking is done, remove the steamer lid.
Finally, remove the steamers with the finished products layer by layer.
kaleidoscope_cookery.ponder.stockpot.tex: To cook with the stockpot, place it on a valid heat source.
First, add a soup base to the stockpot.
After adding all of the required ingredients, cover the stockpot with a stockpot lid.

modernfix.option.category.bugfixes.descr: Core bugfixes to improve game stability
modernfix.option.category.expert_only.de: Do not change unless you know what you are doing
modernfix.option.category.performance.de: Features that help improve game/launch performance
modernfix.option.category.troubleshootin: Features intended to assist in diagnosing problems
modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.blueprint_: Fixes Blueprint's ObjectModificationManager leaking vanilla resources, reducing memory usage. Despite the fix being contributed in PR #195 a release was not yet made.
modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.buffer_bui: Attempts to work around mods constructing BufferBuilder objects that leak memory. This can cause the JVM to crash with an hs_err_pid file in some rare cases. If you experience this type of crash, try disabling this option.
modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.chunk_dead: Attempts to prevent chunk system deadlocks or provide additional debug information in the log when they occur. These deadlocks usually manifest as the server freezing indefinitely (e.g. entities not moving), while the client continues to work just fine.
Patches Valhesia Structures to fix an issue in its code that causes frequent worldgen/chunkloading deadlocks.
modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.cofh_core_: Fixes a multithreading issue in CoFH Core that can cause rare crashes during launch.
modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.concurrenc: The patches in this group fix concurrency-related issues within Minecraft and/or Forge. Most of them result in rare, hard-to-diagnose crashes during loading.
modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.ctm_resour: Fixes a multithreading issue in ConnectedTexturesMod that can cause rare crashes during launch.
modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.edge_chunk: This option is a port of SuperCoder's Chunk Saving Fix mod (because I didn't realize it was already available for Forge at the time).
modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.ender_drag: Fixes a memory leak in vanilla caused by the ender dragon retaining a reference to the previous client world.
modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.entity_loa: Fixes many issues where EntityJoinWorldEvent/EntityJoinLevelEvent cause a worldgen deadlock, by slightly deferring entity loading. Should not, however, cause any noticeable behavior changes in-game.
modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.entity_pos: Fixes Forge issue #9118, where mods can cause undebuggable render crashes by pushing the matrix stack without popping it.
modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.extra_expe: Fixes the experimental feature warning being shown still being shown the first time you reopen a world that was created as experimental.
modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.file_dialo: Fixes a security issue with the worldgen settings file dialog
modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.fix_config: Fixes Forge configs occasionally becoming corrupted when launching the game.
modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.forge_at_i: Fixes a major oversight in Forge's early error handling code that causes some parts of mods to load, but not others, which usually results in the game crashing rather than displaying the intended error screen. This issue was fixed in NeoForge, and eventually fixed in new enough versions of Forge.
modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.forge_vehi: Fixes a bug introduced by a Forge patch that causes excessive amounts of chunk data packets to be sent to the player if they are riding a vehicle on a chunk border.
modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.mantle_mod: Fixes a bug in Mantle that can cause random ConcurrentModificationException crashes when rendering Tinkers Construct content.
modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.mc218112: This option fixes a deadlock that can occur if an exception is thrown while processing entity data. Vanilla does not correctly unlock the data manager when it should. This is tracked as MC-218112 on the bug tracker, and was fixed by Mojang in 1.17.
modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.missing_bl: Hypixel sends chunks to the client that are missing some block entity data, which makes chests etc. appear invisible. This 'fixes' the problem by creating the needed data on the client. Has no effect for properly behaved servers or in singleplayer.
modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.model_data: Works around design flaws in the Forge ModelDataManager system that can cause unexpected concurrency issues.
modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.packet_lea: **Experimental**, not enabled by default. An attempted fix for the memory leak issue that occurs after playing long enough on 1.16.
modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.paper_chun: 1.18 and newer. **A key optimization.** Ports a patch from Paper that fixes issues on 1.17 with chunkloading requiring huge amounts of memory and generating many `CompletableFuture` instances. 1.18+ are now able to load worlds on only 400MB of memory like 1.16 could.
modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.preserve_e: Makes the game window retain its existing size when control is handed over from Forge's early loading to Minecraft code. Fixes the window teleporting back to the center of the screen after being dragged, etc.
modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.recipe_boo: Fixes Forge clients being disconnected when connecting to a vanilla server if mods add custom recipe book entry types.
modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.refinedsto: Fixes Refined Storage external storage blocks occasionally failing to show contents of drawers, etc. when loaded. Backport of Refined Storage PR #3435, which was only applied to 1.18 and later.
modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.remove_blo: Fixes zombie pigmen keeping the 0, 0 chunk loaded perpetually on Forge. Backport of Forge PR #8583.
modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.removed_di: Fixes the game failing to load worlds if dimension mods are removed. Backport of Forge PR #8959.
modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.restore_ol: Fixes MC-272431, which tracks the ender dragon being unable to dive to the portal as it did in 1.13 and older. This causes the dragon to fly quite a bit differently from what modern players are used to and also patches out one-cycling, so it's not enabled by default. Thanks to Jukitsu for identifying the regression in the vanilla code.
modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.starlight_: Fixes an occasional Starlight crash due to emptiness maps not being initialized. Backport of the same fix in Starlight for 1.18.x.
modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.tf_cme_on_: Patches Twilight Forest to perform non-thread-safe client setup using the main thread as it should, rather than the FML worker thread.
modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.unsafe_mod: Fixes various ConcurrentModificationExceptions that can occur in content mods when computing block shapes
modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.world_leak: Reduces the memory usage of old client-side worlds that aren't needed after switching dimensions. These are normally garbage collected in vanilla, but mods sometimes retain references to them.
modernfix.option.mixin.bugfix.world_scre: Fixes MC-251068, where deleting the last world takes you back to an empty world list.
modernfix.option.mixin.core: Core patches required for ModernFix to work
modernfix.option.mixin.devenv: Patches used when running in a development environment, for speed improvement and/or testing
modernfix.option.mixin.feature.blockenti: **This is a debug option and should not be enabled for regular gameplay.** Attempts to detect mods interacting with block entities on the wrong thread and crash the game with more information, rather than an unclear ConcurrentModificationException
modernfix.option.mixin.feature.branding: Adds ModernFix to the branding list on the title screen, and also to the F3 screen.
modernfix.option.mixin.feature.cause_lag: Disables the game's use of worker threads for the server and for chunk rendering. **This will make performance worse on almost all hardware**, and should only be enabled on a client, when you know exactly what you are doing, and probably only on hardware with very few (2 or less) physical CPU cores. In those rare cases, it can reduce lag spikes since there is less contention over the limited cores.
modernfix.option.mixin.feature.direct_st: Normally off, can be enabled to force the raw stack trace to be dumped to the log when a crash occurs. Occasionally vanilla's crash report system fails to work properly and gives an entirely irrelevant stack trace/report.
modernfix.option.mixin.feature.integrate: Adds the vanilla watchdog to singleplayer worlds as well, but just prints out the stacktraces rather than forcefully terminating the world. This version includes the functionality of Fullstack Watchdog, but the latter is still needed for multiplayer.
modernfix.option.mixin.feature.measure_t: Uses a couple injections to measure world load time, datapack reload time, resource reload time, bootstrap time, and adds the necessary hooks to enable vanilla's unused profiler logic for resource reloading if so configured.
modernfix.option.mixin.feature.registry_: Runs the Forge loading screen on a background thread for part of the loading process, to allow progress to be shown while content is being registered. May have compatibility issues with some GPU drivers (e.g. macOS), so do not enable it by default in a modpack.
modernfix.option.mixin.feature.remove_ch: Prevents the Minecraft client from obtaining the keypair for chat signing. This disables the client's ability to sign chat messages (like No Chat Reports, but in a simpler, albeit less user-friendly way).
modernfix.option.mixin.feature.remove_te: Prevents the Minecraft client from sending telemetry to Mojang. The telemetry is generally not relevant to them anyway for a modded instance.
modernfix.option.mixin.feature.snapshot_: Adds easter egg features (does not affect any vanilla visuals or behavior) when running on a snapshot version.
modernfix.option.mixin.feature.spam_thre: **To be used for debugging purposes only.** Causes a thread dump to be output to the log every 60 seconds. This can help to diagnose unexplained freezes during loading/gameplay.
modernfix.option.mixin.feature.spark_pro: If enabled, and a compatible version of Spark is installed, the entire launch sequence will be profiled until the main menu.
modernfix.option.mixin.feature.stalled_c: This option may help to detect the cause of chunkloading freezes. However, leaving it enabled may cause slightly worse performance.
modernfix.option.mixin.feature.suppress_: Prevents the game from logging a very long stacktrace when the narrator fails to load on Linux (usually caused by not having libflite installed).
modernfix.option.mixin.feature.warn_miss: Shows a warning on startup if other performance mods considered essential and highly compatible are not present
modernfix.option.mixin.launch.class_sear: Replaces Forge's resource finder (used to find game and a mod code) with a significantly faster version, speeding up launch
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.async_jei: 1.16 only. **A key optimization.** Patches JEI to perform its reloading on a background thread, completely eliminating the long delay it adds to world loading.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.async_locato: 1.16 only. Backports the Async Locator mod's patches to eliminate server freezes associated with `/locate`, loot table generation, etc.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.biome_zoomer: 1.16 only. Minor optimization to improve the performance of the biome zoomer using logic from 1.18.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.blast_search: All versions. If REI or JEI are installed, construction of the vanilla search trees for creative searching is disabled, and searching is instead done using these mods' search implementations. This saves several seconds during world loading, and probably also saves some RAM as well (although I have not measured).
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.boost_worker: 1.16 only. Removes the hardcoded cap on worker thread count, similarly to what Mojang did in 1.18.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.cache_blocks: All versions. Avoids creating fresh copies of enum arrays each time a blockstate cache is initialized. Minor optimization, but easy to do.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.cache_model_: All versions. Memoizes the `RenderMaterial` (texture) collection and dependency list that models return instead of requiring them to be recalculated on each request. Helps accelerate the model load/bake process.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.cache_profil: Avoids pointlessly creating a URL object and speeds up skull block rendering.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.cache_strong: All versions. Saves the generated list of stronghold positions with the world, instead of regenerating it on every world load. Saves a little bit of time on 1.16, and quite a bit more on 1.18 and 1.19.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.cache_upgrad: All versions. Many mods ship outdated structure files, which requires the game to upgrade them using DFU every single time they are loaded. This can be quite slow. This patch adds logic to instead save the upgraded version of the structure, and reuse it on the next load. To handle the case that the mod changes a structure file but not the name, the original file's hash is compared against the cached version, and if they do not match the structure will be upgraded again.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.chunk_meshin: Implements some minor optimizations to the vanilla chunk meshing logic (they will have no effect with a mod that replaces chunk rendering entirely).
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.clear_fabric: Reduces memory usage by clearing mapping data structures in Fabric Loader that are either redundant or rarely used by mods. Off by default for compatibility reasons.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.clear_mixin_: Force-loads all mixins when launch finishes and then clears out mixin data structures to remove most of Mixin's memory footprint. Disabled by default for compatibility reasons.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.compact_bit_: Fixes memory waste caused by some legacy servers (e.g. Hypixel) sending empty chunks as if they contain blocks. Reduces memory usage significantly on these servers.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.compact_moja: (Fabric) Experimental option that reduces the memory usage of registries by roughly 50%. Not useful in most modpacks unless they contain millions of blocks and items.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.compress_bio: 1.16 only. Minor optimization borrowed from Hydrogen, which attempts to save space in the biome container when possible. This gets disabled automatically if conflicting mods like BetterEnd or Chocolate are installed.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.compress_uni: Stores the glyphs for the Unicode font more efficiently. Kudos to @AnAwesomGuy for the trick.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.datapack_rel: All versions. Reduces log spam and possibly slightly improves loading speed by not printing the stacktraces for some commonly thrown exceptions during datapack reload (e.g. missing items in loot tables/recipes). The message is still printed.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.dedicated_re: All versions. Moves resource pack and data pack reloading to a dedicated worker pool instead of using the default `Worker-Main` threads. This allows mods to Smooth Boot to still potentially improve singleplayer performance at runtime while not slowing down launch due to a limited thread count.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.deduplicate_: Deduplicates climate parameter objects used by the new biome system, can save ~2MB but also slows down datapack reload somewhat.

All versions, but disabled by default due to load time impact. Deduplicates resource location namespaces and paths. This saves RAM but also increases the cost of constructing a new `ResourceLocation` by quite a bit.
Makes most wall blocks share the same shape object instead of each one having its own copy. Can reduce memory usage substantially when lots of wall blocks are added by mods.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.dynamic_bloc: Avoids storing a codec for every block(state) and instead generates and caches it on the fly when needed. Generally not worth enabling unless you have a million blocks/items.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.dynamic_dfu:
All versions. Modifies DFU initialization to happen the first time something needs to be upgraded. This sounds similar to LazyDFU but is distinctly implemented, as it avoids loading *any* DFU classes/data structures, while LazyDFU only disables rule optimization. Essentially, this option is a safer version of DataFixerSlayer as it will still load DFU when needed.

You should typically continue to use LazyDFU even with this option enabled, as otherwise DFU rule optimization will cause lag.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.dynamic_enti: Constructs entity models the first time they are seen instead of during launch. Some mods are not compatible with this option and will cause EntityRenderer crashes.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.dynamic_reso: AE2 compatibility patch for dynamic resources
CTM compatibility patch for dynamic resources
Diagonal Fences compatibility patch for dynamic resources
LDLib compatibility patch for dynamic resources
Refined Storage compatibility patch for dynamic resources
SuperMartijn642CoreLib compatibility patch for dynamic resources
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.dynamic_soun: All versions. Allows the game to unload sounds, instead of sounds indefinitely persisting after being loaded.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.dynamic_stru: All versions. Allows the game to unload structure files after generation concludes instead of keeping them loaded forever.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.fast_forge_d: Speeds up Forge registry freezing during launch by using a faster code path
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.fast_registr: All versions. Forge needlessly looks up a method via reflection every single time a registry is validated. This patch simply caches the returned value since it will be the same every time.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.faster_advan: Rewrites the advancement checking logic to be faster and not cause StackOverflowError in large packs. Port of Advancements Debug from Fabric.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.faster_comma: Mitigate lag when there are hundreds of thousands of suggestions while typing a command
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.faster_font_: All versions. Optimizes the font renderer to load fonts faster, speeding up resource reload.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.faster_item_:
All versions. Avoids rendering the sides of items in GUIs. (Yes, vanilla appears to do that.)

This can triple FPS with a mod like REI/JEI installed on weaker GPUs, if enough items are visible. Disabled by default since it's new and not tested much, but should be safe. The most likely issue is items being completely invisible in GUIs, or appearing flat in the world.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.faster_struc: Improves the speed at which structures like buried treasure can be located.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.faster_textu: All versions pre 1.19.4. Avoids reading textures twice (the first time using a very slow code path) and instead does one faster load (similar to 1.19.3+).

All versions. Enables the game to use a faster texture stitching system originally written by SuperCoder79 for lwjgl3ify on 1.7.10, which can save some time during loading. Rarely, it's been reported to cause weird artifacts on blocks or in GUIs, this may be a Sodium bug.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.fix_loop_spi: Fixes Minecraft's built-in wait function consuming excessive amounts of CPU resources.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.forge_cap_re: Small micro-optimization that makes retrieving custom entity data slightly more efficient on Forge.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.forge_regist: Fixes more oversights in Forge that lead to excessive allocation in hot registry methods.
Fixes oversights in Forge that lead to excessive allocation in hot registry methods.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.jeresources_: 1.16 only. Optimizes Just Enough Resources to not needlessly recreate villager entities many times for the same profession, which saves time during JEI startup.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.kubejs: 1.16 only. Optimizations to KubeJS to avoid needless `ItemStack` copying, etc., which reduces the time taken to load datapacks.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.memoize_crea: Improves on vanilla's existing caching for creative tab contents in a way that is compatible with the timing requirements of mods like JEI/EMI. This can reduce the lag spike when opening the creative inventory for the first time in a modpack.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.model_optimi: All versions. Implements optimizations to speed up the model loading process.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.mojang_regis: Fixes an issue causing registration of blocks/items to slow down proportional to the number already registered. This improves startup time.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.nbt_memory_u: All versions. Uses a more efficient backing map for compound NBT tags that deduplicates key names and also uses an array map for very small compounds. This reduces the overhead of storing many compound tags in memory.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.nuke_empty_c: 1.16 only, inspired by Hydrogen. Avoids storing chunk sections that are full of air in memory, instead marking them as empty.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.patchouli_de: Fix Patchouli books storing many empty items with NBT tags, reducing memory usage.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.potential_sp: Optimizes the Forge event for finding potential mobs that can spawn. This reduces allocations and the overhead of rebuilding a weighted list when no mods modify the potential spawns.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.reduce_block:
All versions. **A key optimization.** Newer Minecraft versions (after 1.12) implemented a blockstate cache system that caches frequently used information about a blockstate, such as whether it is solid, its collision shape, etc. Rebuilding this cache is quite fast in vanilla (it takes only a second or two) but is quite slow with many mods installed, as there are many more blockstates present in the game which all must have their caches rebuilt.

This problem is exacerbated by Forge as the cache is rebuilt at many points when the data would almost certainly be unused before the next rebuild. Examples include right before reaching the main menu (during the "Freezing data" stage), as well as multiple (!) times when a world is being loaded.

ModernFix solves this performance bottleneck by instead making cache rebuilds lazy. Each blockstate rebuilds its cache the first time the data would be accessed. At any point when vanilla or Forge would attempt to rebuild caches for all blockstates, this is redirected to simply invalidate the cache on each blockstate instead.

This should not have any impact on TPS after startup concludes.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.remove_biome: All versions. Removes the biome temperature cache as Lithium does on modern versions.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.remove_spawn: Completely removes spawn chunks from the game. They are no longer loaded at all, unlike Ksyxis.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.resourcepack:
All versions. **A key optimization.** Launches on modern versions are heavily bottlenecked by filesystem access. Many requests are frequently made to resource packs to list resources or check if a given resource exists, and each of these result in a very slow file API call.

ModernFix completely eliminates most of the bottleneck here by simply caching a listing of all resources that exist within mod-provided and vanilla resourcepacks. The cache is rebuilt on resource reload (except for the vanilla resources, since they should never change while the game is running).

There are no known compatibility issues with this patch except for OptiFine (its CTM resources do not load correctly). However I do not recommend using OptiFine in any scenario, as it adds several minutes to launch time by itself and is not tested with ModernFix at all.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.reuse_datapa: 1.16 only. Attempts to speed up switching between singleplayer worlds by skipping the datapack reload when possible. May cause compatibility issues with some mods, but is currently enabled by default.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.rewrite_regi: All versions. **Currently semi-broken.** Aggressively replaces some internals of the Forge registry system with faster versions, however it currently causes freezes when loading some modpacks. Off by default for obvious reasons.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.skip_first_d:
1.16 & 1.19 only. **A key optimization.**

In the middle of the 1.16 development cycle, Forge patched the game to reload datapacks twice when loading an existing world, in order to fix an issue with biome ID shifting. Unfortunately, datapack reloads often take upwards of 30 seconds and so this very severely affects world loading times.

ModernFix makes the necessary changes to avoid this reload, based on the unfinished Forge PR #8163.

This change was removed by Forge in 1.18, but then a similar patch was added *again* in 1.19 to fix mod datapacks not being loaded when creating new singleplayer worlds. Fortunately, the issue is localized to the world creation screen in 1.19, and existing worlds only require a single reload. However, this still doubles the length of the lag spike when clicking "Create New World" in 1.19, and so ModernFix again makes changes to not perform a redundant reload.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.state_defini: All versions. Enabled only if FerriteCore is installed. Takes advantage of FerriteCore's handling of blockstates to speed up their creation. This can help speed up launch with mods that add lots of blockstates, such as furniture mods.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.sync_executo: All versions. Avoids having the main thread spin idly consuming one CPU core while waiting for the modloading workers to finish.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.tag_id_cachi: Speeds up uses of tag entries by caching the location object instead of recreating it every time
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.thread_prior: All versions. Adjusts the worker and server thread priorities to be lower than the client thread. This helps improve FPS stability on machines with few CPU cores, provided that the Java implementation in use respects priorities.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.ticking_chun: Optimizes chunk ticking in vanilla to reduce allocations.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.twilightfore: Fixes lag caused by Twilight Forest worldgen checking structures very inefficiently
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.use_integrat: Mostly for 1.16. Patches JEResources to use the integrated server's loot table data if playing singleplayer, rather than pointlessly reloading loot tables. Saves a couple more seconds during JEI startup.
modernfix.option.mixin.perf.worldgen_all: Optimizes some world generation logic in vanilla to reduce object allocations.
modernfix.option.mixin.safety: Concurrency patches to prevent crashes during launch
modernfix.perf_mod_warning: ModernFix mod warnings can be disabled by turning off mixin.feature.warn_missing_perf_mods in the ModernFix config.
modernfix.redirector_installed: ModernFix detected that Redirector is installed. Redirector is known to cause many strange and hard-to-debug issues, and removing it is strongly recommended.

module.securitycraft.secure_trading_stat: Adding a denylist module to a secure trading station will ban listed players from interacting with the block.
Adding a smart module to a secure trading station will make the station check for enchantments and other metadata when comparing whether the supplied payment equals the payment reference stacks.

Adding a storage module to a secure trading station will allow the block to store received payment items in its inventory. Additionally, the station will be able to give reward items to paying players, which are drawn from the block's inventory.
Adding an allowlist module to a secure trading station will allow listed players to submit transactions without needing to supply payment items.
module.securitycraft.username_logger.sma: Adding a smart module to a Username Logger will prevent the block from creating multiple entries for the same player by updating existing entries instead.
monsterology.monsterexpansion.ignathos.f: Ignathos' base attacks can be easily evaded using dodge rolls. As the fight progresses, Ignathos will search for and consume any valid fuel blocks nearby. Upon eating the fuel, it enters an ignited state, unlocking new flame-based abilities and empowering its standard moves. While ignited, both its beak strikes and its newly acquired flame-spitting attacks deal Fire damage and have a chance to inflict the Flarevein effect. The primary danger here is Flarevein, which will ramp up in severity if not addressed quickly. To cure the affliction, simply sprint or perform dodge rolls until it dissipates. When enraged, Ignathos gains the ability to spew a massive glob of flaming goo. Although this attack boasts increased damage and a wider area of effect, the beast suffers from a short recovery period afterward, providing an excellent opening for a counterattack.
monsterology.monsterexpansion.ignathos.l:
Often referred to by frustrated locals as the "Brushfire Vandal," Ignathos is a medium-sized, flightless Avian covered in dense, heat-resistant plumage. Unlike most predators, this highly specialized creature is an obligate consumer of combustibles, sustaining itself entirely on a diet of raw wood, coal, and other flammable materials. Its anatomy is perfectly adapted for this bizarre ecological niche; it possesses unusually long arms ending in inward-pointing, vice-like claws that allow it to effortlessly grip, uproot, and pull solid blocks of fuel directly from the earth or human structures.

Once consumed, the materials enter a highly specialized stomach that acts as a biological furnace. Ignathos does not digest its food in a traditional sense; instead, it literally burns it, absorbing the resulting thermal and kinetic energy to fuel its own body. Because of its voracious appetite for fuel, particularly during the harsh winter months, unprepared villages often fall victim to its pillaging. However, Ignathos is naturally docile and strongly prefers to flee from confrontation. Over time, settlements situated near birch forests and other natural habitats have learned to coexist with the beast, leaving designated piles of scrap wood and coal on the outskirts of town to prevent the creature from dismantling their houses or raiding freshly mined stockpiles.

Despite its somewhat dopey appearance and timid nature, Ignathos is not defenseless. If it detects genuine hostility and feels it cannot safely escape (or if it is fiercely protecting a particularly rich meal) it will fight back. By hyper-ventilating and forcefully expelling the burning contents of its stomach furnace, Ignathos can spew globs of highly adhesive, flaming goo over a wide area.

While Ignathos is considered physically weaker than most large monsters, seasoned hunters actively avoid confronting them whenever possible. This is not out of fear of the beast itself, but rather the catastrophic environmental damage it causes when panicked. A frightened or cornered Ignathos will spray its flaming goo wildly, easily igniting massive, uncontrollable forest fires that can devastate an entire biome.
monsterology.monsterexpansion.leivekilth: Leivekilth's attacks are slow, but its sheer size makes up for the lack of speed. Shattering its ice armor quickly is crucial, as breaking each section increases the damage the monster takes. Watch out for its belly flop attacks; the safest way to evade these is to run diagonally underneath the beast. Be equally cautious of its ice attacks, which can inflict Frostvein. This effect is highly dangerous if allowed to stack, eventually preventing you from jumping over blocks altogether. Upon enraging, Leivekilth will flip onto its back and begin to hover. Do not waste your resources trying to outrun it. Instead, the safest approach is to remain at its sides. This positioning keeps you clear of the ice spikes erupting directly beneath it, while also preventing the monster from targeting you with its ice breath or tail sweeps.

A colossal, solitary Therian bearing the traits of a walrus, but equipped with membranous wings, a heavy tail, and devastating saber-like tusks. Its fangs serve as a visual marker of its age and dominance.

Leivekilth possesses highly specialized organs that secrete volatile fluids capable of rapidly stripping salt from seawater and shifting freezing points. This also allows the creature to exhale sweeping jets of pure frost. Its thick blubber is laced with a sponge-like tissue, enabling it to absorb water and cloak itself in a dense armor of regenerative ice.

Despite its immense weight, Leivekilth is terrifyingly agile in short bursts, the sheer muscle mass of the creature allows it to leap great distances and even take flight for brief periods. However when enraged, utilizing its blowholes to push freezing air at high speeds, it can temporarily transition into its flying state. This phase is extremely dangerous, as its bodily fluids can now rapidly drip below, flash freezing the ground at impact and creating razor sharp ice spikes. Or increasing the rate and pressure of its blowhole exhalations to supercool the ground below it, creating a massive icy shockwave.

Leivekilth are notoriously brutal with its prey, preserving them in ice and impaling them upon its jagged back spines. These macabre displays serve to store food, assert dominance, and attract mates. During breeding season, its lairs are decorated with mountainous heaps of frozen corpses, a grim warning that stepping foot into its territory is an absolute death sentence.
monsterology.monsterexpansion.rakoth.fig: Rakoth excels at mid-to-short range, so it is best to avoid lingering at these distances. Watch out for its tail attacks, which possess a wide area of effect and can be devastating if caught off guard. Rakoth inflicts more stun than any other monster; taking damage three times in quick succession will almost certainly leave you immobilized. Because the beast is typically very slow, most of its attacks can be easily dodged with proper positioning. After sustaining enough damage, Rakoth will occasionally curl into a ball and attempt to crush you. If you see it suddenly running in an unusual direction, it is preparing to initiate this rolling attack. Do not allow it to create distance, as this gives it the space needed to freely turn and home in on you. Instead, chase after it. If you stay close enough, its turning radius will be restricted, forcing it to helplessly circle around you instead of landing a direct hit.
monsterology.monsterexpansion.rakoth.lor:
A massive, four-legged Lacertian geovore characterized by the heavily armored, rocky shell covering its back. Rakoth primarily roams the arid expanses of badlands and deserts, relentlessly searching for exposed mineral veins and precious metals to sustain itself.

Equipped with a thick, reinforced skull and prominent frontal horns, this beast routinely headbutts solid cliff faces to excavate its metallic diet. While typically docile toward humans, its insatiable hunger for ore makes it extremely dangerous to fully equipped hunters. Rakoth is known to mistake the glint of metallic armor for a walking feast, charging relentlessly to crack open the hunter and consume the raw iron or gold within.

Despite its cumbersome, rocky exterior, hunters must not be deceived by its apparent sluggishness. Rakoths can launch into a terrifyingly swift gallop. If severely threatened, it will tuck its head and tail inward, transforming into a massive, rolling boulder of pure physical destruction. While this rolling charge delivers devastating blunt-force trauma capable of flattening anything in its path, the beast's vision and turning radius are severely compromised in this state, allowing nimble hunters to evade and counterattack.

Beyond its horns and rolling charge, Rakoth boasts a remarkably thick, armored tail used for crushing blows. During mating season, the arid plains echo with rhythmic, thunderous tremors as rival males repeatedly slam their heavy tails into the dirt. This display of raw physical power serves both as a call to potential mates and a violent warning to any competing males in the territory.
monsterology.monsterexpansion.rhyza.figh: Much like Ignathos, most of Rhyza's base attacks can be easily evaded using dodge rolls, though its overall attack speed is noticeably faster. When enraged, Rhyza gains access to two new abilities: Flash and Invisibility. Avoiding the Flash is simple; Rhyza will deliberately dash into your field of vision, so simply look away, preferably in the opposite direction of its dash, to avoid being blinded. Invisibility is a bit trickier, as there is no way to predict where Rhyza will emerge around you. Rather than trying to guess, it is better to rely on a reactive dodge roll. If you do not immediately see the beast, assume it is preparing to strike from behind and roll accordingly.
monsterology.monsterexpansion.rhyza.lore:
A highly elusive, carnivorous Chimeran native to the barren, floating islands of the End. Characterized by its twin tails and specialized forelimbs, the Rhyza is a deadly anomaly in an already alien landscape. Unlike other predators that rely on crushing jaws, this beast rarely utilizes its sharp teeth in combat. Instead, it wields elongated, jagged claws with terrifying precision, evolved specifically to slash and perforate. Even if a target manages to deflect the brunt of a physical strike, the deep, serrated lacerations left behind inflict severe and continuous bleeding.

Despite its lethal anatomy, the Rhyza is naturally cautious and actively avoids unnecessary confrontation. It navigates the desolate void using advanced evasion tactics, primarily shifting into complete invisibility, to stalk small prey or bypass threats. Ecologists have recently discovered that what appears to be pale, white fur is actually a dense coat of microscopic, incredibly complex mirror-like structures. These organic, yet-to-be-understood prisms perfectly bend light around the creature's body, rendering it entirely unseen in its environment.

If cornered, it reveals its secondary defense mechanism: the bulbous, gleam-infused cores at the ends of its twin tails. By smashing these cores together or against the ground, the Rhyza detonates a blinding, disorienting flash of light, allowing it to vanish. However, if the creature is provoked into a lethal encounter, these evasive tools are weaponized, allowing the beast to blind its target and strike from unseen angles with terrifying, omnidirectional leaps.

This timid nature completely inverts during mating season. Expectant female Rhyzas become hyper-aggressive, entirely abandoning their natural invisibility to ruthlessly hunt down anything that moves within their territory. Ecologists theorize this violent behavioral shift is a preemptive evolutionary imperative, a brutal campaign to purge the surrounding islands of any potential threats before giving birth, ensuring the absolute safety of its vulnerable offspring.
monsterology.monsterexpansion.skrythe.fi: When engaging a Skrythe, avoid lingering in mid-range, as this is where its attacks, particularly its roar, are most devastating. Fighting at close range prevents you from simply outrunning strikes, forcing you to rely on diagonal dodge rolls to evade. This dynamic completely shifts when the Skrythe becomes enraged. You must abandon close-quarters combat during this state, as it can unleash a Seismic Roar at any moment. This attack is instantly fatal at point-blank range and still inflicts massive damage further out, so your best strategy is to keep your distance and bait the attack. If you back away too far while the enraged beast is airborne, it will trigger an Aerial Assault. As it ascends to fire sound spheres, do not waste stamina dodging them, as they deal negligible damage. Instead, immediately sprint directly underneath the Skrythe. The true threat is its subsequent angled dive, which boasts an incredibly long forward reach. Positioning yourself directly below the monster is the most reliable way to evade the dive completely.
monsterology.monsterexpansion.skrythe.lo:
A highly territorial carnivorous Wyvern characterized by its dense, ash-grey scales and striking azure wing membranes. The Skrythe thrives in most regions and can be sighted throughout the world migrating or looking for food.

Rather than relying on a breath weapon, its throat houses a highly specialized organ capable of generating devastating, high-frequency vibrations. The prominent blue frills crowning Skrythe's head are not merely for display. They are highly complex biological parabolic reflectors. When the wyvern produces a sound, these frills flare outward to amplify, focus, and aim the vibrations, turning a deafening roar into a localized, kinetic shockwave capable of pulverizing solid rock and shattering the bones of its prey.

To counterbalance the force of its own sonic blasts, Skrythe has developed a heavily calcified, rigid tail. While it prefers to fight at a distance using acoustics, it will ruthlessly swing this hardened tail like a mace to crush anything that manages to get too close.

Skrythe was the very first apex predator officially documented by early explorers. Before humanity understood the true dangers of the world, a massive grey shadow blotted out the sun, accompanied by a deafening roar that shattered village windows. It was the creature that taught the world to look up and fear the skies. Which is why its titled 'First King of The Skies'
