pfg.gui.title: PFG — Frame Generation
pfg.gui.tooltip.adaptive: When the game cannot render fast enough, the effective multiplier is lowered temporarily to keep the base FPS stable (less added latency).
pfg.gui.tooltip.factor: Perceived frame rate multiplier. Higher factors need more GPU time and a render FPS well below your monitor refresh.
pfg.gui.tooltip.fpsCounter: Show a small FPS counter on screen while frame generation is active: the displayed (presented) rate — real fps × factor — plus the real render rate in parentheses.
pfg.gui.tooltip.spikeLag: Just-in-time frame scheduling: delays the capture until just before the display refresh, so every frame sees the freshest mouse and keyboard inputs. The same principle as NVIDIA Reflex — the CPU waits instead of building a render queue ahead of time. Reduces input latency noticeably during fast mouse movement.
pfg.gui.tooltip.spikeLagBoost: Keeps the GPU clock speeds consistently high between frames by submitting a tiny background workload after each burst. Prevents micro-stutters during sudden scene changes (combat, chunk loads, explosions). Like the NVIDIA Reflex 'On + Boost' setting. Slightly increases idle power draw.
pfg.gui.tooltip.toggle: Master switch for frame generation. While on, interpolated frames are presented between the real ones.
pfg.gui.tooltip.uncapped: Present frames as fast as they are drawn, without syncing to the display refresh: the game renders uncapped (no V-Sync, no frame cap) and the F3 counter shows the full presented rate (real fps × factor). Anti-latency and adaptive quality are disabled. For fast GPUs; on slower setups the frames bunch and the image can flicker.
pfg.gui.tooltip.vsync: Bypass the game's internal frame cap. Presents are always synced to the display refresh while frame generation is active (one interpolated frame per refresh — required for a stable image), so this only makes the render rate track the refresh budget exactly.

quark.jei.hint.abacus: Use this on a block and it'll count the distance between the block you're looking at and the one you clicked, up to 48 blocks.
quark.jei.hint.ambience_discs: Ambience Discs can be gotten when a Skeleton kills a Spider. Unlike Music Discs, these loop infinitely.
quark.jei.hint.ancient_fruit: Falls from Ashen Trees when they're chopped down. Gives you a small amount of XP when eaten.
quark.jei.hint.ancient_sapling: Can be sometimes sniffed by a Sniffer.
quark.jei.hint.ancient_tome: Can upgrade an item or book's enchantment by one level, up to one above the normal cap. Rarely found in dungeons or strongholds.
quark.jei.hint.backpack: Wear this to gain an additional three rows of inventory space.
quark.jei.hint.banner_layer_buff: Banners have been upgraded to have up to %s layers now.
quark.jei.hint.beacon_redirect_item: Can redirect Beacon beams. Check the Beacon item for info.
quark.jei.hint.beacon_redirection: The beacon beam can be redirected with %s by placing it in the beam's path. Note that the final one must always face towards the sky, and that the beam has a limited horizontal distance it can cover.
quark.jei.hint.blackstone_furnace: If the block under this furnace produces Soul Fire when lit, the furnace will too.
quark.jei.hint.blue_blossom_sapling: Can be found in cold biomes.
quark.jei.hint.bottled_cloud: Get this by using a Glass Bottle when at Cloud level. Can be right clicked onto the air to create a temporary block that other blocks can be placed on.
quark.jei.hint.chorus_weeds: Uncommon spawns in the barrens of the outer end. Will randomly teleport and reproduce over time or if forced via trampling, bone meal, or adjacent water. May also spawn Endermites when trampled.
quark.jei.hint.chute: Drops any items fed into it by a Hopper/Dropper into the world directly below.
quark.jei.hint.compass_end: Can work in the End, pointing towards the exit portal.
quark.jei.hint.compass_nerf: Must be crafted before it does anything to prevent funny recipe book cheese.
quark.jei.hint.compass_nether: Can work in the Nether, pointing towards the portal you came in from.
quark.jei.hint.corundum: Can be found underground in large clusters of two colors each. Will slowly grow upwards if placed deep underground. Can be waxed to prevent growth and particle emission.
quark.jei.hint.corundum_cluster_grow: Grows alongside the respective Corundum, either naturally spawned or when left to grow.
quark.jei.hint.corundum_cluster_redirect: Can redirect Beacon beams, check the Beacon item for info.
quark.jei.hint.crab_info: Crabs can be found in Beaches, and bred with Wheat, Chicken, or any type of Fish.
quark.jei.hint.crate: Can hold up to %s items, regardless of their stack size. Not that great for bulk storage, but fantastic for unstackables or a large variety of random items.
quark.jei.hint.crystal_lamp: These lamps will only change the color of a beacon beam when turned on.
quark.jei.hint.diamond_heart: Can be gotten by breaking a Stoneling's shell underground. Don't worry - the Stoneling is just fine. The body is just a shell around the heart! If you see a small creature holding an item, that's one! Sneak up to it so it doesn't notice you, or use a Glow Shroom to bait it. If you use the Heart on raw stone, the Stoneling will construct a new body out of it, and will be more comfortable with players after its ride in your inventory.
quark.jei.hint.doors_open_together: When creating a double door, they'll open/close together.
quark.jei.hint.dragon_scale: Drops from the Ender Dragon from any kills beyond the first.
quark.jei.hint.dusky_myalite: Can be found embedded in Spiral Spires around the outer end.
quark.jei.hint.ender_watcher: Emits a redstone signal based on how close to the center of the eye a player is looking.
quark.jei.hint.feeding_trough: Animals can eat any items put in this and breed from it. Sometimes they may eat in excess, will not breed if there's too many nearby, and will not produce XP.
quark.jei.hint.fence_gates_open_together: When another fence gate is placed above or below it, they'll open/close together.
quark.jei.hint.flamerang: Works like a Pickarang, but any items it picks up become immune to fire and lava damage while they travel.
quark.jei.hint.forgotten_hat: Drops from Forgotten, which can be found deep underground. Be wary of their powerful equipment and multiple combat styles.
quark.jei.hint.glass_item_frame: Hides the frame when an item is put inside to show only the item. Has custom behavior for Banners and Shields, and can sit flush with a Sign that's on the floor. Can also be right clicked through to open any inventory behind it.
quark.jei.hint.glow_lichen_growth: Found in the rare Glimmering Weald biome deep underground.
quark.jei.hint.glow_shroom: Found in the rare Glimmering Weald biome deep underground. Bone Meal can be used to create a large variant.
quark.jei.hint.glowing_glass_item_frame: Glowing version of a Glass Item Frame - has all the same properties.
quark.jei.hint.gold_button: Emits a very short, 2 redstone tick, pulse.
quark.jei.hint.gold_tool_fortune: Gold Tools come with a baked in Fortune %s or Looting effect. This does not stack with the Enchantment version of it, only the highest will apply.
quark.jei.hint.gold_tool_harvest_level: Gold Tools now have a harvest level of %s.
quark.jei.hint.golden_apple_crate: Can be used as a Beacon base.
quark.jei.hint.grate: Animals that aren't leashed will not walk on this, and items will fall through.
quark.jei.hint.gravisand: Only falls when given a redstone signal, taking adjacent ones along with it. If it can't fall, it'll float upwards. Emits a comparator signal of 15.
quark.jei.hint.hoe_harvesting: Hoes can now break a 3 wide area of vegetation at once. Higher tier hoes such as Diamond or Netherite can break 5.
quark.jei.hint.hollow_logs: Can be crawled into by sneaking while walking towards the hollow side, can also be climbed when you're inside.
quark.jei.hint.iron_button: Emits a very long, 5 second, pulse.
quark.jei.hint.iron_rod: Will break any blocks in front of it when pushed with a piston.
quark.jei.hint.item_frame_dyeing: Can be dyed the same way you'd dye leather armor.
quark.jei.hint.jasper: Can be found in big clusters in mesas and deserts.
quark.jei.hint.ladder_dropping: Can be right clicked onto another ladder to drop it down.
quark.jei.hint.ladder_freestanding: As long as there's a structurally sound one behind it, can stand without any blocks behind.
quark.jei.hint.ladder_sliding: Looking down while on a ladder will make you descend faster.
quark.jei.hint.ladder_sneak: Opening your inventory while on a ladder will automatically make you sneak.
quark.jei.hint.limestone: Can be found in big clusters in swamps and oceans.
quark.jei.hint.magnet: Can push and pull any blocks made of Copper or Iron when powered, depending on the side. If multiple magnets are moving the same block, the biggest force will win. A magnet's force on a block is the redstone signal it's given minus the distance to the block. Hoppers moved with a Magnet will drop one item in front for each block moved. If the item is a seed, it'll try to plant it instead. Stonecutters moved with a Magnet will try to break the block above them.
quark.jei.hint.matrix_enchanting: Enchanting now uses a new "Matrix Enchanting" system. Pieces can be generated with Lapis and XP and placed onto a grid. Two pieces of the same type can be merged to upgrade the piece's level. Additionally, the Enchanting Table can now hold onto your item and the Lapis in it, hurray!
quark.jei.hint.matrix_influencing: Candles may also be used to increase the odds of specific enchantments. If the candle has soul sand below it or below the bookshelf it's on, it will decrease those odds instead.
quark.jei.hint.minecraft.amethyst_block: Can be placed under a Note Block to make it emit the iconic Amethyst sound.
quark.jei.hint.minecraft.armor_stand: Now has arms, allowing for an item plus a shield to be held.
quark.jei.hint.minecraft.calcite: Additional large calcite clusters are added to mountains.
quark.jei.hint.minecraft.campfire: Will boost players flying with an Elytra above it further upwards.
quark.jei.hint.minecraft.chain: When connected to a block, if that block is moved by a piston, so will the Chain and anything else on the other end.
quark.jei.hint.minecraft.clock: Must be crafted before it does anything to prevent funny recipe book cheese.
quark.jei.hint.minecraft.emerald_block: Can be used to make Villagers follow you much like how animals follow food items.
quark.jei.hint.minecraft.lava_bucket: Right click an item in your inventory onto the Lava Bucket to destroy it forever! Shulker Boxes and items that are immune to fire such as Netherite can not be destroyed this way.
quark.jei.hint.minecraft.magma_cream: A Slime that dies to Magma will split into Magma Cubes instead. Note that tiny Magma Cubes do not drop Magma Cream.

I was clearing out a new tunnel in the badlands and found this round, heavy rock blocking the tracks. It was about the size of a minecart, so I gave it a good whack with my pickaxe to break it up. Big mistake. The 'rock' uncurled, roared, and headbutted my actual minecart off the rails! It's a Rakoth, but it's only half the size of the massive ones we usually see on the surface. Don't let the compact size fool you, it still hits like a runaway train. Go clear it out of our shaft so we can get back to work!
quest.monsterexpansion.a_burning_nuisanc: Listen here, rookie! I know we're supposed to leave out scrap wood to keep those dopey birds happy, but a particularly greedy Ignathos just broke into my yard and made off with a whole stack of my premium crafting coal! I can't forge any armor if my fuel keeps getting treated like an all-you-can-eat buffet. Head out to the woods and teach that overgrown turkey a lesson. Just... try not to panic it near the tree line, yeah? We don't need a forest fire today.
quest.monsterexpansion.a_flash_in_the_da: I know the End isn't exactly a peaceful garden, but normally those pests just turn invisible and run away when I come to harvest Chorus Fruit. Well, not this one. I barely took two steps before it dropped its camouflage, flashed me blind, and came at me swinging those awful claws. The ecologists at camp told me she must be nesting, which means no one is safe near her territory. I need you to go clear it out so I can get back to my research. And hey, bring some bandages, those scratches do NOT stop bleeding!
quest.monsterexpansion.bloody_waters.des: We thought it was just a rogue iceberg drifting into the shipping lanes. Then it turned and rammed our hull. It's a leviathan, Hunter, a colossal beast cloaked in thick frost, with tusks that sheared right through our reinforced bow. As we abandoned ship, the fog cleared enough for me to see its back. It had massive marine predators, sharks and whales, completely frozen and skewered along its spine like grim trophies. It blasted the water with a freezing wind, locking our ruined ship in the floe to mark its new territory. Hunt it down before it pushes any further south.
quest.monsterexpansion.forged_in_ice.des: I'm trying to design a new type of cooling forge, and I need intact Leivekilth materials to make it work. I know hunting a Leivekilth is a massive risk, but if you can isolate one and bring me its parts, I'll forge you a weapon that'll freeze the sea itself.
We finally struck a massive raw gold vein in the badlands ravine, but the noise of our pickaxes attracted a Rakoth. It started eating the ore straight out of the cavern walls! Get in there and crack its shell before it devours our entire payout. Feel free to keep any of the heavy carapace you break off of it, I hear it makes fantastic plating.
quest.monsterexpansion.resonance_and_rui: I thought I was tough enough to take on a Skrythe solo. I was wrong. It shattered my iron shield with one of those sonic blasts and nearly took my head off. I plan on getting my revenge eventually, but first, I need an upgrade. Go hunt one down and bring me back a few of its calcified tail-bones. I'm going to forge a new hammer out of the very thing that beat me.
quest.monsterexpansion.silence_the_skies: WHAT? YOU'LL HAVE TO SPEAK UP! MY EARS ARE STILL RINGING! I was hauling a premium shipment of glass panes through the crossing when this massive grey shadow dropped out of nowhere. It flared up these blue things on its head and just... screamed! The sheer force of the sound shattered my entire cargo into dust! When I tried to scare it off, it swung a tail the size of an anvil and smashed my cart to splinters. I don't care what the guild calls it, just go out there and shut that flying menace up so I can do my job in peace!
quest.monsterexpansion.stolen_embers.des: Winter is setting in early, and one of those fire-birds just raided our communal woodpile again. We need to restock our firewood, but more importantly, the local tanner says Ignathos plumage makes for incredible thermal insulation. Head into the woods, track it down, and bring back enough feathers to line our winter coats.
quest.monsterexpansion.sunscorched_vanda: We have a massive problem on the dry plains. An Ignathos was sighted in the Savanna. Between the scorching sun and the dry brush, its internal furnace has completely overheated. It is permanently ignited, hyper-aggressive, and turning the grass to ash with every step. If we don't put this bird down immediately, the entire biome is going to go up in smoke.
quest.monsterexpansion.the_badlands_bite: Ravines out here are dangerous, so I spent my life savings on a brand-new set of heavy Iron armor. Turns out, to a Rakoth, that just makes me look like a premium, canned meal! I was barely swinging my pickaxe before this massive, rocky lizard charged at me, trying to crack me open like a geode. I dropped my tools and ran, but the overgrown pebble curled up into a boulder and literally flattened my entire campsite. I can still hear it slamming its tail out there. Go deal with it!
quest.monsterexpansion.thermal_shock.des: An Ignathos has wandered far outside its natural habitat, tracking deep into the frozen shores. That kind of reckless, erratic behavior leads us to believe it is a Tempered specimen. There is a Leivekilth territory dangerously close to a nearby coastal settlement. If the Ignathos agitates the leviathan, the resulting rampage will cause great harm to the village. We cannot take any chances. Head to the coast and take them both out before the situation escalates.
quest.monsterexpansion.thermal_shock.obj: Slay a Leivekilth and Tempered Ignathos
quest.monsterexpansion.unseen_blade.desc: I've finally figured out how to weave that microscopic mirrored fur into a stealth cloak, but my workshop is completely out of materials. I need you to head into the Outer Islands and track down a Rhyza. They are going to be incredibly evasive. You'll have to keep a sharp eye out for their shimmering silhouettes and strike before they flashbang you and vanish.
quest.monsterexpansion.unseen_blade.name: Unseen Blade

saintsdragons.gui.draconic_codex.ecology: Cindervanes are not conquerors, nor guardians. They are carriers. Early trade routes, evacuation corridors, and messenger networks were built around known Cindervane migratory paths. Their eggs, scattered rather than hoarded, suggest deliberate dispersion, either by the dragons themselves or by civilizations that understood...

...their value as mobile lifelines rather than weapons. Cindervanes lack complex combat instincts not due to weakness, but specialization. They do not linger in battle. When threatened, they escalate vertically, ignite, and end the encounter in a single decisive descent. Survival over supremacy.
Favorite Food:
Drops:

Ignivoruses are primordial firebound titans whose presence reshapes environments through sheer thermal dominance. Unlike Raevyx, whose authority is enforced through restraint, Ignivoruses exert control by occupation. Where one settles, the land does not recover. Native primarily to the Nether, Ignivoruses are believed to have originated in extreme...

...volcanic ecosystems where constant exposure to magma and hellfire selected for organisms capable of converting ambient heat into sustained power. Their rare appearances in the Overworld are not migratory, but anomalous, often linked to ancient interdimensional traversal or forced displacement. Ignivoruses are not mindless engines of destruction. They are patient...
and acutely aware of hierarchy. Aggression is not constant, but once provoked, escalation is absolute. An Ignivorus does not retreat. It overwhelms.
Favorite Food:
Drops:

Nulljaws are quiet End drifters that spend almost their entire existence suspended in open air. They neither dive for dominance nor settle into territory in the way other dragons do. Instead, they linger, observe, and glide in loose groups through the void-touched barrens.

Raevyxians are ancient storm-bound apex predators whose dominance is expressed not through constant aggression, but through selective, overwhelming enforcement of territory. Emotionally aware and socially complex, they rely on inherited behaviors rather than instinct alone, making improper upbringing fatal. Their rarity is not due to weakness, but restraint.
Favorite Food:
Drops:
Drops
Favorite Food
Overview

Stegonauts' presence defines safe ground, forming mobile bastions around those they are bound to protect. Stegonauts exhibit strong social imprinting and defensive prioritization, willingly placing themselves between danger and allied entities without provocation. Historical accounts imply that early riders used Stegonauts as living shields during...

...dragon-mounted assaults, charging alongside faster aerial units while absorbing retaliatory force. This explains their compatibility with other mounts and their unique ability to protect allied pets and players mid-engagement.
Favorite Food:
Drops:

Varasuchuses are adaptive abyssal predators whose threat lies not in overwhelming force, but in delayed commitment. Commonly encountered in coastal and aquatic regions, Varasuchus initially present as quadrupedal, semi-terrestrial hunters exhibiting restrained aggression and minimal energy expenditure. Early observers frequently misidentified this behavior...

...as docility or passivity. This assumption is universally fatal as Varasuchuses possess a unique phase-shifting physiology, allowing them to reconfigure posture, musculature, and combat behavior in response to sustained threat. The transition from quadrupedal to bipedal stance marks a decisive escalation, not an emotional one.

Once upright, Varasuchus abandon environmental tolerance and engage with deliberate, methodical violence. Their presence near civilization is rarely accidental. Records indicate that settlements which mistook Varasuchus’ initial restraint for safety rarely survived long enough to document its second phase.
Favorite Food:
Drops:

Volitans dwell where land and water blur into one another. Where water stagnates long enough, where rot settles and refuses to leave, where fish float belly-up and the air carries a metallic sting… something begins to form beneath the surface. Not immediately. Not quickly. But inevitably. Unlike other dragons, Volitans do not chase prey across great distances...

They choose a territory… and become part of it. The water settles around them. The soil softens. The air itself carries a weight that lingers in the lungs. Intruders often mistake this for decay. It is not decay. It is pressure. Volitans do not rely on speed alone to dominate their domain. Instead, they reshape the battlefield. Toxic spines erupt not as...

...wild attacks, but as warnings… lines drawn in space. Their breath hangs in the air and clings to the ground, forcing movement, limiting escape. Despite their overwhelming presence, Volitans are not needlessly destructive. They do not scorch, nor do they ravage endlessly. Once intruders are driven out, the waters calm, the air clears, and the land returns to stillness.

The conversion of effects follows this logic:

Haste -> Fatigue.
Regeneration -> Wither.
Strength -> Weakness.
Speed -> Slowness.
Invisibility -> Glowing.
Resistance -> Confusion.
Saturation -> Hunger.
Fire resistance -> Poison.
Absorption -> Damage.

 (increased with sweeping edge lvl)
 Shield Charges can be stored for up to 90 and used in 2 ways:
  - With the Shield, by holding guard and casting a shield attack.
    You will convert all Shield charge into shield Overcharge,
    granting you damage resistance.
  - With the Sword, by holding guard and casting a sword attack.
    You will charge your sword and consume your
     shield charges slowly to perform a spin attack.

 While your shield is Overcharged, your shield attack will do
 increase damage after a sword attack based on the Overcharge amount.

 Getting damaged reduce your Shield Overcharge by 5.
 ( Sweeping edge on your Sword reduce this by 1 per level )
skill.wom.sakura_state.tooltip:
"Sharpest blade forged in absolute serenity"

 On cast, you'll perform a Sakura slash.
 Sakura slashes can be declined in 2 form
  - while sprinting,
  you will fastly pass through enemys in front of you, slashing them along the way.  - while sprinting, (cost 2 stack)
  you will fastly pass through enemys in front of you,
  slashing them along the way.
  - while standing or walking, (cost 1 stack)
  you'll fastly slash in front of you.
 Sakura slashes automaticaly sheath your blade afterward.

 You can stack a total of 12 sakura slashes and Sweeping edge
 on your blade will grant you extra stack depending
 on the amount of stack you have on the first cast.
([initial amont of stack] * 1/3 of the sweeping edge levels)

 After the innitial draw, you'll enter sakura state.
 If you don't draw a Sakura slash again within 4 seconds, you loose all your
 stacks and get out of sakura state.

 Slashing a target with a Dash attack or a Sakura slash,
 will stack Perpetual slashes on the target.
 (3 on dashes and sakura slash.
 6 on sakura dash slash
 this value is then multiply by 1/3 of the Sweeping edge lvl).
 If no action is performed for a set of time after landing perpetual slashes,
 All Perpetual slashes stacked on the target are triggered,
 slashing it in sequence for each stacks of Perpetual slashes
skill.wom.shadow_step.tooltip:
§oSink in the shadows.§r
Moving in the shadow will twist space to make you move faster than the light itself.

While executing this skill, player become immune from physical attacks.
skill.wom.shooting_style.tooltip:
When empty handed, holding sneak while attacking will do kicks.

 The combo contain 3 different kick.
skill.wom.shulker_cloak.tooltip:
Loose the ability to guard.

 Every 5 sec, You gain one level of shulker resistance. 

If you have at least 1 level of Shulker resistance, you will negate 60% of damage.

Getting damaged reduce the level by 1.
skill.wom.solar_arcano.tooltip:
"Witness the full force of a star"

 After each basic attack, a special icon will apear within a short period.
 Press the Skill button when you see it to perform a timed Solar attack.
 Solar attack cycle between ignites ( Polvora ) and explode ( Chispear ):

    Polvora : set the target in fire. if target is
    allready in fire, increase ignitions level by 1.
    (can only go up to 2)

    Chispear: if target is in fire, extinguish the fire and
    explode for a set of damage depending on the ignitions level.
    (3 => 6 => 9, +1 per sweeping edge lvl)

 Solar have a unique skill meter mechanique.
 Heat level, wich is showed by the percentage number on the skill,
 can change color (from red to white) depending on the Heating speed.
 Increase Heat level by increasing heating speed above
 the orange lvl by successfully performing Chispear.
 The heating speed increase depends on the target ignition level.

 Hold guard and press skill to perform Solar Brasero.
 Solar Brasero harvest heat level to perform incendiary spell:

    Obscuridad: Infuse your blade with soul fire,
    melting it into a new form.
    All attacks within this form trigger Chispear.
    Lock your heating speed to red.

    Crematorio: breath soul fire in front of you.
    Burns targets to ignitions level 3.
    Durations depends on the amount of time
    they stay in the flame.

    Infierno: Burn target around you in a spherical shape.
    The area of effect will keep growing until 10 sec.
    Every 2sec, target within the area are affected by polvora.
    (can increase ignition level to 3)
    During infierno, all the speed at wich heat level is affected is doubled.
skill.wom.soul_protection.tooltip:
Loose the ability to guard.

 Each second you summon a soul that give 1% damage negation.
Your own soul give you 20% damage negation.

 Getting damaged will remove 3 souls.
skill.wom.spider_techniques.tooltip:
Allow you to run on walls.

 Hold sprint and jump toward a wall to run on it.
 Release sprint to fall or release movement input to slide slowly.
 Sneak to reduce the slide fall even more.

 You can jump from a wall to another by adjusting horizontal view angle.
 The position you jump from will adjust the hight of the wall jump.
skill.wom.time_travel.tooltip:
Register your position and health on cast.
After 5sec you'll be teleported back to your previus position and half of all damage taken within this time is healed.

Cast again to teleport early or sneak to cancel.
skill.wom.true_berserk.tooltip:
"May the god fear you..."

Torment wrath makes the skill gauge unreadable.
skill.wom.unbreakable.tooltip:
Give you 3 charge of protection that grant you resistance and stun immunity uppon taking damage.
Lose a charge when taking damage.
skill.wom.vampirize.tooltip: You heal yourself by 20% of the damage you deal.
skill.wom.vengeful_parry.tooltip:
Put you in a guarding stance for 2sec.
You will hold your position during that time blocking all attack at no stamina cost.
After that you'll be able to send back all the damage in your next attack.
Refresh damage on recast.
1sec cooldown.

Available Weapon Types : %s

Loosing Stamina increase Health by half.

Sneak to transfer health into stamina at double rate.

Disable stamina auto recovery.

sodium.options.always_defer_chunk_update: If enabled, rendering will never wait for chunk updates to finish, even if they are important. This can greatly improve frame rates in some scenarios, but it may create significant visual lag in the world.
sodium.options.animate_only_visible_text: If enabled, only animated textures determined to be visible will be updated. This can provide a significant boost to frame rates on some hardware, especially with heavier resource packs. If you experience issues with some textures not being animated, try disabling this option.
sodium.options.attack_indicator.tooltip: Controls where the Attack Indicator is displayed on screen.
sodium.options.autosave_indicator.toolti: If enabled, an indicator will be shown when the game is saving the world to disk.
sodium.options.biome_blend.tooltip: Controls the range which biomes will be sampled for block colorization. Higher values greatly increase the amount of time it takes to build chunks for diminishing improvements in quality.
sodium.options.brightness.tooltip: Controls the brightness (gamma) of the game.
sodium.options.chunk_update_threads.name: Chunk Update Threads
sodium.options.chunk_update_threads.tool: Specifies the number of threads to use for chunk building. Using more threads can speed up chunk loading and update speed, but may negatively impact frame times.
sodium.options.clouds_quality.tooltip: Controls the presence of rendered clouds in the sky.
sodium.options.cpu_render_ahead_limit.to: Specifies the maximum number of frames the CPU can be waiting on the GPU to finish rendering. Very low or high values may create frame rate instability.
sodium.options.entity_distance.tooltip: Controls how far away entities can render from the player. Higher values increase the render distance at the expense of frame rates.
sodium.options.entity_shadows.tooltip: If enabled, basic shadows will be rendered beneath mobs and other entities.
sodium.options.fps_limit.tooltip: Limits the maximum number of frames per second. This can help reduce battery usage and general system load when multi-tasking. If VSync is enabled, this option will be ignored unless it is lower than your display's refresh rate.
sodium.options.fullscreen.tooltip: If enabled, the game will display in full-screen (if supported).
sodium.options.graphics_quality.tooltip: The default graphics quality controls some legacy options and is necessary for mod compatibility. If the options below are left to "Default", they will use this setting.
sodium.options.gui_scale.tooltip: Sets the maximum scale factor to be used for the user interface. If 'auto' is used, then the largest scale factor will always be used.
sodium.options.leaves_quality.name: Leaves
sodium.options.mipmap_levels.tooltip: Controls the number of mipmaps which will be used for block model textures. Higher values provide better rendering of blocks in the distance, but may adversely affect performance with many animated textures.
sodium.options.particle_quality.tooltip: Controls the maximum number of particles which can be present on screen at any one time.
sodium.options.simulation_distance.toolt: The simulation distance controls how far away terrain and entities will be loaded and ticked. Shorter distances can reduce the internal server's load and may improve frame rates.
sodium.options.smooth_lighting.tooltip: Controls whether blocks will be smoothly lit and shaded. This slightly increases the amount of time needed to re-build a chunk, but doesn't affect frame rates.
If enabled, translucent effects from surfaces such as stained glass and water will be applied correctly.
sodium.options.use_block_face_culling.to: If enabled, only the sides of blocks which are facing the camera will be submitted for rendering. This can eliminate a large number of block faces very early in the rendering process, saving memory bandwidth and time on the GPU. Some resource packs may have issues with this option, so try disabling it if you're seeing holes in blocks.
sodium.options.use_compact_vertex_format: If enabled, a more compact vertex format will be used for rendering chunks. This can reduce graphics memory usage and bandwidth requirements significantly, especially for integrated graphics cards, but can cause z-fighting with some resource packs due to how it reduces the precision of position and texture coordinate attributes. Disabling this has no effect if Oculus is installed.
sodium.options.use_entity_culling.name: Use Entity Culling
sodium.options.use_entity_culling.toolti: If enabled, entities determined not to be in any visible chunks will be skipped during rendering. This can help improve performance by avoiding the rendering of entities located underground or behind walls.
sodium.options.use_fog_occlusion.name: Use Fog Occlusion
sodium.options.use_fog_occlusion.tooltip: If enabled, chunks which are determined to be fully hidden by fog effects will not be rendered, helping to improve performance. The improvement can be more dramatic when fog effects are heavier (such as while underwater), but it may cause undesirable visual artifacts between the sky and fog in some scenarios.
sodium.options.use_no_error_context.name: Use No Error Context
sodium.options.use_no_error_context.tool: If enabled, the OpenGL context will be created with error checking disabled. This may slightly improve performance, but it also increases the risk that the game will crash instead of gracefully handling OpenGL errors. You should disable this option if you are experiencing sudden unexplained crashes.
sodium.options.use_persistent_mapping.to:
If enabled, a small amount of memory will be persistently mapped as a staging buffer for chunk uploading, helping to reduce CPU overhead and frame time instability when loading or updating chunks.

Requires OpenGL 4.4 or ARB_buffer_storage.
sodium.options.v_sync.tooltip: If enabled, the game's frame rate will be synchronized to the monitor's refresh rate, making for a generally smoother experience at the expense of overall input latency. This setting might reduce performance if your system is too slow.
sodium.options.view_bobbing.tooltip: If enabled, the player's view will sway and bob when moving around. Players who experience motion sickness while playing can benefit from disabling this.
sodium.options.view_distance.tooltip: The render distance controls how far away terrain will be rendered. Shorter distances mean that less terrain will be rendered, improving frame rates.
sodium.options.vignette.name: Vignette
sodium.options.vignette.tooltip: If enabled, a vignette effect will be rendered on the player's view. This is very unlikely to make a difference to frame rates unless you are fill-rate limited.
sodium.options.weather_quality.tooltip: Controls the quality of rain and snow effects.

spell.apextides.parting_sea.guide: A path seventy blocks long opens down your aim, and on either side of it the sea comes up out of the ground: two walls of water sixty blocks high, rising one stretch after another away from you. Whatever stood where a wall rose is thrown into the path. For four and a half seconds the sea stands parted -- light coming through the walls ripples across the floor of the path, water runs down their faces, spray blows off their crests -- and anything that tries to leave through a wall is thrown back out of it, choking, while you and your allies swim through them freely. Then both walls lean in and fall, and the sea closes over the path.
